“the most High ruleth in the kingdom of men, and giveth it to whomsoever he will, and setteth up over it the basest of men.” It does not matter who you vote for; he puts whoever he wants. Donald Trump is one of the basest of men, a caricature and TV personality from The Apprentice, just as Ronald Reagan was an actor. His orange skin is telling you what he is about: he is Esau, the red man. The Most High puts these men over us so we can see: you wanted the other nations to rule over you besides me, and this is what happens.

Deuteronomy 17:14 shows that desire in our people: “When thou art come unto the land which the Lord thy God giveth thee, and shalt possess it, and shalt dwell therein, and shalt say, I will set a king over me, like as all the nations that are about me”. We are not satisfied with the King of kings and Lord of lords, Christ, being over us. We always want to be like the other nations. That is why we dye our hair blonde, put in the contacts, put on the suit and tie, go to their universities and get their education, and assimilate to their way of life.

But the law says “Thou shalt in any wise set him king over thee, whom the Lord thy God shall choose: one from among thy brethren shalt thou set king over thee: thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother.” We have to have a king of our own people, who is for our people, not a base man out for the interest of corporations that rob and steal our resources. We are not supposed to vote for other nations to be over us. Thus saith the Lord.

The same goes for our people in Latin America. In Mexico and in Argentina, where an Italian was set up, what are they doing for you? Nothing, not a damn thing. You cannot set up people of other nations over you. That is why the Most High sets the basest of men over Israel: to show us what it means to choose a stranger over the king he chose.

Deuteronomy 28:37 says Israel would become “an astonishment, a proverb, and a byword, among all nations”: called by names outside of our God-given name. God gave us a name. Israel means prince of the power with God, and there is no mightier name on the face of the earth. Why would you want to call yourself a Latinized negro, a Latino? That is a racist term. You have to do the history and get the knowledge; you have to find yourself so you don't lose yourself.

Isaiah 65:15 says the same: “And ye shall leave your name for a curse unto my chosen.” We left the name Israel for a curse, for racist terms like Latino, Hispanic, and names like Cuban, Colombian, Venezuelan, Dominican. Yet it is “unto my chosen”: we are God's chosen people. You have to see the greatness in who you are. We have fallen so far that we think we can't come out of it, but we are coming out, because there is a God.

“for the Lord God shall slay thee”. For wanting a king of another nation over us, for wanting to assimilate, the Most High slew us and caused the basest of men to rule over us. “and call his servants by another name”: now we are called Latino, blacks, spics, wetbacks, illegal aliens. That is why we do not know who we are, a confusion of faces. We are searching, but we are not searching the scriptures.

So-called Latinos, you are the Israelites. Latino is not your given name; your name is Israel, the twelve tribes of Israel. You think this is a black movement, a negro movement, but the twelve tribes of Israel are mainly so-called Latinos. We have to get back to our history and our true nationality.

Moses blessed the tribes “before his death”, and of Asher he said “Let Asher be blessed with children; let him be acceptable to his brethren, and let him dip his foot in oil.” Asher is Venezuela, Colombia, Peru, Brazil, from Colombia down to Uruguay. When the conquistadors came to conquer, rob and pillage, many fled into the jungles of the Amazon and grew up without fathers, so they must be made acceptable to their brethren, and we have to go there and save our people in the jungles. And the oil: a brother in Venezuela, asked how Venezuelans and Colombians can benefit from their precious resource, stood right on the oil. The oil is the precious commodity the red man covets so earnestly.

Then verse 25: “Thy shoes shall be iron and brass.” Look up the name Brazil: it is associated with the Hebrew word barzel, meaning iron. It is not a coincidence that the name Brazil means iron in Hebrew; these people know where our people are. Brazil is full of iron, Colombia is full of iron, Venezuela is full of iron, Ecuador is full of iron. Mexico has iron too, but not the same abundance as South America.

“and as thy days, so shall thy strength be.” That is the inheritance of our people in these lands. It is not a coincidence, the names these countries get, for those who do not believe that the northern kingdom is the northern kingdom.

The elders in the 60s and 70s deciphered this without Google or the internet; all they had were the scriptures and history books. Now, in the information age, it is so much plainer. Asher's blessing, children, oil, iron and brass, sits right where the Bible said it would.

Esau has to be revealed. The devil has to be revealed, and the scriptures reveal him by his attributes. “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” Red is a warning: when you see the red man coming, destruction and death are coming, so flee. He is red and hairy, so much that they shave nearly the whole body to normalize their appearance. Jacob is not even described, because he looked like his parents. “Two nations are in thy womb, and two manner of people”: we are not the same, and no matter how hard we try we cannot be like them. “Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field”, a predator who loves to kill and prey; “Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents”, simple, living off the land and doing our sacrifices to God.

Then Esau begged, “Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father.” His blessing: “thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above; And by thy sword shalt thou live”. How would he get the fatness of the earth? By the sword: by armies, killing, destroying and preying on other nations. That is what we see on the news.

Then, “and shalt serve thy brother”: he was meant to serve Israel, Jacob’s sons. But “and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”. He broke the yoke and is over us now, because we wanted to be like the other nations and wanted a king; God is a jealous God, and he cursed us with the basest of men over us.

His dominion is the pale horse: “his name that sat on him was Death, and Hell followed with him. And power was given unto them over the fourth part of the earth, to kill with sword, and with hunger, and with death, and with the beasts of the earth.” Hell follows him to Libya, Iraq, Iran, Venezuela, Cuba and Panama. The fourth part of the world is America, as their own book on the birth of America calls it, which is why they call this hemisphere theirs, the Monroe Doctrine become the Donroe Doctrine. With hunger: Cuba starved out by cut-off oil and sanctions. With the beasts of the earth: zoonosis, mixing animal DNA. He is the Chaldeans’ daughter, “that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land, to possess the dwellingplaces that are not theirs”, with some 850 military bases in other people’s lands. If Esau is not the devil, if they're not the wicked, then who is? The Arabs don't have military bases on every land.

Daniel says, “through his policy also he shall cause craft to prosper in his hand”: economic warfare and the witchcraft of a dollar with no gold behind it, which is why he went after Gaddafi’s African gold and Venezuela trading outside the dollar. And “by peace shall destroy many”, with peace summits led by the biggest warmongers on earth. Yet Daniel says, “but he shall be broken without hand”. Christ “shall destroy them without labour by the law”, which is why keeping and teaching God’s laws matters: the foolishness of preaching is destroying this kingdom from within. And no amount of money can hide the man of sin; he is being revealed, “that he might be revealed in his time.” The devil must be revealed in his time, through the words of the prophets and through us teaching his laws.

“Remember, O Lord, what is come upon us: consider, and behold our reproach”: see the curses that fell upon us for our sins. “Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens.” The Chicago mayor was offended by the term alien, but the term is in the scriptures. The aliens are the strangers, the other nations. We are not the aliens; we are the natives of these lands. Esau has taken our lands, our resources, our inheritance.

“We are orphans and fatherless.” Why are we orphans? Deuteronomy 28:32: “Thy sons and thy daughters shall be given unto another people.” We see it all throughout history, and even now our northern kingdom children are separated from their parents. They killed our fathers, our leaders, the caciques and kings like Atahualpa, and burned them at the stake for not accepting the Christian religion. That is why the Asher in the Amazon grew up orphans and fatherless.

“and thine eyes shall look, and fail with longing for them all the day long”. You will look to the white Jesus, but he can't save you. Donald Trump is not going to save you. The US government is not going to save you. No matter how much you perfect your English, the accent is going to slip out and they are going to catch you.

“and there shall be no might in thine hand” to save our children. We saw ICE agents, grown men with weapons and body armor, surrounding a five-year-old autistic girl and holding her hostage: a nation of fierce countenance. How much plainer can it be?

So-called Latinos, you have to see yourselves in the scriptures. You are no different from your black brothers, from Haitians, Jamaicans and African Americans; we are the same people, oppressed together. All these curses have to afflict you so that you can see this is your book, and what is happening to you for turning your back on the black Messiah, Jesus Christ. We have to return to our true nationality.

“Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand”. Who is ruling over us? Servants. The Most High made Esau to serve us, but we are serving them now.

Look at the statue they took down: Theodore Roosevelt on horseback, with a Native man and an African man walking beside him. They took it down, but it is too late; they know who they are and they know who we are. Roosevelt represents Esau, the servant. Now watch the scripture come to life: “I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth”. The horse represents authority, power and rulership. The princes walking on foot are Israel, the northern kingdom on the left and the southern kingdom on the right, walking as servants.

Esau knows who he is, and he knows this is his time to rule. But it is coming to an end. There is none that can deliver us out of their hand, not Hugo Chavez, not Fidel Castro, not Maduro with Russian helicopters and Chinese spyware. No man can save us. Our power is to keep God's commandments in the faith of Christ; when we do that, the Most High and his angels will fight for us. We have to see ourselves in these scriptures, no longer as blacks or as Latinos, but as one people, one nation.

“Our fathers have sinned, and are not; and we have borne their iniquities”. Their sins are our sins. Why? It goes back to Exodus 20:5: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them”. We cannot serve idols: Christianity, white Jesus. “for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me”.

Our fathers “are not”: they are dead and gone. But the Most High visits their sins to the third and fourth generation, so we take on those sins. Basically, we are our fathers.

That is why Lamentations goes straight on to “Servants have ruled over us”. We bowed to other gods, and a jealous God gave us over to be ruled by the nations. The ones in our own communities who lead our people into thinking we can assimilate, that this is our kingdom, are leading us deeper into it. Our fathers watched for a nation that could not save us, and we are still doing it. The way out is not to serve their idols but to come back to the God who visits the iniquity.
Why do we have to keep the book of the law in our mouth and meditate on it day and night? Because of the work of Satan. Peter shows it: “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”.

Your adversary doesn't sleep. You think Satan sleeps for a minute? He does not sleep, brothers. When you know the enemy and know his job, you understand the scripture more. The book of the law shall not depart out of your mouth because Satan is like a devouring lion waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments.

James 1:14 already showed where the fight is: “But every man is tempted, when he is drawn away of his own lust, and enticed.” When you are drawn away of your own lust, you are not in control; the lust is in control of you. So take every little thing as a big thing, because Satan is well alive here.

That is why the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty must continue therein, not a forgetful hearer but a doer. It is easy for us to go left, so we have to constantly put ourselves in the works. Either you are about it or you are not, and you cannot just be cool to everything while the lion is walking about.

James says the blessed man is the one who looks into the perfect law of liberty and continues therein, “not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of the work”. Joshua says the same thing another way: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night”.

Ask yourself, brothers and sisters: are you meditating in this book they call the Bible? Don't lie to yourself. If you have to ask, it means you need to do it more, because it is supposed to be a natural thing.

Why meditate on it day and night? Because we want to keep the ministry blameless, and because we know the job of Satan: he is like a roaring lion, waiting to get your soul, waiting for you to come off the commandments. When you meditate on something day and night, you have no time for foolishness. It is like the scriptures warning not to be idle, because when you are idle you fall back into sin. When you are constantly in the scriptures, your mind is focused on keeping the commandments. That is the pattern: stay focused.

The enemy is at work every day. Turn off the TV and the phone and you might have a two or three percent upper hand, but as long as these devices and human beings exist on this earth, our battle is serious and we are battling every day.

Joshua goes on: “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous”. That is James 1:25 again. The perfect law of liberty is what we look into: the commandments, the mercy of God, the grace of God. Christ died on the cross and gave us that grace as the platform to build upon, so we can no longer go backwards; now we have to go forward. The one who is not a forgetful hearer but a doer of the work “shall be blessed in his deed”, blessed in his teaching and his business, whatever he does.

The enemy does not sleep, and Revelation shows what he is doing: “And I heard a loud voice saying in heaven, Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.”

Satan isn't sleeping day and night. He is accusing us day and night as we study, trying to accuse us before the Lord. So we don't have time to be idle. We have to keep our minds focused, brothers. Y'all sleep on the devil if you want.

He is at work through this world too. They are trying to change times and laws and make people think that what is immoral is moral. The mind of the sinner says don't judge me and don't snitch, but the one living in sin influences others and destroys others. That is why the laws of God are important.

This is why James 1:25 calls us to look into the perfect law of liberty and continue therein. The accuser works against us before God day and night, so we must meditate in the law day and night and be doers of the work, so that we are blessed in our deed and the ministry stays blameless.

David was anointed more than once, and it starts here in Bethlehem: “Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward.” Samuel anointed him in the midst of his brethren, and the Spirit of the Lord stayed on him from that day.

After Saul was dead, David went up to the cities of Hebron, and the men of Judah came and anointed David king over the house of Judah. So he was anointed again in Hebron, but only over Judah; he was the king of Judah in Hebron.

Then all the tribes came: “Then came all the tribes of Israel to David unto Hebron, and spake, saying, Behold, we are thy bone and thy flesh.” They remembered that “when Saul was king over us, thou wast he that leddest out and broughtest in Israel”, and that the Lord had said, “Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be a captain over Israel.” So “they anointed David king over Israel.” Now he is king over all twelve. “In Hebron he reigned over Judah seven years and six months: and in Jerusalem he reigned thirty and three years over all Israel and Judah”: both kingdoms. And “David took the strong hold of Zion: the same is the city of David.” Zion is the city of David.

But the beef was already there before the split. In 2 Samuel 19 the men of Israel asked, “Why have our brethren the men of Judah stolen thee away”; Judah answered, “Because the king is near of kin to us”: he is our tribe. Israel said, “We have ten parts in the king, and we have also more right in David than ye”: there are more of us than you, why can't we anoint him over here? “And the words of the men of Judah were fiercer than the words of the men of Israel.” Judah cursed Ephraim out, and that enmity between the two stayed.

Ephraim felt more entitled, and in a way rightfully so: Joseph saved Israel from starvation in Egypt, Joshua of Ephraim brought us into the land and gave out the allotments, and Ephraim held Shiloh, Bethel and the first places of worship. So the anointing that began in the midst of David's brethren is also where the dividing hatred between Judah and Ephraim shows itself, a rivalry that went on long after David.

Where is Cornelius from? Some people say Italy. He is from Cesarea. There are three Caesareas: one in Africa, which is not written of, Caesarea Philippi, and Caesarea Maritima. Cornelius is from Caesarea Maritima, the place the maps call Strato's Tower, right under Dor, in Samaria, the same country where Christ spoke to the woman at the well. When Rome colonized our land they named it for Caesar, and Maritima because it is a port on the water. And the maps mark that land West Manasseh.

Somebody will say that's just a map, it ain't in the Bible. So here it is in the Bible, for the doubters: “And the coast of Manasseh was from Asher to Michmethah, that lieth before Shechem; and the border went along on the right hand unto the inhabitants of En–tappuah.”

Read on. “Now Manasseh had the land of Tappuah: but Tappuah on the border of Manasseh belonged to the children of Ephraim”. The coast went down to the river Kanah: “the coast of Manasseh also was on the north side of the river, and the outgoings of it were at the sea”. “Southward it was Ephraim’s, and northward it was Manasseh’s, and the sea is his border”: the Mediterranean Sea. Peter dwelt in Joppa and went some thirty to forty miles up the coast to Caesarea Maritima, just before Dor.

Then verse 11: “And Manasseh had in Issachar and in Asher Beth–shean and her towns, and Ibleam and her towns, and the inhabitants of Dor and her towns”. Under Dor was Caesarea Maritima; that was all Dor before. Endor, Taanach and Megiddo were Manasseh's too. “Yet the children of Manasseh could not drive out the inhabitants of those cities; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.” There were too many of them to conquer them all.

So that is Manasseh's land. It is called West Manasseh because Manasseh also dwelt on the other side of Jordan, East Manasseh. This was once Manasseh's allotment right under Ephraim, the sons of Joseph. Asher shared that port, but the land was Manasseh's.

Cornelius was not Italian. He was of the Italian band, a unit of the Roman army. There were Israelites in Rome's military, just as there are Israelites in America's military today. But negroes love master so much they see the word Italian and get excited: yes, he's white, I knew it. No, he was of the Italian band, from Caesarea, West Manasseh, one of the northern kingdom. A centurion was over a hundred men. He was “A devout man, and one that feared God with all his house, which gave much alms to the people, and prayed to God alway”, the exact same thing Tobit said he did.

“When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan–aram, to take him a wife from thence; and that as he blessed him he gave him a charge, saying, Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother”, Esau, seeing “that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father”, went his own rebellious way anyway. “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son”. That is how Ishmael and Esau started intermingling, and that is where the light-skinned Arabs come from.

Jacob went toward Haran, and at a certain place he dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven, “and behold the angels of God ascending and descending on it.” The Lord promised, “the land whereon thou liest, to thee will I give it, and to thy seed; And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. That is all four corners: before they were even born, it was prophesied that Jacob’s seed would be found in the four corners of the earth, scattered among the families of the earth, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.” And the Lord promised, “I will not leave thee, until I have done that which I have spoken to thee of.”

Jacob said, “this is none other but the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven”, a portal to paradise. He set up his stone for a pillar, poured oil on it, “And he called the name of that place Beth–el: but the name of that city was called Luz at the first.” He vowed the tenth, the tithe.

Keep Bethel in mind. On the map it sits right under Shechem, the place where Abraham first built an altar in Canaan and where Rehoboam was later crowned. These early holy places all lay in the land that would become Ephraim’s.

The division between Ephraim and Judah did not begin at the split of the kingdom; it was building long before. Part of it goes back to Joseph, the father of Ephraim.

Joseph was raised up to tell Pharaoh what was coming: “Behold, there come seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt: And there shall arise after them seven years of famine; and all the plenty shall be forgotten in the land of Egypt; and the famine shall consume the land”, and “it shall be very grievous”. “And for that the dream was doubled unto Pharaoh twice; it is because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.” Joseph prophesied the famine and showed Egypt how to prepare for it, and by it Israel was saved when Jacob and his sons ran down to Egypt.

The same pattern ran through Abraham. After the Lord told him, “Get thee out of thy country, and from thy kindred, and from thy father’s house”, he came from Ur of the Chaldees beyond the Euphrates, up to Haran, and down into Canaan, the stretch called the Fertile Crescent. When famine struck Canaan, Abraham ran to Egypt too, just as Jacob and his house later did. The parallels line up.

So Joseph’s house carried a great deal: Joseph saved Israel in the famine, and later Joshua, of Ephraim, divided the land. That is part of why Ephraim felt more entitled than Judah, and why the rivalry that tore the kingdom in two was already there long before Rehoboam.

“And the whole congregation of the children of Israel assembled together at Shiloh, and set up the tabernacle of the congregation there. And the land was subdued before them.” From there each tribe received its allotment of land.

On the map, the hill country of Ephraim holds Shiloh, Ai, Shechem at the top, and Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal, where the law’s blessings and curses were received. Bethlehem and Jerusalem lie further down, in Judah. All of Israel’s earliest places of worship were in Ephraim’s land: Abraham’s first altar at Shechem, Bethel, the mountains of the law, and the tabernacle at Shiloh.

So Ephraim felt entitled. They had the places of worship, the historical landmarks, and they were more in number than Judah. That is where the beef started, the buildup of the dividing hatred.

It broke open with Rehoboam. “And Rehoboam went to Shechem: for all Israel were come to Shechem to make him king”, crowned at the very place of Abraham’s first altar. Solomon had laid a heavy yoke of taxes on the people to build sanctuaries of heathen worship for his wives. The old men who had served with Solomon said, lift it and they will serve you forever; Rehoboam “forsook the old men’s counsel” and listened to the young men he grew up with: “my father also chastised you with whips, but I will chastise you with scorpions.” It was so “for the cause was from the Lord”, to fulfill what Ahijah the Shilonite told Jeroboam when he tore the garment into twelve pieces and gave him ten.

Israel answered, “What portion have we in David? neither have we inheritance in the son of Jesse: to your tents, O Israel: now see to thine own house, David.” They stoned Rehoboam’s tax collector, and made Jeroboam king. Only Judah, with Benjamin at its side, followed the house of David. When Rehoboam gathered an army, the Lord said, do not fight your brethren, “for this thing is from me.” The split was the Lord’s doing, and its roots ran back to the land at Shiloh.

“Jesus the son a Nave was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God”. This is Joshua. He fought for us to gain the land and possession promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them”, the ones who did not belong in the land, “that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Joshua was used to set us in our promised land through war, as David did later as king.

Joshua 8 shows him valiant in the wars. At Ai, when the men of the city looked back and saw the smoke of their city rising to heaven, “they had no power to flee this way or that way”, and Israel smote them until none remained: twelve thousand fell that day. “And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide”, and they raised a great heap of stones over him at the gate.

“Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal”, “an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron”. All Israel, “as well the stranger, as he that was born among them”, stood “half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal”, and there they received the blessings and the cursings of the law.

Ebal and Gerizim, like Ai, Bethel and Shechem, are in Ephraim’s land. And Joshua himself was of Ephraim. The one who set Israel in their inheritance and divided the land came from that tribe, which is part of why Ephraim felt so entitled.
blog/2026/2026-01-31-2026-01-31-my-templ:
Paul says the meat “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” So where were the animals sanctified to be eaten or not to be eaten? In the law.

Leviticus 11 closes: “For I am the Lord your God: ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He repeats it: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” How do you become holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. To sanctify yourself and be holy you have to apply the law, the statutes and the commandments.

Then: “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.” This law takes in all the animals, whether they live on the earth or in the waters. That is how the word sanctifies the meat: by making a difference between what can be eaten and what cannot. Some animals are clean, some are unclean. It is basic.

The churches don't want you to learn the Old Testament, because they don't want you to be saved. “Keep my commandments, and live”. If you don't keep the law you are not going to live. John says “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food is sin; eating pork is going to kill you, and overeating is going to kill you.

You are supposed to be the temple of God. If you keep destroying yourself with the way you eat, you are working against what the Lord says, and against the work we are all called here to do. The meat that is received with thanksgiving is the meat the law sanctified.

Christians take this chapter and say every creature is good to eat, so long as you pray over it. But Paul says the meats God created are “to be received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth.” So what is the truth? “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” The truth is the law.

That changes the whole verse. The meat is not received by everybody who bows his head over his plate. It is received by them that know the law. People say, just give thanks, just pray on it, and it's all right. Then can I pray on a human's foot and eat it? Pork carries the worm that lives in the muscle and can go to your brain; the shrimp, the lobster, the catfish and all the shellfish are bottom feeders whose job is to clean the ocean, the roaches of the sea. A prayer does not change what they are.

“For every creature of God is good” means what Genesis means: “God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good to serve its purpose. Worms prepare the land for planting, but we don't eat worms. The pig was the garbage disposal before there were trucks to pick up the garbage. Good for its work, not for your plate.

And Paul finishes: “For it is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” A Christian never reads up to that verse. The word of God is the law, the truth, and the law is what tells you which creatures are sanctified to eat. Many who have come into the truth, who know Christ is black and that we are Israel, are still struggling with that pork and that shrimp. This is the answer to that struggle: the ones who receive it with thanksgiving are those who know the law.

Paul says the meats are received “of them which believe and know the truth.” What is it to believe? “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment”. If you take heed to the commandments, you believe. Does a Christian believe in the commandments? So when he says you can eat anything as long as you receive it with thanksgiving, no: you can pray all you want, but you don't believe and you don't know the truth. Those are the very things that can save your life.

Finish the verse: “and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” If you believe in the commandments and keep the dietary laws, will you be worrying about high blood pressure? Will you be worrying about a foot amputation because of diabetes, about high cholesterol, about gout that takes brothers' fingers and feet? No, because you are not eating in a way where those sicknesses can come your way. The law tells you the food you can eat and the food you cannot eat.

All of that comes because people wanted to eat nasty, dirty food the Lord said don't eat. So take heed to yourself. Believing is not a prayer said over the plate; it is taking heed to the commandment, and the one who does fares never the worse.

Many of our people who believe Christ is black and believe they are Israelites still struggle with Paul’s words: “For every creature of God is good, and nothing to be refused, if it be received with thanksgiving”. They take it to mean, just pray over it and eat whatever you want. But what makes every creature good? “And God made the beast of the earth after his kind, and cattle after their kind, and every thing that creepeth upon the earth after his kind: and God saw that it was good.” Every creature is good for its purpose. Worms are one of the best ways to prepare land for planting, but we do not eat worms. Pigs were the garbage disposal, because they eat everything. Can you pray over a human foot and eat it?

The bottom feeders have a purpose too. Catfish, loaches, shrimp and snails are sold as natural tank cleaners: they eat the uneaten food, the algae and the waste. Put crab or any bottom feeder in murky water and in a few hours it will be clear. The filter you change in a fish tank is what you eat when you eat shrimp; that is why they are called the roaches of the sea. Lobster was once fed to prisoners. And pork carries the trichinella worm, which can travel into the muscles and even the brain. If a creature’s job is to eat garbage, what will it do to you? Gout, high cholesterol, hypertension, even lost fingers and feet.

Read the verse before and the verse after. The meats are “received with thanksgiving of them which believe and know the truth”, and “thy law is the truth.” To believe is to keep the law: “He that believeth in the Lord taketh heed to the commandment; and he that trusteth in him shall fare never the worse.” And the creature “is sanctified by the word of God and prayer.” Christians never read that far.

So where does the word of God sanctify the animals? Here: “ye shall therefore sanctify yourselves, and ye shall be holy; for I am holy: neither shall ye defile yourselves with any manner of creeping thing that creepeth upon the earth.” He says it twice: “ye shall therefore be holy, for I am holy.” And how are we holy? “Wherefore the law is holy, and the commandment holy”. “This is the law of the beasts, and of the fowl, and of every living creature that moveth in the waters, and of every creature that creepeth upon the earth: To make a difference between the unclean and the clean, and between the beast that may be eaten and the beast that may not be eaten.”

“Keep my commandments, and live; and my law as the apple of thine eye.” You move like a flash when something comes at your eye; flee from sin that fast. John says, “sin is the transgression of the law”, and “the wages of sin is death”. Eating unclean food, and overeating, is destroying the temple the Most High gave you to do his work. He wants a fit army: you cannot teach discipline in the street without having it yourself, and you cannot go to camp and become a liability.
blog/2026/2026-01-31-2026-01-31-the-prid:
“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.”

Actions are weighed when it comes to the Most High. That is why he gave us the excellent things of Proverbs 22:20: to learn them and apply them, because he wants actions behind those things. Not lip service, but actual action from all of us that he called.

Romans 15:4 says the scriptures were written for our learning; 1 Samuel 2:3 says what he does with that learning. He weighs what we do with it. Proud talk and arrogancy out of the mouth weigh nothing with him, because he is a God of knowledge and knows whether the words are backed by works.

That is the pride of thine heart: to talk big about the things of God and not live them. The one who has been given the excellent things has to put his actions where his mouth is, and keep arrogancy out of it.

“Verily thou art a God that hidest thyself, O God of Israel, the Saviour.” He hides himself. That means he is not dealing with everybody. It is not like you just say, hey God, and he turns around. He answers and reveals himself to whom he wants to.

So for you to have even a little understanding of his excellent things, to learn them and apply them to your life, means something. He is the “God of Israel, the Saviour.” If God has revealed himself to you, that you are an Israelite, that you even have a mind to conceive his words and understand them, that means something to God. It means you are worthy enough for him to reveal his words to you, so that you get a chance to know what these excellent things are.

You can’t take that lightly. Far too many people in this world do, and use the Bible for material gain and to feel good on their terms. God doesn’t get down like that. He is a God that hides himself, so if he is letting you know what these words mean, you better take heed to him.

And that is where the humbling comes in. Romans 12:3 follows it: “not to think of himself more highly than he ought to think; but to think soberly, according as God hath dealt to every man the measure of faith.” If he is revealing himself to you when he does not deal with everybody, you better have some humbleness, because that is the King of kings, the omnipotent Most High God. We are Israelites and we have to keep God’s commandments, so don’t think too highly of yourself. Humble down.

“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning.” The excellent things God wrote in Proverbs 22:20, the counsels and knowledge that make us “know the certainty of the words of truth”, were written for us to learn.

And not only to learn: “that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” These excellent things are written for us to apply to our lives, so that we can be excellent and great in God’s eyes. Learn and apply, that is what Romans 15:4 is telling us.

Everything in this Bible is the excellent things of God, the truth he wants us to know. It is not to be used to get rich off of prosperity teaching, and it is not up for debate for us to decide what we should and should not do. It is not up for debate whether we want to be great or average. God gave us excellent things because he expects excellence out of us.

So we have to change our mindset and live up to the standards of God, not the standards the world has placed on black men and women and Hispanic men, to be comfortable with the crumbs society gives us. Those excellent things are what we have to apply, and it starts with a change in the mind.
blog/2026/2026-02-01-2026-02-01-the-divi:
John says it again in his fourth chapter: “If a man say, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar: for he that loveth not his brother whom he hath seen, how can he love God whom he hath not seen?” And: “this commandment have we from him, That he who loveth God love his brother also.”

You can't love one and hate the other. It is impossible. If you love your brother, by default you love God; if you love God, by default you love your brother. They go hand in hand: God and people, God and race. What the white man promotes among his people is what we should promote among ourselves. When we say it, we're called racist; when they say it, they're patriots.

That is the light and darkness of 1 John 2. “He that saith he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is in darkness even until now.” Picture our people in captivity, while the ones who enslaved us rule. For hundreds of years they spent billions, even trillions, to hide our history from us. They tortured us, beat us, raped us, castrated us, and broke us physically, mentally, psychologically and spiritually. Their ruling is their heaven; we are in hell. And an Israelite in that hell spends himself teaching the heathen the access he has to our heaven. That is hate. You hate your people and you hate yourself, and for that you are in darkness.

Esau does not forget. He holds grudges: when they took Maduro, rumor has it they bombed the mausoleum where Hugo Chavez is buried, because Chavez spoke ill of America. But Jacob forgets, even in the midst of captivity. The man who says he loves God while caring more for his oppressor than for his own brother is, in John's own word, a liar.

Where did John get this “new commandment”? From Christ: “A new commandment I give unto you, That ye love one another; as I have loved you, that ye also love one another. By this shall all men know that ye are my disciples, if ye have love one to another.”

Christ said it to the disciples, and John repeated it in his epistle. Christ said it over and over again: “These things I command you, that ye love one another.”

That is why John can say in the same breath, “I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning”, and then, “Again, a new commandment I write unto you”. It is old because it came from Moses' time. It is called new because Israel was not following it. Going back to Moses, we were children in whom is no faith, rebellious; we waxed fat and kicked.

So the mark of Christ's disciples is love one to another, among our own people. “He that loveth his brother abideth in the light, and there is none occasion of stumbling in him.” The one who despises his brother and his people will stumble, and stumble in a lot of deep but basic things.

Christ isn't saying anything new. He calls it a new commandment, but we heard it before, in the law: “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him. Thou shalt not avenge, nor bear any grudge against the children of thy people, but thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself: I am the Lord.”

Your neighbour is your people. Your neighbour is your brother. Love your neighbour as yourself. When you despise yourself, you despise your God that resembles you and your brother that resembles you. It is a domino effect. You can't love one and hate the other.

That is what John means: “Brethren, I write no new commandment unto you, but an old commandment which ye had from the beginning.” It was there from Moses' time. And it is the very hatred Moses warned against in the beginning, when we were all together, that divided Ephraim and Judah. They began to despise each other, and that is why both fell: the northern kingdom first, and the southern kingdom afterward.

So “he that hateth his brother is in darkness, and walketh in darkness, and knoweth not whither he goeth”. Christ's new commandment was already in the law, and Israel's fall came from not keeping it.

Normally Matthew 22 is read for this, but Mark is heavy. A scribe asked, “Which is the first commandment of all?” “And Jesus answered him, The first of all the commandments is, Hear, O Israel; The Lord our God is one Lord: And thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind, and with all thy strength: this is the first commandment. And the second is like, namely this, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself. There is none other commandment greater than these.”

There is none greater, because if you love your brother as yourself you can keep all the commandments; they all go hand in hand. You cannot love God and hate your brother. By loving God you will love your brother, and by loving your brother you love God.

What Christ is really saying is: love your people, love your ways. Why would the Most High give us these laws? Because we had learned how to hate one another, and the law was given to teach us. The same laws we give to our people today: love your ways, love your people, love your neighbour.

Think how brainwashed you are in this captivity if, like Deacon Nathan was saying earlier, you are in captivity and care more about your oppressor than your own kind. Your people are being oppressed and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. That is the darkness that “hath blinded his eyes.”

Deuteronomy 17:14-15 is law. If, when you get into your land, you decide you want a king like all the nations round about, the law says fine: set a king over you. But “whom the Lord thy God shall choose”: God has to choose him, you cannot. He must be “one from among thy brethren”, of your own people, and “thou mayest not set a stranger over thee, which is not thy brother”: do not set a heathen over you. That scratches our voting right there.

Now 1 Samuel 8. “when Samuel was old, that he made his sons judges over Israel”, Joel and Abiah, judges in Beer-sheba. “And his sons walked not in his ways, but turned aside after lucre, and took bribes, and perverted judgment.” So the elders of Israel gathered to Samuel at Ramah and said, “now make us a king to judge us like all the nations.”

That is exactly what the law allowed. Samuel was righteous, and he was a priest, so it should not have been a problem. Yet “the thing displeased Samuel, when they said, Give us a king to judge us. And Samuel prayed unto the Lord.” Why would something found in the law upset such a righteous man? The Lord answers: “they have not rejected thee, but they have rejected me, that I should not reign over them.”

That is why the law is there. The Lord knew Israel would want to be like the other nations, the Hamites, the Arabs, and would reject him ruling over them from the throne above. So he said: I have something for them. I will come down through David's loins and be king over them anyway, either up here or down there. We should not want a king over us; we have a king right there.

The Lord saw it before it happened. Israel was appointed, predestined, to desire a king over them and to reject him, and he came and ruled over them on the throne down here regardless. That goes to another level, a class in itself.

At Bethel the Lord promised Jacob, “thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and thou shalt spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south”. Israel would be everywhere on the earth, through captivity and through migration, forced or willing. And the promise goes on, “and in thee and in thy seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed”: that is the Israelite families in those lands, north, south, east and west. The nations are not the ones blessed; their blessing is servitude.

Then the Lord renamed him: “Thy name is Jacob: thy name shall not be called any more Jacob, but Israel shall be thy name”. “I am God Almighty: be fruitful and multiply; a nation and a company of nations shall be of thee, and kings shall come out of thy loins”. In context that can mean all twelve tribes, but prophetically it is written that way for the division to come: the nation is the southern kingdom, Judah, and the company of nations is the northern kingdom, Ephraim. The kings out of his loins are Saul, David, Hezekiah and Josiah.

Moses shows where the division came from. “When the most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the sons of Adam, he set the bounds of the people according to the number of the children of Israel. For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the lot of his inheritance.” He kept us “as the apple of his eye.” “But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked”, rich, comfortable and rebellious, and “lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation”, which is Christ. So the Lord said, “I will move them to jealousy with those which are not a people; I will provoke them to anger with a foolish nation.” Isaiah names who is not a people: “within threescore and five years shall Ephraim be broken, that it be not a people”, after the northern kingdom joined Syria against Judah.

Hosea says the same of the company of nations: “Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” Ephraim became as Gentiles, heathens, the uncircumcision. “But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah”. Yet the number of Israel “shall be as the sand of the sea”, as promised to Jacob, and “in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God. Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head”, and that head is Christ. Ezekiel agrees: “they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all”.

The hatred between the nation and the company of nations is why both fell, the north first and Judah after. The law always said, “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart”, and “he that hateth his brother is in darkness”. Esau never forgets and holds his grudges, while Jacob in captivity forgets his own and cares more for his oppressor. The people that enslaved us tortured us, beat us, raped us, castrated us and hid our history for hundreds of years, and now they are ruling: that is their heaven, and we are in hell. Imagine being in the heathen's hell and teaching the devil in his kingdom the access he has to heaven, our heaven. That's hate. You hate your people and you hate yourself, and for that you are in darkness. In captivity, your people being oppressed, and all you care about is your oppressor: you're a dummy, and that is the kindest word for it. Love your people and love your ways, and the nation and the company of nations become one again.

“And walk in love, as Christ also hath loved us, and hath given himself for us an offering and a sacrifice to God for a sweetsmelling savour.” Christ gave himself as a sacrifice for us. His blood on the altar is the atonement Leviticus speaks of: “I have given it to you upon the altar to make an atonement for your souls”.

Likewise, we are going to have to do the same thing for our brothers and our sisters. We have to become their sacrifice. Many don't pay attention to this: when they put you to death out here, the Lord looks at it as a sacrifice. That is why it is said that in Babylon they see your altar. What did they do on the altar? Offer blood sacrifice. They are going to put us to death out here, and that is what the altar represents.

We are unto God “a sweet savour of Christ, in them that are saved, and in them that perish”. The ones who walk the other way are the ones who “in time past” walked “according to the course of this world, according to the prince of the power of the air, the spirit that now worketh in the children of disobedience”. Those children of disobedience are in the churches, in the mosques, in everything, thinking that is the way. Satan works in them because they keep no commandment. The way is through God's law, statutes and commandments, to his son Jesus the Christ.

So walking in love is walking as Christ walked: keeping the commandments, and giving ourselves for our people as he gave himself, an offering the Lord receives as a sweetsmelling savour.

Leviticus says what the blood is for: “it is the blood that maketh an atonement for the soul.” Paul shows whose blood: “For if, when we were enemies, we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son, much more, being reconciled, we shall be saved by his life.” When we were breaking God's law, we became his enemies. Being reconciled now, by Christ's life we are going to be saved.

“And not only so, but we also joy in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now received the atonement.” The blood of Christ is what gave us the atonement, so that we can build upon grace. The blood of Christ is more powerful than the animal sacrifice; it is the most powerful thing in this universe.

Read on in the chapter: “For if by one man’s offence death reigned by one; much more they which receive abundance of grace and of the gift of righteousness shall reign in life by one, Jesus Christ.” By one man's offence death came into the world because of sin, and it reigned from then until today; look at our condition. “For as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the obedience of one shall many be made righteous.”

That is the platform we have now. The platform we had under the one man's sin, we got messed up on. But Christ did it right this time, so we can build upon him and do it right because he did it right. It is through mercy we make it to the door, because our righteousness is as filthy rags; so nobody should be boasting of how perfect he is. Christ did not come for the righteous; he came for the sick, so he could heal them. And “in bringing many sons unto glory”, his death brings many sons into glory: a new body and a new mindset. So keep on trying, keep on working, and don't give up.

When Rachel wanted a child and came demanding one from Jacob, “Jacob’s anger was kindled against Rachel: and he said, Am I in God’s stead, who hath withheld from thee the fruit of the womb?” Jacob could not give what only God gives. Go ask God for that baby.

That is the same answer for the single sister who points at leadership because she has been here five, six, seven years and has no lord, while a sister who came after her already has one. Leadership is not in God’s stead. If you want a lord, go ask God, and ask him what he wants you to change first. Check yourself: maybe talk to the sister who came after you and ask how she did it, instead of calling it hatred from leadership. God put leadership in your life to watch over your soul. Be the Proverbs 31 woman, fix your mouth, do the work on the body, stop eating the ice cream at night, and know your size before you point at the fit brother. It is not something you deserve; it is something you earn, by sacrifice.

The same dumb spirit Christ cast out of the boy tells that sister to go into the world, get a lord, and bring him in, when in the world she caught nothing before. Go into the world and you are still the same negro, still the same woman; you never changed, because you would not go to the Lord. Some came here for the ride and not the work. One sister reached out to a man in the world, and he is gone; another left for a man online who said he did not believe in two or three wives, then found out he did. Some of you are not going to get a lord in this captivity, and if that is what you came for, Satan will move you out of the way.

That spirit is the one that “ofttimes” cast the child “into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”: the paycheck spent in the club that gets sprayed up, the drunk drive that costs your limbs, the mob on Eastern Parkway, in the mix of a bunch of no-good negroes up to no good. Leaving your house to go with the dumb negroes is a dumb spirit. We thought it was cool; it was a dumb and deaf spirit, not listening and not seeing our condition. “If thou canst believe, all things are possible to him that believeth”: your belief is your power. When Satan keeps attacking you, your faith is weak, so cry like the father, “Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.”

“This kind can come forth by nothing, but by prayer and fasting.” Some demons are higher than others, so fast and pray, and do not let it conquer you. And once made whole, hear Christ: “sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.” The world you left two years ago is not the world you would go back to; sin has multiplied, and worse demons are jumping on people.

Korah, Dathan, Abiram and On “took men”, “two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly, famous in the congregation, men of renown”. They were not nobodies; they had a name, and what they had was influence over the congregation. They used it against Moses and Aaron: “Ye take too much upon you”. And the results of those leaders: the earth “swallowed them up, and their houses, and all the men that appertained unto Korah, and all their goods”, and fire from the Lord “consumed the two hundred and fifty men that offered incense.” Everyone who followed them went down with them.

These things were written aforetime for our learning, and Acts 5 shows the same lesson. The apostles were brought before the council, and Gamaliel stood up and warned them: “Ye men of Israel, take heed to yourselves what ye intend to do as touching these men.” Then he gave examples.

“For before these days rose up Theudas, boasting himself to be somebody; to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves”. Four hundred men joined themselves to a man who came across as a leader, and he “was slain; and all, as many as obeyed him, were scattered, and brought to nought.” Then “rose up Judas of Galilee in the days of the taxing, and drew away much people after him: he also perished; and all, even as many as obeyed him, were dispersed.”

That is the pattern with false leaders: the leader perishes, and the ones that obeyed him perish and are scattered with him, just like the men that appertained unto Korah. “For the leaders of this people cause them to err; and they that are led of them are destroyed.” The leaders of the black community today, the Christian pastors, have our people living in hell, with drugs, gang violence, shootings on the block and adultery, and those that follow them are destroyed with them.

The Israelite way of life is structured so that if you lose your nationality, you are also cut off from your heritage. Ezra prayed for “seed unto our heart, and culture to our understanding”: culture is heritage.

So “If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget her cunning.” The right hand is your strength; you usually work with your right hand. Jerusalem is our homeland, the place where you keep the laws and keep the feasts. Forget Jerusalem, and it is like forgetting your ability to work, the thing you know how to do.

Deuteronomy 33:2 shows what is in that right hand: “The Lord came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir unto them; he shined forth from mount Paran, and he came with ten thousands of saints: from his right hand went a fiery law for them.” The law came from God's right hand.

So if you forget your identity, guess what else goes with it? Your way of life, the fiery law. Forgetting Jerusalem and losing the cunning of the right hand is losing the law along with the nationality.

“If I do not remember thee, let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth.” If we do not remember the Lord and his laws, statutes and commandments, the tongue sticks and you cannot talk; you cannot teach his laws to your people. The pastors in the churches have their tongues cleaving to the roof of their mouths, because they are not teaching the laws of God.

Ezekiel 3:26 says God does it: “And I will make thy tongue cleave to the roof of thy mouth, that thou shalt be dumb.” That thou shalt be a Christian. You are not Israel anymore, you are not keeping the commandments, you do not have faith in Christ; you have faith in white Jesus and in the white man. God made you into a Christian dummy.

Try to talk with your tongue cleaving to the roof of your mouth and hear how you sound. Everybody looks at you like, what's wrong with this dude? That is how Christians sound to those who know the Bible: level five retards, dumb ass Christians making up dumb doctrines, who think they are in the spirit of the Lord. To other Christians they sound totally fine and normal.

“and shalt not be to them a reprover”: you will be unable to reprove your people with this Bible. You are going to be like Michael Todd and Pastor Pam and all these foolish idiots, ordained ministers from the white man's theology schools and seminary classes.

And “if I prefer not Jerusalem above my chief joy”: we cannot prefer Jerusalem as our chief joy if we do not even know we are the Israelites.

What is supposed to be in your mouth? “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.” The book of the law, the Bible, God's laws: that is what belongs in your mouth, the word of God and the laws of God.

But because we have been so wicked, God made our tongue to cleave to the roof of our mouth, and we sound like idiots trying to break this Bible down. When you are a Christian you do not know it, so you say strange things and strange doctrines, like the burning mountain is a meteorite. That is the stupidness that comes out when the law is not in the mouth.

Look at the black pastor today, preaching a sermon while getting a haircut: soft, sweet, moist, squishy, and a leader in the black church. That is the result when the law departs out of the mouth of those who are supposed to teach it.

So Psalms 137:6 is the curse on the tongue for forgetting Jerusalem, and Joshua 1:8 is what the tongue was made for: the law, spoken and meditated on day and night, so that we may observe to do all that is written therein.
