blog/2026/2026-02-28-2026-02-28-navigati:
“But that no man is justified by the law in the sight of God, it is evident: for, The just shall live by faith.” Justified by the law here is the same law as the works of the law in verses 2, 5 and 10 and in Galatians 2:16: the law of sacrifice.

Paul preached the same thing in Acts 13: “Be it known unto you therefore, men and brethren, that through this man is preached unto you the forgiveness of sins: And by him all that believe are justified from all things, from which ye could not be justified by the law of Moses.” Through Christ is preached the forgiveness of sins, and all that believe in Christ's death are justified from all things, all sins.

Could you receive justification from all things under Moses? No, because animals do not atone for all things. Does Christ's death atone for all things, reconcile us from all things, justify us from all things? Yes. That is the difference.

And the law is not of faith because faith came first. “The man that doeth them shall live in them”: the man who does the sacrifices lives until he commits a sin worthy of death, and then he cannot live anymore. The just live by faith in the one whose death covers what no animal could.

“for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. That is written in Deuteronomy 21: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree: His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled.” Hanging was capital punishment among us.

So Christ took on the curses for us, the punishment and consequence of violating that covenant, when he was hung. Some say he wasn't hung, he was nailed to a cross. But if you are nailed to a wooden pole, you are hanging by your hands and feet. That is a lynching. He was hung for hours.

Peter calls it the same thing, twice: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” And again, “whom they slew and hanged on a tree.” They hung Christ on a tree, on wood, a cross. Christ died a black man's death.

Do you think the lynchings among our people were a coincidence, when the white man hung us from trees and lamps and bridges? People have been hung from time to time, but not to the capacity we have been hung; it was enforced all around among us. The curse of the tree came on our people, and Christ bore that same curse to redeem us from it, “That the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ; that we might receive the promise of the Spirit through faith.”

“For as many as are of the works of the law are under the curse.” The works of the law, in Galatians 3:2, 3:5, 3:10 and 2:16, is sacrifice, as in Nehemiah 10:33. Under the curse means under the curse of the covenant. And “Cursed is every one that continueth not in all things which are written in the book of the law to do them” is Paul quoting Deuteronomy 27.

What does that curse mean? “Cursed be the man that maketh any graven or molten image”, “And all the people shall answer and say, Amen.” Can he atone for it, reconcile with God, find justification? What animal can he use? None. Under the old covenant you get death. That is what cursed means.

So it goes all the way down. “Cursed be he that setteth light by his father or his mother”: disrespects, curses or strikes them. “Cursed be he that removeth his neighbour’s landmark.” The so-called white man has removed the neighbor's landmark: America is a stolen landmark, Africa is a stolen landmark, Australia is a stolen landmark. How can he atone when the land is still in his possession? He can't; he sits on stolen land. “Cursed be he that lieth with his father’s wife”, his stepmother. “Cursed be he that lieth with any manner of beast.” “Cursed be he that lieth with his sister”, “with his mother in law.” “Cursed be he that smiteth his neighbour secretly”: kills his brother secretly and does not get caught. “Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person”: a hitman, a mercenary.

After each one, “all the people shall say, Amen”: we all agreed to it. Then “Cursed be he that confirmeth not all the words of this law to do them”, which is exactly what Paul quotes. None of these could be atoned for with an animal. It is death all throughout.

That is why those of the works of the law are under the curse. We confirmed to do everything under that covenant of sacrifices, and if you violate a law that no animal can cover, you get the curse, which is death.

“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law.” Some people read right past that. What is the curse of the law? Death. But you need a scripture to back up what you say, and John 11 is it.

“And one of them, named Caiaphas, being the high priest that same year, said unto them, Ye know nothing at all, Nor consider that it is expedient for us, that one man should die for the people, and that the whole nation perish not.” The whole nation, all twelve tribes, perishing: that is the curse of the law. All twelve tribes broke the first covenant, and by that default we were all worthy of death. When Christ died, he took that curse upon himself for us. That is “being made a curse for us”: dying for us.

“And this spake he not of himself: but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus should die for that nation; And not for that nation only.” Not for Judah only, “but that also he should gather together in one the children of God that were scattered abroad.” Gather together in one is reconciliation, at-one-ment, atonement.

So Christ died for Judah and for Israel, all twelve tribes. Those scattered abroad are the ones Paul was going to among the heathen, among the Gentiles, while being called Gentiles themselves. That is how “the blessing of Abraham might come on the Gentiles through Jesus Christ.”
blog/2026/2026-02-28-2026-02-28-power-un:
God told Cain, “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Demons do not simply possess someone; it is a process, and they need a series of yeses. The spirits can only communicate through your thoughts and set the stage. To take full control, you have to agree with the thought, make a contract or covenant with it, and act on it. If you say, I do not agree with that, that is not according to the scriptures, the demon cannot take control of your eyes, your ears, your mouth or your tongue.

Doing well is keeping the commandments. It is a covenant with God: I am not going to watch that, eat that, touch that, taste that. Doing not well, sin lying at the door, is a covenant with death, a covenant with Satan. Satan has commandments too, and any time you disagree with keeping God's commandment, you agree to keep Satan's.

See how the yeses add up. You agree to go past the blood alcohol limit and you let a spirit take control of your body, then wonder why you slept with that person. A thought says, I do not like that sister, you agree with it and start gossiping, and now it spreads through the whole body. You know that food is not for you, but you agree with the hunger pains, the sight of it and the smell of it, and now a gluttony spirit is on you. Every contract with a thought lets the demon tunnel through the five senses to full possession of your vessel.

The answer is in Galatians 5:16: “Walk in the Spirit, and ye shall not fulfil the lust of the flesh.” Walk in the spirit by studying, keeping a strong unit, sitting at the doorsteps of the Bishop and the Deacons, and addicting yourself to God's word, and you will not have time to entertain the flesh. Stop feeding your mind hours of shows and music that taint your thinking. Reprogram and rewire yourself to develop godly habits, because “the flesh lusteth against the Spirit, and the Spirit against the flesh”.

Christ is the example. His disciples prayed him, “Master, eat”, and he said, “I have meat to eat that ye know not of.” He was the master of his own vessel: his sight, smell, taste, hearing and thoughts. Nobody programmed him but the Father. “My meat is to do the will of him that sent me, and to finish his work.” That should be our agenda: to consume the scriptures, to see, taste, hear and believe them. That is our meat and our life.

Peter warns, “Be sober, be vigilant; because your adversary the devil, as a roaring lion, walketh about, seeking whom he may devour”. Job shows how that adversary works. Satan says to God, “Hast not thou made an hedge about him, and about his house, and about all that he hath on every side?” God had a hedge of protection around Job, and Satan wanted it taken down: “put forth thine hand now, and touch all that he hath, and he will curse thee to thy face.”

God answers, “Behold, all that he hath is in thy power; only upon himself put not forth thine hand.” Notice what Satan was given. He could take Job's possessions and stir up his life, but he could not touch Job himself, meaning he could not control Job's actions. The devil does not make anybody do anything. He sets the stage, creates an environment to nourish his goal, and watches; you pull your own strings.

Keep reading into Job 2. Satan “smote Job with sore boils from the sole of his foot unto his crown”, and Job sat down among the ashes. Then his wife said, “Dost thou still retain thine integrity? curse God, and die.” Satan did not take control of her mouth. He could not get to Job, so he put the thought in the wife, the weaker vessel, because women give in to their emotions and their own thought process more than men do. She had a decision to make, and she chose to act on the thought Satan put in her.

That is the lesson for us. There are spirits in an unseen realm communicating through our minds. You cannot stop a thought from coming, but agreeing with it and acting on it is your choice. America is Satan's stage; everyone acts in the play, but you choose which script you follow.

“And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him”. Look at what it says the devil did: he put it into the heart of Judas. He did not reach in and move Judas's hands. He put the thought there, and Judas acted on that thought and betrayed Christ.

This is the same pattern as Job's wife. Satan works through the thought process. He watches, he looks for the one who will receive the thought, and he plants it. Everything after that is the person's own decision. That is why nobody can say, the devil made me do it. You made you do it.

Peter's warning fits right here: the adversary walks about “seeking whom he may devour”. He is searching for a heart that will take the thought and carry it out, the way Judas did.

Christ told his disciples what was coming: he would be betrayed and killed by the Pharisees, the scribes and the Sadducees. Then “Peter took him, and began to rebuke him, saying, Be it far from thee, Lord: this shall not be unto thee.” Peter was saying, I am not going to allow that to happen.

“But he turned, and said unto Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan: thou art an offence unto me: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but those that be of men.” Christ was supposed to die for the sins of the nation, and Satan whispered to Peter to stand in the way. Christ spotted Satan from a distance, and Peter did not even know Satan was there. That is how crafty and cunning Satan is.

Did Peter have good intentions? He did. But even when good is present, evil is always there. So good intentions are not enough; you have to measure and weigh the words you are about to speak and filter them through the word of God, to see whether this is God's intention or your own desires being worked on by the voice of Satan.

If your mind is not in tune with the scriptures, he can whisper something through your thoughts and take control and manipulate you. Being sober and vigilant means checking even your good ideas against the word.

Wisdom “goeth about seeking such as are worthy of her, sheweth herself favourably unto them in the ways, and meeteth them in every thought.” The devil walks about seeking whom he may devour, and wisdom goes about seeking those worthy of her. Wisdom has to meet you in every thought.

When a thought comes to your mind, measure it: what is the outcome of this thought? Say you get into an argument with your husband. The first thought says, say this certain word, and you can trigger him and make him feel the way you feel. Those thoughts are being fed to you: say this, say this. Wisdom filters that thought and makes sure it has godly intentions before it comes out of your mouth.

Paul wrote in 2 Corinthians 13:10 that he used his words “according to the power which the Lord hath given me to edification, and not to destruction.” The power God gave us is for edification. With every thought, ask: am I exhorting this person, or could the way I am saying it destroy them? Even good intentions and exhortation can land the wrong way.

It works the other way too. Someone may say something to you that was positive when they said it, but it hits you as negative because Satan knows what you are going through and used that person's vessel. Then comes the thought: why would they say that to you? Say this back. You choose whether to respond for edification or unto destruction, whether to bring contention or to wink at ignorance. Everything is a choice.
blog/2026/2026-02-28-2026-02-28-the-vant:
“And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.”

The men who gathered to David were not the full package. They were in distress, in debt and discontented: men with problems and issues. David took them in and became a captain over them. That was the beginning of IUIC too: men with problems and issues, taken in and built with structure and discipline. The women are built the same way, through Ladies in Waiting, Titus 2 and Daughters of Sarah.

Later those same men are spoken of differently. In 2 Samuel 17:8 Hushai says to Absalom, “thou knowest thy father and his men, that they be mighty men, and they be chafed in their minds, as a bear robbed of her whelps in the field.” They were not mighty at first. David put in the work, the same way the leadership put the work in us.

That is why it sits with “Be not deceived: evil communications corrupt good manners.” Everyone comes in with negative impulses, and we expect it. Hard times create warriors against sinful impulses, and the men are the vanguards of righteousness, to ward off any semblance of sin. When evil communications come to men and women, you shut them down and do not entertain them. The ones who come in get tried and watched, and the demons get exercised out of them through the congregation, the brothers and sisters that are watching them. If you really want to get yourself right, you will thank them for the wounds of a friend rather than the kisses of an enemy. But if you refuse to change, you have to go, because we cannot let a bad example destroy the rest of the flock.

Leviticus warns that if a daughter is prostituted, “the land become full of wickedness.” Hosea shows what full of wickedness looks like: “Hear the word of the Lord, ye children of Israel: for the Lord hath a controversy with the inhabitants of the land, because there is no truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land.” Controversy means against: the Lord is against how we live. It speaks mainly of the northern kingdom, but all of us are doing this now.

No truth: “Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and thy law is the truth.” Truth is the Bible, the laws. Nobody in the land is adhering to “Do not prostitute thy daughter”; nobody is paying attention to it or bringing that precaution into the land. No mercy: people get killed over this. Brothers have gone to jail and been shot down over it. No knowledge of God, meaning his commandments: the priest's lips should keep knowledge and the people should seek the law at his mouth, and they are not getting it at all.

“By swearing, and lying”. We heard complete lies two weeks ago: a man told everybody that nobody had told him to leave the sister alone, to make it look as if the leadership didn't know what was going on. Brothers had to stand up, bring him right back to his lying statement, and correct his wicked ass in front of everybody, so nobody would think he had a toe to stand on to justify the evil he did. Then: “and killing, and stealing”: we saw that in the videos.

All of it because the woman was taught to let her behind hang out. The Bible gives a dress code: cover your ass. The Lord gave a dress code because he knows that when the clothes come off, all kinds of things go on. David saw Bathsheba, and he lost it all. Then: “and committing adultery, they break out, and blood toucheth blood”. People get stabbed and shot up, all because she had her clothes off in the street. Do you see the connection?

So “full of wickedness” means literally full of wickedness: that is what you get when God's laws are not taught, no Bible, no scruples, no laws. Having kids through backdoor marriages produces madness like this. That is done here. You're going to do it right or you ain't going to do it at all; nobody is holding a ceremony over fornication. It starts with the fathers and mothers, who must not prostitute the daughter, because the enemy goes after the women: mess them up and the children are done.
blog/2026/2026-03-07-2026-03-07-marriage:
“But in all Israel there was none to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty: from the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no blemish in him.” Beauty became part of Absalom's identity. It was synonymous with him: his hair, his physical perfection.

And what came behind that? Ambition and rebellion. You get a big head about yourself and you start to believe certain things. Absalom rose up against his father, it came to civil war, and he died hanging from that very hair, the same thing that was vanity to him.

That is the same lesson as David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. David saw a woman “very beautiful to look upon”, he saw her, he inquired, and he took her, the same pattern as Shechem with Dinah. Out of one fleeting moment of attraction came adultery, the murder of Uriah, a national scandal, the death of the child, and chaos in David's house the rest of his days. The Lord forgave him, but he left him with drama for moving that way. Then Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty, came to pride and rebellion.

Whenever physical attraction becomes the forefront of anything, the Bible shows you that trouble comes behind it. Y'all take chess and spades seriously, seeing moves ahead and counting books, but not marriage: she look good, I got to marry her so I can have her. Attraction is the gateway to destruction if that is the only thing you are moving on.

This is why the scripture says these things: “Lust not after her beauty in thine heart; neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” The scripture teaches you not to lust after her beauty, and it says where: in thy heart, in thy mind.

“neither let her take thee with her eyelids.” She gives you the look back. You make the eye contact, you feel the chemistry, the sparks fly, the tentacles of auras come out and they embrace, and you done lost your mind. I got to have her. Bring me that. That's what I want.

That is exactly what happened to David in 2 Samuel 11:2. He walked on the roof, saw a woman washing herself, “and the woman was very beautiful to look upon”, and he moved on what he saw. Shechem saw Dinah and took her, and it ended in violence and massacre. Samson went after the one who pleased him well, and it ended in betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty, had to have her, and it ended in adultery and murder.

So Solomon's warning is the guard against the very thing David fell into: do not let the beauty get into your heart, and do not let the eyes take you. Attraction is not the foundation, and a man who moves on it alone gives up his strength.

“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” There is the physical again: the attire of an harlot and subtil of heart. She is trying to entice, and you fall for it. It works.

Here Solomon warns about being captured by appearance. How does he know these things? He said not one out of a thousand of the women he dealt with. He knew, and he probably knew before the thousandth. It goes to show how intoxicating it can be. You get caught up.

That is the thread through David on the roof in 2 Samuel 11:2. Shechem saw Dinah and took her: violence and massacre. Samson, she pleased him well: betrayal and blindness. David saw Bathsheba's beauty and had to have her: adultery and murder. Absalom, celebrated for his own beauty: pride and rebellion. And the strange women, being beautiful, lead to ruin.

That is why the Bible rarely makes much of the beauty of wives. Rebecca is known for her character, her hospitality and her faith; Zipporah's beauty is never described; Elizabeth is called righteous, not beautiful. What is highlighted in our foremothers is righteousness, obedience, wisdom and faith. The Bible doesn't deny attraction; it just isn't the foundation.

“Likewise, ye husbands, dwell with them according to knowledge, giving honour unto the wife, as unto the weaker vessel”. The knowledge and the honour you give is the commitment to play your role as a husband in all matters. Not, this is the wife you gave me. Not complaining, and not hating her, because the scripture says no man ever hated his own flesh. You deal with the situation.

Men have a moral sense in us, most of us, though some are full of error and lack that integrity. “The just man walketh in his integrity: his children are blessed after him”. Integrity is doing what's right when nobody's looking, when nobody is there to hold you accountable, like Paul said, not in my presence only. A just man moves with integrity in how he manages and steers his household and in everything else he does as a man of God.

And his children are blessed after him because he raised a stable, sound household. Dwelling with your wife according to knowledge and giving her honour is part of that provision, leadership, instruction and honour the husband owes the house, the same duty Exodus 21:10 says he shall not diminish.

Husbands are responsible for provision, leadership, instruction, and showing honour in the household to the wife and the children. Exodus 21:10 shows the provision: “her food, her raiment, and her duty of marriage, shall he not diminish”. He has to provide for his wife's basic needs. “But if any provide not for his own, and specially for those of his own house, he hath denied the faith, and is worse than an infidel”. That is how bad the Lord sees it.

Ephesians 5 describes the husband's role as sacrificial leadership: “For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body”. And verse 25: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it”. He gave himself for it. It is a sacrificial relationship.

That is why the brother who destabilizes the whole household economically is out of order. Hard times may come and the wife may hold it down for a while, as in Tobit, where she took woman's work to support the house. But Tobit did not say, you're doing good, so I'm going to play around and figure out what I want to be when I grow up. Brothers here have done that: not happy with the job, so try this business, since the wife makes good money. Knowing damn well you couldn't take those risks by yourself, you take more risk with more lives on the line than when you were responsible only for you.

The husband's measure of accountability is the heavier one. He is the saviour of the body: accountable for his wife, the house, the children, and for those moving for the nation, the nation behind that too. He puts his soul on the line for that accountability, and that is what giving himself for it means.

In Eden there was no courtship, no feast and no attraction language. God took the rib and made a woman, “and brought her unto the man.” God formed the union himself, and behind that union is a covenant. Malachi shows it: “the Lord hath been witness between thee and the wife of thy youth”. God was the one who did the first marriage, and God is in the midst of every marriage; what God joins together, man is not to put asunder.

The world kept pieces of this. When a minister says, before the Lord and all these witnesses I now pronounce you man and wife, that is a rudiment of what the Bible says, and a rudiment is only a part, not the whole.

A covenant is a contract. People understand contracts: a sports fan understands a player's contract, you understand the contract for your job and the contract for your phone plan, but somehow we do not understand the contract of marriage, which is far more powerful and profound. Covenants are built on commitment and obligation, not feelings: if you do this, then this will happen.

God speaks of the wife “against whom thou hast dealt treacherously: yet is she thy companion, and the wife of thy covenant.” Even if you are being treacherous with your wife, or she with you, you are one flesh, and that is still your companion, the wife of the covenant you made.

Signing a contract on feelings is how people get ripped off buying a car: they like the smell and the color and end up paying the interest rate and the add-ons. Some brothers marry that way: I will deal with all this because she is bad. She is not going to be bad forever. When you get old and the hormones change, you have to be able to live with that person through every dinner, every drive and every wake-up. It has to be stronger than romance and attraction.

Modern ideas about marriage assume feelings are the foundation: find the love of your life, find your prince charming. That is the confusion. The marriage God ordained in Eden stands on his order and on the covenant he witnesses, and that is what carries it through the trials.
blog/2026/2026-03-07-2026-03-07-wars-are:
“The Lord is my strength and song, and he is become my salvation: he is my God”. He will guide us. Many of us choose the ways of the world to guide us: the job guides you, the children guide you. But each of us has to walk a path, some of us start to go off it, and we have to seek good and not evil. Proverbs 3 shows what his guiding looks like.

“My son, forget not my law; but let thine heart keep my commandments”. Whose law? God's laws. Your heart is your mind. You have to learn the laws and keep the commandments, and that proves the laws are the commandments. “For length of days, and long life, and peace, shall they add to thee”. You want to live long? Despite all these wars, rumors of wars and mayhem throughout the world, you want peace? Do what he said.

“Trust in the Lord with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding”. Trust that the prophecies have to go in order. Iran is not going to bring in World War III; Iran will help unite the Arabs, and you are seeing it. And lean not on your own understanding: in the Christian church some of us used to say we're already saved. No, that's not the understanding. He that endureth to the end, the same shall be saved, and we don't know when that end is coming. So we keep enduring, keeping the commandments, seeking the good and not the evil. “In all thy ways acknowledge him, and he shall direct thy paths”.

That is how the Lord becomes our salvation in Exodus 15:2: trust in him, endure to the end, and do his commandments. Then the habitation we prepare him is the kingdom, where we have power and rule and every wrong done to us is turned upside down, not the pie-in-the-sky fairy tale of modern Christianity. The Lord is a man of war, and he is using these nations to bring a final battle. I pray I make it, and I pray you make it.

God told Noah, “Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation.” Why was Noah chosen to be delivered with his family? Peter explains it: God “spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly”.

The old world is the world we read about in Genesis 7, and God did not spare it: he killed all flesh. Noah was righteous because he preached righteousness and kept the commandments. He was a godly man in an ungodly world, and he had received his orders from God on exactly how to build the ark and did it faithfully. His standing up for God is what brought the flood in upon the ungodly.

Why is he called the eighth person? The other seven were his wife, his three sons, Shem, Ham and Japheth, and their wives. Noah is counted eighth because a true captain, a true leader, made sure his wife, his sons and their wives were on first, and he was the last one to get on the ark. When Noah gave the word, they did not question him; they got on.

That is why men of God have to be strong. We come to the Sabbath because we are sick. We are surrounded by the world all week and fighting the sin around us and in our own thoughts, so we need to be around brothers and sisters who will correct us in righteousness.

The flood shows the mind of God for destruction. Nobody was righteous except the ones on the ark. The coming destruction, a thermonuclear war, will be on another level, and we want to be spiritually the men and women in that ark, not the ones drowning. A lot more than eight will make it this time, but very few, so do not be surprised when your family does not listen. Keep the commandments, preach righteousness, and God will deliver us.
blog/2026/2026-03-08-2026-03-08-hope-ami:
The foundations of the kingdom of heaven are the same stones, the same gems, that the high priest wore. “And thou shalt make the breastplate of judgment with cunning work”: cunning work means make it look fancy. It has to be dope; it has to look good, not corny. It is made “of gold, of blue, and of purple, and of scarlet, and of fine twined linen, shalt thou make it.”

“Foursquare it shall be being doubled; a span shall be the length thereof, and a span shall be the breadth thereof.” It was designed like a square, the same height as it was wide, just like the kingdom, where the length and the breadth and the height are equal.

“And thou shalt set in it settings of stones, even four rows of stones”: sardius, topaz and carbuncle; emerald, sapphire and diamond; ligure, agate and amethyst; beryl, onyx and jasper. And “they shall be set in gold in their inclosings”, the gold holding them in.

“And the stones shall be with the names of the children of Israel, twelve, according to their names, like the engravings of a signet; every one with his name shall they be according to the twelve tribes.” These stones are the names of the children of Israel. Revelation 21 says the same thing about the kingdom of heaven: its foundations and its gates carry the twelve tribes. The Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20 is built on Israel.

Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people”, and Isaiah 25 shows why: those fierce nations will be subdued. “Therefore shall the strong people glorify thee, the city of the terrible nations shall fear thee.” The terrible nations, the ones that made everyone afraid, will themselves fear the Most High.

“For thou hast been a strength to the poor, a strength to the needy in his distress, a refuge from the storm, a shadow from the heat, when the blast of the terrible ones is as a storm against the wall.” That is us. Verse 4 is Israel: the poor and the needy that the terrible ones have been blasting against like a storm, and God has been our refuge through it.

“Thou shalt bring down the noise of strangers”, and that goes right back to verse 3: the city of the terrible nations shall fear. Then, “the branch of the terrible ones shall be brought low”: their branch, their people, brought low. So when Isaiah 33 says we shall not see that fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, it is because God has brought them down.

Psalms 122:5 says “For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Christ tells his apostles where those thrones are: “That ye may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.”

The thrones in Jerusalem are thrones for judging the twelve tribes. That is why Psalms 122 says it is whither the tribes go up, the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, and not all nations.

So the quiet habitation of Isaiah 33:20, the city of our solemnities, is the seat of the kingdom, with Christ's table and the thrones of the house of David set in it.

“I was glad when they said unto me, Let us go into the house of the Lord.” That should make you glad. When somebody says, let's go up to the sanctuary, and you sigh, there is something wrong with your spirit. “Our feet shall stand within thy gates, O Jerusalem.”

“Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”: the same height and the same width. Revelation 21 shows it: the city lieth foursquare, the length and the breadth and the height of it equal, measured by the angel, its foundations garnished with the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28, the stones with the names of the twelve tribes.

“Whither the tribes go up.” Wait a minute. Where all nations go up? No: whither the tribes go up, “the tribes of the Lord, unto the testimony of Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the Lord.” The testimony of Israel, because that kingdom is what was always prophesied. The kingdom is not for everybody.

“For there are set thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.” Luke 22:30 shows those thrones, sitting on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel, and Revelation 20:4 shows who sits on them: the souls beheaded for the witness of Jesus, who had not worshipped the beast, the white man's kingdom, nor his image, his religion and his politics, nor received his mark, his lies in their foreheads, their minds. They live and reign with Christ a thousand years. This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

Psalms 140 proves who the people are that delight in war. “Deliver me, O Lord, from the evil man: preserve me from the violent man.” Psalms 68 said scatter the nations that delight in war; don't you see Trump and them delighting in war?

“Which imagine mischiefs in their heart; continually are they gathered together for war.” You thought it would end with Venezuela. Oh, no. He said we are going to hit Iran. You thought it ended there; next week Mexico, and maybe Cuba. The party is not over.

“They have sharpened their tongues like a serpent”: the things they say. Don't you hear them mocking the nations? They wanted to land in Spain, Spain said no, and now they are mad and talking about Spain. And “adders’ poison is under their lips”: their philosophies, their religions, their politics. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

“Keep me, O Lord, from the hands of the wicked”: this so-called white man, keep me from their hands. Then, “preserve me from the violent man; who have purposed to overthrow my goings.” They purposed to overthrow the goings of the children of Israel. “The proud have hid a snare for me, and cords; they have spread a net by the wayside; they have set gins for me. Selah.” Traps all around.

These are the fierce nations of Isaiah 33:19. When the Lord scatters them, we shall not see that fierce people any more, and Jerusalem will be a quiet habitation.

Isaiah 33:20 says to look upon Zion and see Jerusalem “a quiet habitation, a tabernacle that shall not be taken down”. Habitation meaning at rest, at peace. Like a tent with stakes driven down, not one stake of Jerusalem shall ever be pulled up, and not one cord broken.

Psalms 46 says the same: “There is a river, the streams whereof shall make glad the city of God, the holy place of the tabernacles of the most High. God is in the midst of her; she shall not be moved: God shall help her, and that right early.”

“The heathen raged, the kingdoms were moved”: all the heathen nations, the same ones we read about in Isaiah 33:19, the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue that we cannot understand. Their kingdoms shall be moved. And “he uttered his voice, the earth melted. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.” God is our refuge; it is true.

So the nations are moved, but Jerusalem is not. She shall not be moved, because God is in the midst of her.

“Great is the Lord, and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, in the mountain of his holiness.” The mountain of his holiness is Jerusalem.

“Beautiful for situation, the joy of the whole earth, is mount Zion, on the sides of the north, the city of the great King.” This is the Zion that Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon: “Look upon Zion, the city of our solemnities.” It is the city of the great King, the joy of the whole earth.

So the quiet habitation Isaiah saw is not a small thing. It is the city where the Lord is greatly praised, beautiful for situation, and it will never be taken down again.

“The Lord said, I will bring again from Bashan, I will bring my people again from the depths of the sea.” Why bring them again? Because God's people are not in the holy land. “That thy foot may be dipped in the blood of thine enemies, and the tongue of thy dogs in the same.” Damn! Our foot shall be dipped in the blood of our enemies, and those nations that run their mouths against us, the same with them.

“They have seen thy goings, O God; even the goings of my God, my King, in the sanctuary.” That is the sanctuary. “The singers went before, the players on instruments followed after; among them were the damsels playing with timbrels.” People singing before the Lord, not like these churches: beautiful songs, with men and women behind them playing instruments and young girls with timbrels. “Bless ye God in the congregations, even the Lord, from the fountain of Israel.” The fountain of Israel is Christ.

“There is little Benjamin with their ruler, the princes of Judah and their council, the princes of Zebulun, and the princes of Naphtali.” Little Benjamin because they almost got wiped out, and they are the youngest tribe, the baby tribe. This is his re-established kingdom.

“Because of thy temple at Jerusalem shall kings bring presents unto thee”: tribute. “Rebuke the company of spearmen”, the soldiers, “the multitude of the bulls”, the people that have power in the other nations, “with the calves of the people”, their little ones, “till every one submit himself with pieces of silver”: till every nation submits and brings us tribute. Then, “scatter thou the people that delight in war.” You know who that is? The white man. If there is no war, he will make one; if there is peace on earth, he will undo it. They changed the Department of Defense to the Department of War. They delight in war.

This is the Jerusalem of Isaiah 33:20: the temple standing, the tribes gathered, the kings bringing tribute, and the fierce nations subdued.

“Arise, O Lord; let not man prevail”: let not man prevail against us. Then, “let the heathen be judged in thy sight”: let the heathen nations be judged in his sight. “Put them in fear, O Lord: that the nations may know themselves to be but men.” These nations must learn that they themselves are only men. “Selah”, meaning it is true.

Then read Isaiah 33:19 again: “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” Why? Because they shall be subdued. It is “a people of a deeper speech than thou canst perceive; of a stammering tongue, that thou canst not understand”: that is the other nations, whose languages we do not know.

The nations have acted like gods over Israel. The Most High puts them in fear so they know they are but men, and then they are subdued and forced to worship the King. That is why we will not see that fierce people again.

“Who shall not fear thee, O Lord, and glorify thy name? for thou only art holy: for all nations shall come and worship before thee; for thy judgments are made manifest.” His judgments made manifest are his prophecies and his laws coming to pass before everyone's eyes.

This is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” When all nations come and worship before the Most High, they are no longer fierce against Israel. They are subdued. That is what the Lord is saying here: these nations will be brought down and made to come and worship before him.

So the fierce people of a deeper speech and a stammering tongue, the nations whose languages we cannot understand, will not be seen raging against us any more. They will be bowing before the King, because the Lord only is holy and all the nations will fear him.

“And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”: the thrones of judgment of Psalms 122.

Then “I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: that is great tribulation. They are the ones “which had not worshipped the beast”: which had not worshipped this white man, this kingdom. Nor “his image”: his religion, his politics. And they had not “received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: they did not receive his lies in their foreheads, in their minds.

And so “they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years.” Those who come through great tribulation without bowing to the beast are the ones who sit on the thrones in the Jerusalem Isaiah 33:20 describes, the tabernacle that shall not be taken down.

Psalms 122 says “Jerusalem is builded as a city that is compact together”, and Revelation 21 shows what that means: “the city lieth foursquare, and the length is as large as the breadth”, measured “with the reed, twelve thousand furlongs. The length and the breadth and the height of it are equal.” It is as tall as it is wide.

Twelve thousand furlongs is about 1,500 miles by man's measurement, but it is not man's measurement: “according to the measure of a man, that is, of the angel.” It is angelic measurement, so the size is not what we are thinking.

And “the building of the wall of it was of jasper: and the city was pure gold, like unto clear glass. And the foundations of the wall of the city were garnished with all manner of precious stones.” Garnished means decorated: all kinds of fancy designs in the walls of Jerusalem. Jasper, sapphire, chalcedony, emerald, sardonyx, sardius, chrysolite, beryl, topaz, chrysoprasus, jacinth, amethyst. Each stone represented one of the tribes, the same stones the high priest wore in Exodus 28. “And the twelve gates were twelve pearls”, “and the street of the city was pure gold, as it were transparent glass.”

And the city “had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel.” So the kingdom is not for everybody. This is the Zion Isaiah 33:20 tells us to look upon, the tabernacle that shall never be taken down.

Zechariah shows what it looks like when the nations are subdued: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Those that are left are the ones who came against Jerusalem. These nations are going to be forced to give up their idols and come before the King. Year after year they must go up and keep the feast of tabernacles, the very feast they never kept.

That is why Isaiah 33:19 says “Thou shalt not see a fierce people.” The fierce nations with a stammering tongue will not be fierce any more; what is left of them will be worshipping the King, the Lord of hosts, at Jerusalem.

When the books of Jerusalem were burned, the Lord told Ezra not to worry, and gave him the cup: “And I took it, and drank: and when I had drunk of it, my heart uttered understanding, and wisdom grew in my breast, for my spirit strengthened my memory.”

That last part is the point. God needed something to work with. The Spirit had to access Ezra's memory so that he could rewrite the records. It is like the movie Limitless: the pill opened his memory all the way back, so he could remember things he had only glanced at.

So if you do not read the Bible except on the Sabbath and you pray, Lord, open my wisdom, the Spirit comes and there is nothing in there: no memory to access and bring to your mind. Wisdom and knowledge can only be the stability of your times if the word has been put in you first, so give the Lord something to work with.

Wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times. 2 Peter 2:14 is the flip side of that, what it looks like when your life is not stable and your mind is not saturated with the word of God: “Having eyes full of adultery, and that cannot cease from sin; beguiling unstable souls: an heart they have exercised with covetous practices; cursed children.”

Our people have eyes full of adultery and cannot cease from sin. They beguile unstable souls, the ones without the stability of the word. Our people are cursed children.

Many of us have children, and we all want them to walk right with the Lord. We train them up the best we can, just like the prophet Samuel, yet Samuel's sons went to hell off. Be mindful, especially the women: you have to know the spirits in your children. You are going to find out which ones serve the Lord and which ones don't.

“And wisdom and knowledge shall be the stability of thy times.” Why is that important? The wisdom and knowledge of this Bible keeps us mentally and spiritually stable. Deuteronomy 28:28 shows the opposite: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

Madness: our people are crazy, mentally unstable, mentally insane. Blindness: we are spiritually blind. Astonishment of heart: our people are always shocked at what is going on in the world.

That is the curse that wisdom answers. Brothers, we all need the wisdom of God and the knowledge to keep us mentally and spiritually stable. The people who know the Bible are not shocked when these things happen, because the Bible already said it; the people without it are astonished at every turn.

“If any of you lack wisdom, let him ask of God, that giveth to all men liberally, and upbraideth not; and it shall be given him.” If any of you are dumb as a rock, ask of God. Some do not have the spirit of discernment: they see right and wrong in front of them and cannot discern it. When judgment is passed there is always that one who asks why a brother or sister had to be put out of the school when all they did was commit a little adultery. Shut up and sit down; they cannot discern. So pray, as Hezekiah laid his prayer before the Lord: pray for wisdom, knowledge and the spirit of discernment.

“But let him ask in faith, nothing wavering.” And give the Lord something to work with. You cannot sit at the table with a chicken leg in one hand and a steak in the other praying, Lord, help me lose weight. Likewise you pray for wisdom but the Bible is closed Sunday through Friday and opened only on the Sabbath. The views on the classes peak on Saturday and nobody watches the rest of the week, the same as Christians on Sunday. Many are called, few are chosen; this is for the chosen few that know what to do.

“For he that wavereth is like a wave of the sea driven with the wind and tossed.” “A double minded man is unstable in all his ways”: not some of his ways, all of them. Reading once a week leaves nothing for the Lord to work with.

“Let the brother of low degree rejoice in that he is exalted.” That brother is studying, reading and praying, Lord help my understanding, even when he does not understand yet. The quiet brother who did not do much talking years back becomes the one breaking down what the scriptures mean. If reading hurts your eyes, put on Bible audio at night and wake up to the scriptures.

How has the Lord “filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”? Jeremiah 23:5: “Behold, the days come, saith the Lord, that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.”

This righteous Branch is Christ. He is the King who shall reign and prosper, and he is the one who executes judgment and justice in the earth. So when Isaiah 33:5 says “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness”, it is through Christ, the King, the King of kings.

That is our hope amid destruction. When the Lord rises up, the nations are scattered and their spoil is gathered like the gathering of the caterpillar, and the righteous Branch of David reigns over Zion with judgment and justice.

“O Lord, be gracious unto us; we have waited for thee”: that is our prayer, just like Hezekiah prayed. We have to wait on the Lord. “The Lord is exalted; for he dwelleth on high: he hath filled Zion with judgment and righteousness.”

Jeremiah 9:24 shows what Israel glories in: “But let him that glorieth glory in this, that he understandeth and knoweth me, that I am the Lord which exercise lovingkindness, judgment, and righteousness, in the earth: for in these things I delight, saith the Lord.” That is what we have to glory in, brothers: that we understand and know the Lord.

All nations do not understand and know the Lord, so they do not glory in the Lord. The judgment and righteousness the Lord delights to exercise in the earth are the same judgment and righteousness he has filled Zion with. Knowing him is Israel's glory, while the nations are scattered at the lifting up of himself.

Luke 21 shows people who are unstable in all their ways, wavering like the waves of the sea. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars”: eclipses of the sun, lunar eclipses, what they call blood moons. “and upon the earth distress of nations, with perplexity”: we are living in that time now. Perplexity means confusion. They said Venezuela was drug dealers, as they did with Manuel Noriega; they said Iraq had weapons of mass destruction and did not find one bomb. Anytime white people say it is a complex issue, it is something very easy that they don't want you to know: Maduro was selling his oil in foreign currencies, not the United States dollar; Iran was doing the same; Gaddafi wanted to.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear, and for looking after those things which are coming on the earth.” Why are they afraid? We are not afraid, because wisdom and knowledge are the stability of our times: this is what the Bible was talking about, while everybody else is confused. “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken”: America, England, France, Germany.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory. And when these things begin to come to pass, then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” It is going to be almost time to go home.

But there is more to the one word perplexity: it goes into Jacob's trouble, the great tribulation that comes to try us. People want to skip the tribulation and say, war, Christ might come back tomorrow. No he won't. Jacob's trouble has to come to pass first.

Christ says it himself: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days.” People say there is no tribulation; there is going to be tribulation. Then “shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light”, as Luke read, “and the stars shall fall from heaven”: missiles. “and the powers of the heavens shall be shaken”: America, Britain, Germany, France, Russia, Canada, Spain, all those European nations, shaken with war.

How do we know the heavens are those nations? Isaiah 34: “And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine”: bombs, nuclear bombs, missiles and satellites dropping out of the sky. “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea.” Idumea is the Greek and Roman name for Edom: America, France, Germany, Britain, Russia. That is heaven.

“And then shall appear the sign of the Son of man in heaven.” After the tribulation there is still war; so don't say there's war, we're going home tomorrow. Where is the great tribulation, Jacob's trouble?

“And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds.” He is not gathering everybody, only the elect: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect.” The elect are the Israelites, not Baptists, Pentecostals, Muslims or Catholics. That is our hope amid destruction.

For the brother who says he has a reading impediment, or that his eyes hurt: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” This is a brother who is mentally slow, lacking ability, and poor.

“yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate”. The Lord lifted his head from misery, so that many who saw it marveled. It is the same as James's brother of low degree who rejoices that he is exalted.

So it is not impossible, but give the Lord something to work with. Show him that you believe and have faith, and he can do wonders. If you want to lose weight, get in the gym, eat smaller portions, walk around the block once, then twice, and let the Lord do the rest. Instead of five pieces of chicken, eat one; you won't die. In the same way, put on Bible audio if reading is hard. Do your part and the eye of the Lord will look upon you for good.

“the fear of the Lord is his treasure.” Sirach 19:20 says “The fear of the Lord is all wisdom; and in all wisdom is the performance of the law, and the knowledge of his omnipotency.”

So the fear of the Lord is all wisdom. Brothers and sisters, if you don't fear the Lord, that is where your problems are.

And in all wisdom is the performance of the law: the application of God's law. We must not just talk about it; we must be about it. We must do it. The wisdom and knowledge that are the stability of our times are not only words in the head; they are the law performed, joined to the knowledge of his omnipotency. That is the treasure the Lord loves.
blog/2026/2026-03-15-2026-03-15-prophesy:
Daniel says the king of fierce countenance “shall destroy the mighty and the holy people.” Haven't we been destroyed? We have been destroyed as a people. Watch the wording of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee.” The Lord sent Europe against us; the Lord sent America against us. “in hunger”: for food. “and in thirst”: for water. “and in nakedness”: for clothing. “and in want of all things”: if you want anything, you have to go to your enemies. If you want education, go to your enemies. If you want to learn about God, you have to go to your enemies.

“and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Here is the part we want: until he have destroyed us. The yokes of iron have been taken off. What does that prove? That we have been destroyed, exactly what Daniel 8:24 says.

And Daniel goes on: “by peace shall destroy many.” Donald Trump calls himself the president of peace and set up a board of peace, yet he has bombed Yemen, Somalia, Iraq, Iran, Syria, Nigeria and Venezuela. We are living in that time right now.

Who is in the heaven that is going to rejoice? Isaiah 34:5: “For my sword shall be bathed in heaven: behold, it shall come down upon Idumea, and upon the people of my curse, to judgment.”

Christ's sword shall be bathed in heaven and come down upon heaven. Look up Idumea: pertaining to Edom, the Greek and Roman name for Edom. That is what the heavens are. Edom today is America, Germany, France, Great Britain, Australia, Canada.

Don't let anybody tell you Edom was already destroyed. If he were, then who is Christ coming back to kill here in Isaiah 34? The people of his curse are still standing in the heavens, and that is why Daniel's king of fierce countenance “shall be broken without hand” in the last kingdom.

“And in the latter time of their kingdom, when the transgressors are come to the full, a king of fierce countenance, and understanding dark sentences, shall stand up.” A leader, a system of fierce countenance, which understands dark sentences, scriptural texts, to a degree. John shows the same thing in Revelation 12:12.

“Therefore rejoice, ye heavens, and ye that dwell in them.” That is not the sky; the sky doesn't go woo. It is men living in dominion, in rulership: Edom today, America, Germany, France, Great Britain, Australia, Canada. Those are the heavens, and those that dwell in them.

“Woe to the inhabiters of the earth and of the sea!” Woe means destruction. The earth is the third world countries, like the continent of Africa. The sea is the islands: Puerto Rico, Santo Domingo, Haiti, Jamaica, the Melanesian islands. If you do not live in the heavens, if you are beneath them, woe to you.

“for the devil is come down unto you, having great wrath, because he knoweth that he hath but a short time.” The devil lives in the heavens, and his time is almost up. That is the parallel between what Daniel said and what John said: the king of fierce countenance who stands up in the latter time is the same devil who rules from the heavens with great wrath.

“And his power shall be mighty, but not by his own power.” What does that mean? Revelation 13: “And the beast which I saw was like unto a leopard”, like the Greeks, “and his feet were as the feet of a bear”, like the Medes and Persians, “and his mouth as the mouth of a lion”, similar to Babylon, “and the dragon gave him his power, and his seat, and great authority.”

That dragon is Satan. They say God bless America, but no: Satan gave them their power. That is why Satan said to Christ that if he would bow down and worship him, he would give him all the glory and kingdoms of the world, for that was given to him to give to whomsoever he desired.

Then Daniel says he “shall destroy the mighty and the holy people”: the twelve tribes of Israel. This man destroyed us. Revelation 13:7 says it too: “And it was given unto him to make war with the saints, and to overcome them.” The same man who stands up in the last days made war with the saints, and the saints are the twelve tribes of Israel. They overcame us and destroyed us. “and power was given him over all kindreds, and tongues, and nations”: he ruled everybody.

Seventy weeks are determined “to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.” To make an end of sins is Christ coming to die, and the reconciliation for iniquity is all through Christ.

And who is the most Holy that is anointed? “How God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Ghost and with power: who went about doing good, and healing all that were oppressed of the devil; for God was with him.” Christ is the anointed one.

So the bottom of Daniel 9:24, “to anoint the most Holy”, is Christ, anointed as the most Holy. That is why the seventy weeks run unto “the Messiah the Prince”: the whole prophecy is counted to him and fulfilled in him.

The Lord gives the same count a second time, to Ezekiel: “thou shalt bear the iniquity of the house of Judah forty days: I have appointed thee each day for a year.” Each day for a year. With Numbers 14 that is two witnesses to the code: a day in prophecy is a year.

Now Daniel 9 opens up. “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people”: seventy weeks equals 490 years. “from the going forth of the commandment to restore and to build Jerusalem unto the Messiah the Prince shall be seven weeks, and threescore and two weeks”: seven weeks plus sixty-two weeks is sixty-nine weeks, 483 years. That commandment started with Cyrus, when God told the Persians to let his people go to rebuild; Israel was hindered two years, then came Darius and Artaxerxes, and the building went on under Zerubbabel, Joshua, Ezra and Nehemiah, with Haggai and Zechariah. “the street shall be built again, and the wall, even in troublous times”: our forefathers caught hell from the nations and built with a sword in one hand and a brick in the other.

“after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself”: Christ crucified, not dying for himself but for the twelve tribes of Israel. “the people of the prince that shall come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary”: Rome, in 70 AD. Then the last week: “he shall confirm the covenant with many for one week: and in the midst of the week he shall cause the sacrifice and the oblation to cease”, and “for the overspreading of abominations he shall make it desolate”, the abomination in the temple Christ warned about.

The total of seventy weeks has been fulfilled. Amalek tells Christians that last week has not happened yet and belongs to a rebuilt temple today, counting on blacks and Latinos not understanding the scriptures and going along with whatever they say because they are white. Counted a day for a year, the way the Lord counts it, all seventy weeks are done.

Edom twists Daniel 9, so here is the code to break it down. Write it down: each day represents one year, each week represents seven years, and seventy weeks is 490 years. How do we know? Start with why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

“After the number of the days in which ye searched the land, even forty days, each day for a year, shall ye bear your iniquities, even forty years”. The spies searched the land forty days. Because Israel sinned, they bore their iniquity forty years in the wilderness, a year for every day. “and ye shall know my breach of promise”: the Lord told them not to go up there, and they went up anyway.

That is the Lord himself counting a day for a year. So when Daniel is told “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city”, those weeks are counted the same way: seventy weeks of seven days, every day a year, 490 years.

“And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” This answers the question of who the people of all nations, kindreds and tongues are. They were Jews, Israelites, and they came out of every nation under heaven.

That is exactly what Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4: the Lord would scatter Israel among the nations. So when scripture shows a people coming out of every nation, it is not speaking of the nations themselves. It is speaking of Israel, found in every nation because the Lord scattered them there.

So Acts 2:5 is the key for Revelation 7:9. Out of every nation does not mean every nation's people; it means the devout Israelites dwelling among every nation, the same scattered people Deuteronomy 4:27 speaks of, who are seeking the Lord from thence.

“James, a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad, greeting.” James wrote his letter to the twelve tribes, and he says where they are: scattered abroad. The scattering Moses prophesied in Deuteronomy 4:27 had already come upon them, and the apostles were writing to Israel in the nations.

It stands with Ezekiel 28:25, read in the same moment: “When I shall have gathered the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered, and shall be sanctified in them in the sight of the heathen, then shall they dwell in their land that I have given to my servant Jacob.” Israel is scattered among the people, and the Lord gathers Israel out of them back to the land he gave Jacob.

So the great multitude out of all nations in Revelation 7:9 is the twelve tribes scattered abroad, gathered back. This is what you say when they try to tell you on the street that people coming out of all nations means all peoples. If you let them confound you with Revelation 7:9, shame on you.

“After this I beheld, and, lo, a great multitude, which no man could number, of all nations, and kindreds, and people, and tongues, stood before the throne, and before the Lamb”. Christians go to Revelation 7:9 to try to confuse you. They say all people coming out of all nations means all peoples, every race, standing before the throne.

But Moses already told us who would be found in all nations: “the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen”. That scattering was slavery, and we were left few in number because they were killing us. So a great multitude coming out of every nation and kindred and tongue is the scattered children of Israel, gathered back out of the lands they were taken to.

The precepts read right behind it settle it: Acts 2:5 shows Jews, devout men, “out of every nation under heaven”; Tobit 13 says “ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them”; Ezekiel 28:25 speaks of the Lord gathering “the house of Israel from the people among whom they are scattered”; and James wrote “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. The multitude before the throne is Israel out of every nation. If they confound you with Revelation 7:9 on the street, shame on you.

“Confess him before the Gentiles, ye children of Israel: for he hath scattered us among them.” Tobit is speaking to the children of Israel, and he tells us plainly where they are: scattered among the Gentiles. The Lord did the scattering, just as Moses said in Deuteronomy 4:27.

“There declare his greatness, and extol him before all the living: for he is our Lord, and he is the God our Father for ever.” There, in those lands where we were scattered, declare his greatness. It is the same thing Moses said in Deuteronomy 4: “But if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him”. From thence, from the lands we were taken to, we seek him, and we are seeking him now here in America and finding him.

So Tobit proves both halves of the opened scripture: Israel scattered among the Gentiles, and Israel turning to confess the Lord right there among them. He is our Lord, the God of our fathers for ever, and he has not forgotten the covenant of our fathers.

If they want to use any scripture about a third temple, this is where you go. If they build that temple, this is what we are going to use: “Who opposeth and exalteth himself above all that is called God, or that is worshipped; so that he as God sitteth in the temple of God, shewing himself that he is God.”

Who is that? The white man, who opposes everything the Bible says. Before 70 AD, before they destroyed it, Rome entered our temple and sat their rusty butt down. And after Titus destroyed Jerusalem, Rome built Aelia Capitolina on its ruins, named for the emperor Hadrian, whose clan name was Aelius, and for Jupiter, Juno and Minerva: that is the trinity, where Christianity got that doctrine. A sanctuary to Jupiter, that is Zeus, the devil, was built on the Temple Mount, statues of Roman gods were set up in intentional violation of Old Testament law, and the real Jews were forbidden the city. The walls of the old city today follow the Roman walls: the wailing wall they hump on nowadays.

Now they are trying to build on the Temple Mount again. If the Lord allows them to be successful, one will sit there saying I am God, and everybody will cheer. No. That is the man Paul warned of.

The true third temple is the one in Isaiah 60, under Christ: the strangers build its walls, the nations bring their wealth to its gates, and those who despised us bow at the soles of our feet and call it “The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.”

What about the strangers? Are they going to be in the kingdom? Yes, but read how. “For the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will yet choose Israel, and set them in their own land”. He is not having mercy on everybody on the planet. He said Jacob: the twelve tribes of Israel. That's us. He will set them in their own land: not the League of Nations, not the UN.

Then: “and the strangers shall be joined with them, and they shall cleave to the house of Jacob”: joined to obey us. “And the people shall take them, and bring them to their place”. All nations will be put where they rightfully belong. The Arabs in North Africa are not supposed to be there; that belongs to Ham, and they will be moved out. The white man in Australia does not belong there, and the white man in South Africa will be removed out of that land.

Then: “and the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors”. That is the law of Leviticus 25 just read: the laws will be re-implemented.

“And it shall come to pass in the day that the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow, and from thy fear, and from the hard bondage wherein thou wast made to serve”. That is why Christ said come unto me, all ye that labour and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. People say rest from sin; not just sin. Slavery is the result of sin, and oppression is the result of sin. That is the rest Christ was talking about.

Back in Isaiah 60, that is why “the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”: we will possess them, as servants and handmaids. The Bible does not contradict itself; Christianity contradicts the Bible.

Isaiah 60 is the true third temple. Solomon built the first; Zerubbabel and Joshua rebuilt the second during the Persian captivity; and here is the third. “And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls”. The third temple is built by the other nations, because the other nations will be our slaves. That makes some nervous, but that is what it says.

Here is the law behind it, for anyone struggling: “Moreover of the children of the strangers that do sojourn among you, of them shall ye buy, and of their families that are with you, which they begat in your land: and they shall be your possession.” Those are the same strangers Isaiah speaks of in verse 10. We shall own them, possess them as slaves.

“And ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you, to inherit them for a possession; they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? For ever. Then: “but over your brethren the children of Israel, ye shall not rule one over another with rigour”.

So when Isaiah says “their kings shall minister unto thee”, it is that law being carried out in the kingdom. God was angry with us and smote us, and we went into slavery: “in my wrath I smote thee”. Then: “but in my favour have I had mercy on thee”: that is why he sent Christ. Now the order is turned back to what the law always said: the strangers serve, and Israel is not ruled with rigour.

Still on the third temple: “And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them”. Power was given unto them.

Then: “and I saw the souls of them that were beheaded for the witness of Jesus, and for the word of God”: the martyred. Then: “and which had not worshipped the beast, neither his image, neither had received his mark upon their foreheads, or in their hands”: the mark of sin, that lets you know it is somebody in these last days, who would not support the beast.

Then: “and they lived and reigned with Christ a thousand years”. Notice the top of it: thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given unto them. This is the third temple being built up. We are going to reign with Christ for a thousand years.

That is why Isaiah 60 ends with the ones who afflicted us bowing: “all they that despised thee shall bow themselves down at the soles of thy feet; and they shall call thee, The city of the Lord, The Zion of the Holy One of Israel.” It is the same thing Revelation 3:9 said. The third temple is under Christ, not what the Christians make of Daniel 9.

“And the nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it: and the kings of the earth do bring their glory and honour into it.” Saved here does not mean what people get confused about. It means left over: “every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem”. Those that are left walk in the light of it: they obey the commandments, and come up to worship the King of kings and keep the feast of tabernacles.

“And the gates of it shall not be shut at all by day: for there shall be no night there.” That is the third temple, the same gates of Isaiah 60: “thy gates shall be open continually; they shall not be shut day nor night; that men may bring unto thee the forces of the Gentiles, and that their kings may be brought.” Forces means wealth, and their kings are brought in chains. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish”.

“And they shall bring the glory and honour of the nations into it. And there shall in no wise enter into it any thing that defileth, neither whatsoever worketh abomination, or maketh a lie: but they which are written in the Lamb’s book of life.” So the nations themselves are not walking in. They are bringing their glory and honour up to the men of God at the gates. Those written in the Lamb's book of life are the Israelites. Only the Israelites get in.

When Revelation says “the nations of them which are saved”, Zechariah gives the thought: “And it shall come to pass, that every one that is left of all the nations which came against Jerusalem shall even go up from year to year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to keep the feast of tabernacles.”

Everyone that is left. Christ is not killing everybody. There are going to be remnants of people left over from the nations that came against Jerusalem. Those are the “saved” of Revelation 21: the ones left.

And what they do is go up every year to worship the King and keep the feast of tabernacles. That is walking in the light of it: obeying the commandments. That is how the nations serve in Isaiah 60, bringing their wealth and their kings to the gates while Israel is inside. “For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish; yea, those nations shall be utterly wasted.”

The iniquity visited upon the children in Exodus 34:7 is the same sin carried from generation to generation, and covetousness is one of them. “Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s house, thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant, nor his ox, nor his ass, nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.”

To covet means to take what does not belong to you: to take it by wickedness, by deceit. The same BS we were doing back then, we still do today, coveting our neighbour's house and our neighbour's wife.

Then, “nor his ox”: hold it right there. That points to Exodus 22, the same chapter Negroes use to beguile you sisters. The whole of that chapter is about thou shalt not covet. Then, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s”: you are not supposed to covet, to take, anything that belongs to that father, that neighbour.

So the iniquity of the fathers that is still being visited on us is the same covetousness, and we should learn not to carry that evil all the way up to now.

Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will “by no means clear the guilty; visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children, and upon the children’s children, unto the third and to the fourth generation.” Exodus 20:5 shows who that is spoken of: “Thou shalt not bow down thyself to them, nor serve them: for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation of them that hate me.”

Of them that hate me. To disobey God's commandments is to demonstrate that you hate God. He pardons iniquity and transgression and sin, but if we are guilty of breaking his laws, we are going to pay.

That is why this is read in the wilderness, right after the commandments and statutes were given. A lot of us did not learn from the mistakes we made back then. We came back and did the same damn thing, still wicked and evil and covetous to this day, and the Most High is going to keep sending those afflictions until the lesson is learned. Read the book of your fathers to find out what we did and why all this hell is on us, and you will know what not to do today.

Exodus 22 is the law put in place for those that wanted to do evil, and it is proper. The whole chapter is about putting restraints on covetousness. It is not telling you how you are supposed to move. It is like a speeding ticket: your insurance goes way up, and that is the consequence of breaking the original law. Drive the damn speed limit.

“If a man shall steal an ox, or a sheep, and kill it, or sell it; he shall restore five oxen for an ox, and four sheep for a sheep.” That is covetousness: you coveted thy neighbour's ox, exactly what Exodus 20:17 forbids. If you do, you pay for the one you stole and give him five oxen for it.

“And if a man entice a maid that is not betrothed, and lie with her, he shall surely endow her to be his wife.” The maid belongs to her father. To entice her means you coveted to get her; you did it behind the father's back, in deceit. You broke the tenth commandment, “nor any thing that is thy neighbour’s.” You lured her away from her father, and you are going to try to tell me that is righteous? You are a damn fool. And a woman that has no wisdom will follow that and pay for the judgment.

Verse 17 kills it: “If her father utterly refuse to give her unto him, he shall pay money according to the dowry of virgins.” The father said hell no. Even though you enticed her, you are not taking her. That is what happened with Dinah: she was enticed, spoken to sweetly and kindly; she was not raped. Even though he wanted to marry her, her brothers said no, snatched her out of that house, and she had to sit there defiled.

That should be a warning to you women. No backdoor marriages will be approved, period. If we have to snatch you out, and you have to sit with that scarlet letter knowing you were defiled, that is better than being tied up with somebody that means you pure evil. How could you even respect a man who went behind your father's back, your protection's back? This is the guilty that Exodus 34:7 says the Lord will by no means clear.
