The word of the Lord told Ezekiel, “Son of man, set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it”. To know who Mount Seir is, go to Genesis 36. Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, his cattle and all his substance “and went into the country from the face of his brother Jacob”, because “the land wherein they were strangers could not bear them because of their cattle.” “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.”

So prophesying against Mount Seir is prophesying against Edom. Mount Seir today is called Petra. The Arabs, the Nabataeans, took it over around the third or fourth century, but the scripture is speaking of Esau. Ezekiel 35 is not a prophecy against the Arabs; the whole chapter is about Esau.

Now the chapter reads plainly. God says he will make Mount Seir “most desolate”, “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred, and hast shed the blood of the children of Israel by the force of the sword in the time of their calamity, in the time that their iniquity had an end”. Any time our iniquity came to an end and we thought we would be all right, Esau came behind. When the Emancipation Proclamation said we were free and we started to build, Esau terrorized us with the Ku Klux Klan, Jim Crow and the black codes. They bombed our homes, flooded them, took our properties and live in them today. They tell us to go back to Africa while they rob Africa, yet in World War II they made laws forbidding blacks to fly to Ethiopia to help fight Mussolini. They do not really want us to leave.

“I will prepare thee unto blood, and blood shall pursue thee: sith thou hast not hated blood”. Esau is a bloody race, going back to the red pottage of raw meat he begged Jacob for. God will fill his mountains with his slain men and make him “perpetual desolations, and thy cities shall not return”. Their cities are still here today, so this destruction of Edom has not happened yet.

“Because thou hast said, These two nations and these two countries shall be mine, and we will possess it; whereas the Lord was there”. The two nations are the kingdom of Judah and the kingdom of Israel. The two countries are the land of Israel and North America. Edom took the Americas in 1776 as Christians, calling themselves the anointed of God, and took the land of Israel in 1948 as Jews, calling themselves the praise of God, which is what Judah means. That is why God says to the wicked, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” and Malachi calls Edom “The border of wickedness” and “The people against whom the Lord hath indignation for ever.”

“And all the people that were left of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites, which were not of the children of Israel, Their children that were left after them in the land, whom the children of Israel also were not able utterly to destroy, upon those did Solomon levy a tribute of bondservice unto this day.”

They were our servants, our slaves. The Jebusites left in the land did not rule over Israel; Solomon put them under a tribute of bondservice.

So when we go back to the last part of Zechariah 9:7, “and Ekron as a Jebusite”, it means they are going to be our servants. Those that are left of the Philistines will be to Israel what the Jebusites were to David and Solomon, while he that remaineth of Israel “shall be as a governor in Judah.” The pride of the Philistines is cut off, and the order is turned back the way God set it.

“The burden of the word of the Lord in the land of Hadrach, and Damascus shall be the rest thereof”: this is Syria. And it comes “when the eyes of man, as of all the tribes of Israel, shall be toward the Lord.” All the eyes of Israel, our people, shall be toward the Lord.

2 Chronicles 20:12 has the wording for it: “O our God, wilt thou not judge them? for we have no might against this great company that cometh against us; neither know we what to do: but our eyes are upon thee.” That is what we are saying to the Lord.

The nations are at war around Syria, Lebanon, Gaza and Ashkelon, and we have no might against that great company. We do not know what to do. So we keep our eyes on the Lord, and we have to put our attention toward him. That is the moment Zechariah is speaking of, when the burden of the Lord falls on those lands and all the tribes of Israel look to him.

Zechariah 9:7 ends: “but he that remaineth, even he, shall be for our God, and he shall be as a governor in Judah, and Ekron as a Jebusite.” He that remaineth is you and I. And on the map, Ekron sits right there above Jerusalem.

What does it mean to be as a Jebusite? “And David said on that day, Whosoever getteth up to the gutter, and smiteth the Jebusites, and the lame and the blind, that are hated of David’s soul, he shall be chief and captain. Wherefore they said, The blind and the lame shall not come into the house. So David dwelt in the fort, and called it the city of David.”

When you read the history, David smote the Jebusites and made them servants. That is what he did. So when Zechariah says “Ekron as a Jebusite”, the land that the Philistines hold will be brought under Israel the way David brought the Jebusites under him.

Zechariah 9:8: “And I will encamp about mine house because of the army, because of him that passeth by, and because of him that returneth: and no oppressor shall pass through them any more: for now have I seen with mine eyes.” No oppressor shall oppress us any more; they will not pass through.

And “now have I seen with mine eyes” is the same as Exodus 2:25: “And God looked upon the children of Israel, and God had respect unto them.” In Egypt God looked upon Israel under their oppressors and had respect unto them, and then he brought them out.

So when he says now have I seen with mine eyes, he is looking upon us to have respect unto us. The Lord encamps about his house, the oppressor is stopped, and right after it Zechariah says “Rejoice greatly, O daughter of Zion”, because the King comes.

Zechariah 9:7 says “And I will take away his blood out of his mouth, and his abominations from between his teeth”. First the scripture about blood: “whatsoever man there be of the house of Israel, or of the strangers that sojourn among you, that eateth any manner of blood; I will even set my face against that soul that eateth blood, and will cut him off from among his people. For the life of the flesh is in the blood”.

“Therefore I said unto the children of Israel, No soul of you shall eat blood”. Whoever hunts and catches a beast or fowl “shall even pour out the blood thereof, and cover it with dust.” “Ye shall eat the blood of no manner of flesh: for the life of all flesh is the blood thereof: whosoever eateth it shall be cut off.” That includes those of you who came from Santo Domingo: you are not to be eating blood sausage, black sausage. Don't eat that.

Now look at the blood in his mouth and the abomination between his teeth. These people, these bastards in Ashdod, in the ritual they call metzitzah b'peh, remove the foreskin of the baby and put their mouth on the wound and suck the blood from it. Infants have caught herpes from it, and the rabbis in New York negotiate to keep doing it. That is an abomination from between your teeth. What the hell is wrong with you? Your mom ain't teach you nothing?

One man called them a militarized vampire nation, living on death and destruction, on blood. Ezekiel 35:5-6 says it of Esau: because thou hast had a perpetual hatred and shed the blood of the children of Israel, “sith thou hast not hated blood, even blood shall pursue thee.” The Most High is exposing them: the bloody mattress and baby clothes in the tunnels in Brooklyn, the baby clothes and toys on Epstein Island. God will take away the blood out of his mouth.
blog/2026/2026-04-03-2026-04-03-edom-the:
Esau left Canaan because his riches and cattle were too great for him and Jacob to dwell together, and the land did not belong to him. “Thus dwelt Esau in mount Seir: Esau is Edom.” But Genesis 14:6 had already shown that the Horites dwelt in Mount Seir. So what became of them?

Genesis 36 lists the dukes of Esau's sons, the high titles: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz, Korah, Gatam and Amalek, all of Eliphaz, Esau's firstborn by Adah. Remember these dukes, because they are all around today under various names like German, Israeli and Polish. Then comes a surprise: “These are the sons of Seir the Horite, who inhabited the land; Lotan, and Shobal, and Zibeon, and Anah,” “And Dishon, and Ezer, and Dishan: these are the dukes of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.” Seir the Horite was a Hamite, and the Horites had dukes first. That is where Esau learned about dukes: he got among them, took their title and took their land.

This is where Christ pulled the parable from. The law says, “when ye shall come into the land, and shall have planted all manner of trees for food”, fig trees included, “then ye shall count the fruit thereof as uncircumcised: three years shall it be as uncircumcised unto you: it shall not be eaten of.” Uncircumcised means unclean, not ready. For three years the fruit is not fit to be eaten.

“But in the fourth year all the fruit thereof shall be holy to praise the Lord withal.” That lines up with the dresser of the vineyard: after three years with no fruit, he asks the lord, “let it alone this year also, till I shall dig about it, and dung it”. After the third year, the fourth year may start bringing forth fruit. “And in the fifth year shall ye eat of the fruit thereof, that it may yield unto you the increase thereof: I am the Lord your God.” Now it is edible.

So growth is a process. It takes time before fruit becomes presentable, suitable for use, whether a fig tree, an apple tree, an orange tree or a peach tree. And it has to be dug about and given dung, its fertilizer. It has to be nourished, like soil that takes in the nutrients of the earth to produce fruit. Digging and dunging is teaching: when you apply what is given to you in class, you are that soil taking in the nutrients, and you start to grow and bring forth fruit.

We are a work in progress. You don’t become whole right away; repairing yourself and humbling yourself takes time, so we set things up for you to get better. But pride goeth before the fall. Refuse the fertilizer, say you don’t need it, and the Most High will uproot you and throw you into the fire. That is the lot of the plant that refuses to grow: “if it bear fruit, well: and if not, then after that thou shalt cut it down.”

Psalms 51:16: “For thou desirest not sacrifice; else would I give it: thou delightest not in burnt offering.” David is saying, you don’t desire sacrifice, otherwise I would give it to you; you don’t care about that either. The Lord revealed to David, I don’t care about sacrifices. And Saul didn’t listen either.

“And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord?” Samuel is asking the question: does the Lord require sacrifices above obeying what he tells you to do?

“Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.” To hearken is to listen and humble yourself. That is better than the fat of rams.

So “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit: a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” The sacrifice God accepts is a broken spirit. The animals were just temporary; your mind being broken and humbled is the best sacrifice the Lord desires. You can offer and sacrifice all you want, but make sure you offer with a good heart. “Then shalt thou be pleased with the sacrifices of righteousness, with burnt offering and whole burnt offering: then shall they offer bullocks upon thine altar.” Once the sacrifices of righteousness are offered, then the bullocks on the altar become acceptable.

Psalms 51:17 says “a broken and a contrite heart, O God, thou wilt not despise.” Ecclesiasticus 35:17 shows what happens when the humbled one prays.

“The prayer of the humble pierceth the clouds.” It pierces the clouds: the Lord hears it. “And till it come nigh, he will not be comforted; and will not depart, till the most High shall behold to judge righteously, and execute judgment.”

That is David in Psalms 51. When Nathan confronted him after Bathsheba and Uriah, he did not stay the smartest guy in the room. He said, you are right, I am guilty: “For I acknowledge my transgressions: and my sin is ever before me.” He kept the promise he made in Psalms 32:5, “I acknowledged my sin unto thee, and mine iniquity have I not hid.” He held himself accountable, and you have to hold yourself accountable when it comes to your sins.

The bones that were broken were his humbling: being confronted with his wrong, confessing it and acknowledging it, and the consequences that followed. And out of that broken, humbled place he prayed, “Create in me a clean heart, O God; and renew a right spirit within me.” That is the prayer of the humble, the one that pierces the clouds, and it is the same humility that brought mercy to King Manasseh.

Deuteronomy 28:15 says that if we will not hearken unto the voice of the Lord to do all his commandments and his statutes, “all these curses shall come upon thee, and overtake thee”. Verse 27 names one of them: “The Lord will smite thee with the botch of Egypt”. Then verse 60: “Moreover he will bring upon thee all the diseases of Egypt, which thou wast afraid of; and they shall cleave unto thee.”

That is what we need to see. The curses of Deuteronomy 28 did not just come out of nowhere. A lot of them are the same curses that were on us in ancient Egypt: the botch of Egypt, the diseases of Egypt, the oppression of Egypt. God said in Exodus 3:9, “I have also seen the oppression wherewith the Egyptians oppress them.” Our forefathers were oppressed in ancient Egypt, and they were oppressed here in America, and are still being oppressed here. The oppression is real.

So when the scripture calls America spiritually Egypt, it is because the same things that happened to us in ancient Egypt happened to us here, and the curses show it. The diseases of Egypt cleave unto us in this land, along with the rest: we grope at noonday, we do not prosper in our ways, and as a nation of people we are only oppressed and spoiled evermore.

Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships, by the way whereof I spake unto thee, Thou shalt see it no more again”. Moses is being very specific, and Exodus 14:13 explains it. At the Red Sea he told the people: “Fear ye not, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will shew to you to day: for the Egyptians whom ye have seen to day, ye shall see them again no more for ever.”

The scripture already said we would never see those Egyptians again, for ever. So when Moses says we will go into Egypt a second time, the Egypt he is speaking of cannot be ancient Egypt. The people would have said, Egypt again? We are going back to Egypt a second time? And he explains: I am not talking about the Egypt you just came out of. The way whereof I speak unto thee, thou shalt see it no more again. It is a different Egypt.

And this time we go into it with ships. Moses saw the end. The Lord showed him the Israelites thrown on cargo slave ships and brought here to America: the transatlantic slave trade. Egypt, from the Hebrew Mizraim, means shut in, restraint, misery, tribulation, distress. So going into Egypt again means going into captivity, misery and tribulation again, carried there on ships, sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen. That is why Revelation 11:8 calls the great city, Mystery Babylon, America, spiritually Egypt.

Christ has the power over life and death, which is why Daniel 12 says some shall awake. “And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.”

Many of them are going to awake. Some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt. When you die, you go to sleep, yes. But Christ has the power to wake your behind up and torment you.

That is what stands behind the carcases of Isaiah 66:24, whose worm does not die and whose fire is not quenched, and behind the land of Deuteronomy 29 that is all brimstone, salt and burning. Those who forsook the covenant of the Lord God of their fathers and served other gods do not simply die and disappear: they are awakened to shame and everlasting contempt. As 2 Esdras 9 says, read in the same moment, those who despised his law while the place of repentance was open “must know it after death by pain.” And the righteous awake to everlasting life, the seed and the name that remain.

Deuteronomy 29:22 speaks of “the generation to come of your children that shall rise up after you”. Who is that? Isaiah 66 shows it: “For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith the Lord, so shall your seed and your name remain.” The seed and the name that remain in the new heaven and new earth are the righteous of our people that make it, those of us that get the kingdom.

“And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith the Lord.” After they come up to worship, “they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me”. Go forth where? To look on this place, America. That is the same moment Deuteronomy 29 describes, when the generation to come and the stranger from a far land see the plagues of that land, “brimstone, and salt, and burning”, and ask, “Wherefore hath the Lord done thus unto this land?”

After somebody dies, their carcase is supposed to just disappear. So this is letting you know it is something spiritual. “for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.” They are in damnation, cast in hell, being tormented. That is why Deuteronomy 29 says the Lord will separate the man that did not repent unto evil.

There is a place of torment, and it will be set up when Christ returns. After this place is destroyed physically, a spiritual prison and damnation will be set up here, the place of torment for the devils that said, have you come to torment us before our time. Christ has the power over hell and death: he can give you life and immortality, or wake you up and torment you.

In Deuteronomy 31 Moses says, “For I know that after my death ye will utterly corrupt yourselves”, and “evil will befall you in the latter days”. How is Moses able to say I know? Deuteronomy 4 shows what he saw.

“I call heaven and earth to witness against you this day, that ye shall soon utterly perish from off the land whereunto ye go over Jordan to possess it; ye shall not prolong your days upon it, but shall utterly be destroyed.” When we went into the land of Israel, our days were not going to be prolonged in it; we were going to be destroyed from off that land. “And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you.” Moses saw the Israelites being scattered throughout the four corners of the earth.

He could see it because God showed it to him. In 2 Esdras 14, read right after, the Lord says, “In the bush I did manifestly reveal myself unto Moses, and talked with him, when my people served in Egypt”, and he held him on the mount a long season, the forty days and forty nights, and “shewed him the secrets of the times, and the end”. Moses saw the secrets of the beginning, which is how he wrote Genesis, and he saw the end.

So Moses saw what would happen to us in the time of the Babylonians, the Greeks and the Romans, and he saw us here in America, in the transatlantic slave trade, and America being destroyed. That is why he could say with certainty that evil would befall us in the latter days: he had already seen it.

Pharaoh told the Hebrew midwives, “if it be a son, then ye shall kill him”. Where is that in Deuteronomy? “Cursed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land”. What is the fruit of our body? Our children. That is why it says our children are going to be cursed.

In ancient Egypt, when the baby came out, Pharaoh commanded the midwives to kill it if it was a male. That is oppression. Today they do the same thing, and it is called abortion.

And how do they get rid of the males today? The school to prison pipeline. They create conditions for our people to live in poverty, bring drugs into the community, and when the brothers are out there selling, they put them away for the rest of their lives. That whole system was set up by Esau. That is them dealing wisely, “let us deal wisely with them.” And through the vaccines: when you look at the rate of autism in young black and Hispanic men, it is very high. They put things in the vaccines to mess with the babies' minds. But Esau has been mixing with us, so some of our DNA is in theirs, and now white people complain that their kids are coming out with autism too.

It goes back to the scripture that says they try to destroy the poor secretly. Secretly they try to kill every male child amongst us, because they are trying to stop the prophets from coming on the earth. What Pharaoh did in ancient Egypt, America is doing in spiritual Egypt.

Exodus 1:14 says “they made their lives bitter with hard bondage, in morter, and in brick, and in all manner of service in the field”. We were in the fields in ancient Egypt; we were not just building pyramids. They had us doing plantation work and cropping there too. Deuteronomy 28:16 is that curse: “Cursed shalt thou be in the city, and cursed shalt thou be in the field.”

The same way ancient Egypt made us slaves and worked us in the fields with all manner of service, in America that curse also fell upon us. We were cursed in the cotton field, in the sugar cane field, in the tobacco field, with five year olds and two year olds picking cotton. Our lives were made bitter, and that is why we eat the bitter herbs at Passover: they represent our lives being bitter in Egypt.

And all manner of service: we were their servants, cooking their food, watching their kids, entertaining them. Sing, this Hebrew got a good voice, sing me one of the songs of Zion. That is what we do here in Babylon. Some of you drive a bus, fix the road, drive a taxi cab: servant jobs, and you don't see it. We have been slaves so long we got comfortable with the jobs they give us. We are kings and priests; we are not supposed to serve any nation. Our job is to serve God.

Read the curses of Deuteronomy 28 and then read what happened to us in ancient Egypt, and you will see they are the same. America is spiritual Egypt.

“And they built for Pharaoh treasure cities, Pithom and Raamses.” We built cities in ancient Egypt, and it is the same thing here in America. Deuteronomy 28:30 lists it among the curses: “Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her: thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein: thou shalt plant a vineyard, and shalt not gather the grapes thereof.”

In ancient Egypt we built cities and houses, and we did not build them for ourselves; we built them for the Egyptians. We were a commodity, and they did not look at us as human. America did the same.

What house did we build here in America and could not dwell in it? The White House. Construction began in 1792 in Washington D.C., and hundreds of enslaved people rented from plantation owners quarried the stone, cut the timber and laid the bricks, dawn to dusk, with no wages, whipped if they slowed down. Most are not even named in the records, just negro hired. When it was finished in 1800 and President Adams moved in, the enslaved workers were sent back to the plantations with no credit and no freedom, and for the next 65 years more enslaved people worked there. Some of you thought the white man built that.

We built cities in Egypt and did not dwell in them, and we built the White House and cannot dwell in it. The same curse, in ancient Egypt and in spiritual Egypt.

Exodus 1:11 says “they did set over them taskmasters to afflict them with their burdens.” Deuteronomy 28 names that as a curse: “The stranger that is within thee shall get up above thee very high; and thou shalt come down very low. He shall lend to thee, and thou shalt not lend to him: he shall be the head, and thou shalt be the tail.”

The strangers are the people that were amongst us. They get above us very high, and we come down very low. To be above us means they rule and tell us what to do, and another name for that is taskmaster.

That curse was on us in ancient Egypt: the Egyptians were over us, and we were on the bottom of society. It is the same way the so-called white man and the nations are above us today, and we are the bottom of society. The taskmasters today are the governors, the politicians, the police officers, the FBI agents, people set to keep us in check and keep us in order, with laws like Jim Crow and the black codes to keep us low. On the cotton field there was always a white overseer to make sure we did the work, or you got your ass whooped. Today your taskmaster is your boss.

What was done to us in ancient Egypt is what was done to us in America. That is why this place is spiritually called Egypt.

Exodus 1:12 says “the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and grew. And they were grieved because of the children of Israel.” No matter how much they afflicted us, we kept multiplying and growing. And what does it mean that the Egyptians were grieved because of us? They were mad; they were angry.

Exodus 12:15 says, “even the first day ye shall put away leaven out of your houses”. That is purging the old leaven. We had to do it physically, but it is something spiritual today. So what is your house today? “Know ye not that ye are the temple of God, and that the Spirit of God dwelleth in you?” You, me, we are the temple of God, and the Spirit of God is to dwell in us because our temple was destroyed.

“If any man defile the temple of God, him shall God destroy; for the temple of God is holy, which temple ye are.” You will pull this out on a brother in the street: brother, you got tattoos, you got the devil on you, you are defiling your temple. We know tattoos are wrong. But meanwhile you have a whole yeast factory in your spirit. If you are out there with the leaven of bitterness in your spirit, you are out of order too, and you will be destroyed just like that brother if he and you do not repent.

Some brothers say, I am going to tuck mine in, tuck away my hatred and my bitterness and save it for later. Paul answers that: “What? know ye not that your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you, which ye have of God, and ye are not your own?”

We are not our own. So when we hide hatred, bitterness, malice, whatever sins we deal with, we are throwing that back in Christ's face. He is our Passover, our sacrifice; he bought us back, twice he bought us back. So we do not own our bodies to even have the angle to defile our temple. When a brother lends you something, you are supposed to take extra care of it. Christ gave us our bodies and bought us back again, and we need to keep them like brand new.

“For ye are bought with a price”: with Christ's blood. Then, “therefore glorify God in your body, and in your spirit, which are God’s.” We have to use our bodies to glorify him in every way possible, and our spirit too, because both belong to God. When we hold back malice, hatred for our brothers or hatred for our wife, we put that on Christ, and it is not of the Lord. We have to let go of that spirit.

That is the leaven Exodus 12:15 says to put out of your house: not only the yeast on the box, but the bitterness tucked in when Bishop comes around and let out again when he leaves.

Exodus 12:15 says, “whosoever eateth leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.” What is that really saying? How do we eat the leaven today? A dumb thought jumps into your mind and you say, damn, I don't like that brother. You are spiritually consuming it, entertaining sin and not purging the leaven from your house. That is how you get cut off from your people, and this is a serious thing.

How you get cut off: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.” Christ is our Passover, who set the example. That is the gift, the promise made to Abraham, for us to get repentance for sins, because we are in a wicked place.

And Exodus 13:7 says “there shall no leavened bread be seen with thee, neither shall there be leaven seen with thee in all thy quarters.” We do not want to be seen in the midst of sin, Passover or not. Don't be the brother who does not throw the bread out but puts it in his storage closet and brings it back when Passover is over: laying the bitterness aside for the season and picking right back up hating the brother. That is not the spirit. Throw it out. Let it go.

“And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing wherewith his father blessed him: and Esau said in his heart, The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” That is the bitterness, and it plans over a process of time. It is the same thing we read in Genesis 4: Cain slew Abel, and Esau wanted to kill Jacob. Cain was the firstborn and Esau was the firstborn. Same spirit.

To see how someone can hold bitterness, hatred and malice toward you and hide it completely, look at Genesis 33, long after Esau said he hated his brother: “And Esau ran to meet him, and embraced him, and fell on his neck, and kissed him: and they wept.” Someone who hates you can play the long game. He can pretend to be your friend and on your side while he waits for the moment to hit you at your worst. They call them liberals today. That's the liberal for you: oh, we love you niggers, I mean black people. Jacob knew Esau's heart. That is why he sent the gifts ahead: he thought Esau might be coming to kill him.

Hebrews explains what was working in Esau: “Looking diligently lest any man fail of the grace of God; lest any root of bitterness springing up trouble you, and thereby many be defiled”. Looking diligently means looking within yourself. The root of bitterness is a hidden sin under the ground that nobody sees, but over time it springs up and troubles you. It distorts your thoughts and your perception, so that things you once saw clearly, with eyes anointed with eye salve, are no longer pure to you.

“Lest there be any fornicator, or profane person, as Esau, who for one morsel of meat sold his birthright.” Profane means devoted to what is not sacred, secular rather than religious: Esau was a carnal man, a man of the field, whose religion is sin. When we follow the carnal ways of Esau, we throw away our birthright, the kingdom of heaven. Hebrews says “for he found no place of repentance, though he sought it carefully with tears.” Hold on to a bitter spirit and you are a spiritual Edomite, and you will find the same place of no repentance on that day.

An officer drew the parallel: “He that committeth sin is of the devil; for the devil sinneth from the beginning.” Christ came “that he might destroy the works of the devil”, so we cannot move in the devil's spirit and think we move in Christ's. Whoever does not love his brother is not of God. If there is an offense, deal with it by Matthew 18:15, not by sowing discord in the congregation. “For to be carnally minded is death; but to be spiritually minded is life and peace.” The spiritually minded man seeks to gain his brother, not keep him as a rival to get back at, “Because the carnal mind is enmity against God: for it is not subject to the law of God”.

Esau cried, “Is not he rightly named Jacob? for he hath supplanted me these two times: he took away my birthright; and, behold, now he hath taken away my blessing.” Is that true? Go back to Genesis 25. Esau came from the field faint and said, “Feed me, I pray thee, with that same red pottage”. “And Jacob said, Sell me this day thy birthright.” There was no trickery. Jacob asked him straight, and it was up to Esau to say no. Esau said, “what profit shall this birthright do to me?” Jacob made him swear, because the word of that man is no good, just as with the four hundred and some treaties they broke. Scripture sums it up: “thus Esau despised his birthright.”

So Esau was lying and playing the victim. The Psalm describes it: “Thou givest thy mouth to evil, and thy tongue frameth deceit.” “Thou sittest and speakest against thy brother; thou slanderest thine own mother’s son.” Did we not just read the slander? He tricked me two times. Nowhere does scripture show Jacob dealing with deceit over the birthright. They were liars from the beginning, because they moved in the same spirit as their father Cain, who was of the wicked one.

It is how they do today: throw the rock, hide the hand, and as soon as the other side hits back, run to the UN as the victim. Now all of a sudden he cares about the birthright, just as his children want to stand in our place claiming to be the Jews and the people of the book. Where was that energy when he threw it away for something to eat, or today for money and fame?

You got the children of God and you got the children of the devil; there is no in between. You either got the godly mind or the Edomite mind. The same Psalm says to the wicked, the white man, “What hast thou to do to declare my statutes, or that thou shouldest take my covenant in thy mouth?” “Seeing thou hatest instruction, and castest my words behind thee.” They say in God we trust and swear on the Bible while doing nothing the scripture says.

Esau “lifted up his voice, and wept”, but that was worldly sorrow. “For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.” We must come to the Lord sincerely, because of those who wait, God says, “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer; they shall seek me early, but they shall not find me:” “For that they hated knowledge, and did not choose the fear of the Lord”. “Therefore shall they eat of the fruit of their own way”. We all have to examine ourselves so we are not moving in that same spirit.

“Let us not be desirous of vain glory, provoking one another, envying one another.” Cain wanted to be the man; that is vain glory.

Provoking one another means agitating a brother to play him out of position, because you are envious of him. You do something to provoke him to evil so you can justify your position against him.

We see this even in marriage. A brother provokes his wife, she leaves the house and does something foolish, and he sits back saying, I told you the sister was off, I told you she was evil. No, brother: you are the evil one, you provoked your wife. We are not going for that foolishness here. Envy provokes, and provoking is how the bitter spirit sets up its victim.

“For where envying and strife is, there is confusion and every evil work.” Genesis 4 is an account of envying and strife. Cain was not doing right, he saw Abel doing right, and that built envy, the same spirit that shows up later between Esau and Jacob. It was there from the beginning.

Then comes confusion. All of a sudden Cain did not know right from wrong, and every evil work followed: he slew his brother. When you are confused, saying, I do not know where this is coming from, every evil work will be the result.

Confusion is Satan's playground. Satan loves us operating in confusion. That is why his children throw every kind of confusion into the media and everywhere they go, and why leaders of other nations have said they do not want that American media in their countries. They know every evil work hides behind that cloud of confusion.

Bitterness does not travel alone. Envy, pride, hatred and evil suspicion come bundled together like a cable TV package. Solomon names one: “Only by pride cometh contention”.

Cain was contending because pride was on him. Cain's attitude was: I am not going to make it right with my brother; my brother is the one who is off; in fact, I have to put him to death, because he is making me look bad. That is pride. Cain did not want to take the correction.

Then: “but with the well advised is wisdom.” The well advised are the ones who do well, like Abel. Wisdom says, let me get my spirit right; I cannot have an evil eye toward my brother. When correction comes, pride contends with it, while wisdom takes it and makes things right with the brother.

Cain was born first, just like Esau. “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground”, a man of the field, which already tells you what is going on. “And in process of time it came to pass, that Cain brought of the fruit of the ground an offering unto the Lord.” Cain already knew right from wrong, because his father taught him animal sacrifice, but over a process of time Cain turned evil and did not do what the Lord commanded.

Abel brought “of the firstlings of his flock and of the fat thereof. And the Lord had respect unto Abel and to his offering:” “But unto Cain and to his offering he had not respect. And Cain was very wroth, and his countenance fell.” His countenance fell because he was corrected. What really started all of this? Correction.

Solomon says, “Correction is grievous unto him that forsaketh the way”. Cain had forsaken the way over a process of time, so the correction was grievous to him. That grievous spirit nourished bitterness, and the bitterness grew until he murdered his brother. That is the spirit you are rolling in when you move with a bitter spirit.

Then: “and he that hateth reproof shall die”, because the wages of sin is death. Paul says, “For if we would judge ourselves, we should not be judged.” If we judged ourselves we would not have to be told about the bitterness, envy, hatred and malice inside us; when we refuse, the Lord has to bring the chastening. Cain refused to get himself right, and he became the father of wickedness.

“Cease from anger, and forsake wrath: fret not thyself in any wise to do evil.” That bitterness is the spirit of Cain, and in that wrath you might slay a brother, or in that bitterness you might betray one. None of us is above this. Do not sit in the congregation thinking so-and-so is getting cut with the scriptures; brother, that is you. Every lesson the leadership brings out is for us. The moment you think, I am not dealing with that, Satan already has you lined up and counts you on his team.

Go back to Genesis 4:8: “And Cain talked with Abel his brother”. This is the deception. Cain acted like his friend, talking with him over time about his flocks, until he could lure him out to the field: “when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him.” Solomon describes that man: “He that hateth dissembleth with his lips, and layeth up deceit within him;” “When he speaketh fair, believe him not: for there are seven abominations in his heart.” Murder, envy, pride and covetousness are all in there. “Whose hatred is covered by deceit, his wickedness shall be shewed before the whole congregation.” That is why it is called a root of bitterness: roots are covered by soil where nobody can see them, but the Lord always brings it to the surface. “Whoso diggeth a pit shall fall therein”, and “a flattering mouth worketh ruin.”

John names the spirit: “Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.” Cain was the first recorded hater in the scriptures, and he came back as Esau. The scribes and Pharisees were bitter toward Christ and wanted him dead; carry an evil eye toward your brother and you are in the same spirit. “We know that we have passed from death unto life, because we love the brethren. He that loveth not his brother abideth in death.” “Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer”. And Sirach warns, “When the ungodly curseth Satan, he curseth his own soul.” Brothers say, the white man is the devil, they are going to be destroyed, they are going into captivity, and then carry hatred toward their own brother, moving in the same spirit.

“Be not hasty in thy spirit to be angry: for anger resteth in the bosom of fools.” Bitterness is a progression: it starts with a correction or an offense, then pride comes in and you will not speak to the brother, then when you do speak it is in deceit, masking envy, anger and hatred, and in the end it destroys you and those around you. “A little leaven leaveneth the whole lump”: a little bitterness defiles the whole soul. Christ said, “Beware ye of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy.” “For there is nothing covered, that shall not be revealed”. Leaven looks flat at first and grows as it bakes, so do not let the hate bake. Deal with your brother and sister uprightly according to the laws of God before it festers and overcomes you.

What is bitterness? It is sin. “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me, and by it slew me.” Taking occasion by the commandment means you can only recognize sin through the commandments of God. How do you know you are in the middle of sin? The law says you shall not hate your brother in your heart, and when you meditate on it you realize, I have an evil spirit toward that brother. The law brings it to the surface.

Sin “deceived me”: you did not know bitterness was a sin, because you were deceived. But the law gives clarity. Like fog lights, it pierces the cloud of confusion. That is why the law is called a light: so you can see through the nonsense your mind was thinking.

Then sin “by it slew me.” When the scripture comes out, you feel cut, because you are no longer deceived and can see clearly. What you see on the other side of the fog is yourself in the mirror of the Bible, realizing how evil you were. Some people do not like the light and love to walk in darkness, saying, do not call that out, that is not me; brothers wearing purple and gold, a ribbon of blue and fringes, who are only blue ribbon Christians. We do not want to be those night walkers.

It was the Most High God who called you, not the bishop, deacon or captain, and once hands are laid on you, you are sent away. When the phone call comes to travel, we do not want to hear anything from you but yes. Paul travelled, departing unto Seleucia and sailing to Cyprus, and we continue the Acts of the Apostles, bringing the good news all over the world, whatever hate we get for it.

Moses charged the judges: “Ye shall not respect persons in judgment; but ye shall hear the small as well as the great”. You shall not have respect of persons in judgment; you cannot be partial. You have to hear both sides, the small as well as the great. That is the qualification of a judge, and if you are not ready for it, do not accept the position.

James speaks of the same thing: “My brethren, have not the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Lord of glory, with respect of persons.” Here is respect of persons, and James sets it against the faith of Christ itself. You cannot hold the faith of the Lord of glory and at the same time judge one brother by a different measure than another.

“ye shall not be afraid of the face of man”. You are not here to be loved or to be liked; you are judges. Some are afraid to make a decision because of what men will think of them, and some get offended when judgment falls on their friend, even without knowing what happened. What does that have to do with you? The judgment is God's, and a judge in Israel must be just, not partial.

“Are ye not then partial in yourselves, and are become judges of evil thoughts?” Respect of persons goes into having a certain type of man in admiration over another: respecting one over another, preferring one over another, and it shows in how you deal with matters with that brother or those brothers. You are ready to have men's persons in admiration for advantage; there is something you are going to gain by showing favoritism.

And here is the end result: you “are become judges of evil thoughts”. Some brothers are horrible judges because there is something about the person they should judge that they can gain from them. Whether he gives you gifts, whether he is your ride to Sabbath, whether he got you a job, whatever the case may be, now you are partial in your judgment because of what that person can provide for you. The Lord says that is an evil, evil thing.

So you might think, I am just not going to judge because that is my friend. The Bible says you are evil. That is exactly what Moses forbade when he charged the judges to “judge righteously between every man and his brother, and the stranger that is with him.”

“But if ye have respect to persons, ye commit sin, and are convinced of the law as transgressors.” We always hear thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steal; we know those like the back of our hand. But if you have respect of persons, whether in judgment or in having men's persons in admiration for advantage, you commit sin. You are a transgressor, breaking the commandments of God.

You want to be in that position, but much is required of you in the position as judges. You must judge matters and deal righteously, because that is the law of God we just read in Deuteronomy: judge righteous judgment, whether it is your friend or not. In a position of leadership you cannot conceal your friend's folly; none of us should.

What has been discovered is that because someone is your friend, you do not want to speak out. You do not want to reveal the sin, as Leviticus 5:1 requires, and you do not want to be part of the judgment once the sin is revealed. You sit there quiet while the others bring out the transgressions, because you do not agree with the judgment God says to bring forth. Something is wrong with that. We have to stand on what God said. Anyone you consider a friend who goes against God and does not repent: I never knew you. Give us a little time and we will not even remember his name, because he chose wickedness and evil over the righteousness of God.

“Now the serpent was more subtil than any beast of the field which the Lord God had made.” The serpent is counted among the beasts, and in the scriptures the Most High compares men to beasts. Solomon wrote, “I said in mine heart concerning the estate of the sons of men, that God might manifest them, and that they might see that they themselves are beasts.” So the serpent in Genesis 3 is a representation of a man.

He was more subtle than any beast: more crafty, better with his lies, better with his persuasion. Satan’s first weapon was persuasion. Eve was not subdued physically; he did not grab her. He came to her with words. “Yea, hath God said, Ye shall not eat of every tree of the garden?” Notice what he brings: doubt and fear. Eve answered correctly, that God had said “Ye shall not eat of it, neither shall ye touch it, lest ye die.” Then came the doubt: “Ye shall not surely die,” and “ye shall be as gods, knowing good and evil.” She was already meant to be eternal, but he threw doubt in to persuade her to eat.

“she took of the fruit thereof, and did eat, and gave also unto her husband with her; and he did eat.” She was persuaded by the serpent, and then she defiled Adam as well. The serpent used no force; he used words to sway Eve’s perception of reality, and then she went into sin. He went to the woman first, which is why the woman is to learn from her husband at home.

That same serpent spirit is still speaking. Christ told the Pharisees, “Ye are of your father the devil,” “a liar, and the father of it.” The serpent seed came through Cain, and it lives on in Esau, the so-called white man, the pioneer of lying, who persuades the world today through his media and his religion. It is a battle for the minds of the people, and the answer is to stay in the word.

Genesis 5 traces the lineage from Adam down to Noah, who “begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.” Then Genesis 6 says “the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair.” The sons of God are that lineage just named; the daughters of men are the daughters of the other nations that were created. These are not literal angels. The chapter before gives the understanding, and the scriptures that follow prove who the sons of God are.

John writes it in the New Testament: “Behold, what manner of love the Father hath bestowed upon us, that we should be called the sons of God.” That is what God calls us. Brothers, you are walking gods, whoever gets upset about it, the apologists included.

“therefore the world knoweth us not, because it knew him not.” The world looks at our people, calls us Negroes, and refuses to believe these could be the people of the book, the sons of God. And it knew him not: to this day they refuse to say Christ was a black man. They put the image of Cesare Borgia in every church, comic book and piece of media, while the Bible says he is black, of the tribe of Judah.

So when Genesis 6 speaks of “the sons of God” going in to the daughters of men, it is speaking of the same people John calls the sons of God: Adam’s line, our forefathers.

Baruch says the same thing as Genesis 6: “There were the giants famous from the beginning, that were of so great stature, and so expert in war.” Those giants were the offspring of the sons of God, the mighty men of renown, and they were expert in war as well.

“Those did not the Lord choose, neither gave he the way of knowledge unto them.” God did not choose them; they were wicked. “But they were destroyed, because they had no wisdom, and perished through their own foolishness.” How were they destroyed? The flood. God saw that “every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually,” and he wiped it out.

But those same spirits came right back, by way of the three sons of Noah, Shem, Ham and Japheth. There is no new thing under the sun. Jude speaks of “certain men crept in unawares, who were before of old ordained to this condemnation,” the same words, “of old,” that Genesis 6 uses of the men of renown. The same kind of wickedness is still here, reserved “unto the judgment of the great day,” which has not yet come.

So the giants are not a fantasy of fallen angels, the Nephilim Esau talks about. They were men, the offspring of the sons of God, who had no wisdom, and whose spirit lives on until the judgment.

The sons of God in Genesis 6 are Adam’s line, the lineage traced in Genesis 5. Did that name change later, after the flood and after Egypt? No. Deuteronomy 14:1, spoken after the Exodus, says to Israel: “Ye are the children of the Lord your God.”

We are the children of the Lord our God because we are the sons of God. The same people carried the same title from Adam through Noah, through the fathers, out of Egypt, and into the law.

This matters for reading Genesis 6 rightly. The sons of God who went in to the daughters of men were not angels coming down from the sky; they were men of that same chosen line, God’s own children, who mixed with the other nations when it was forbidden. That sin brought the flood, and later the affliction of our people. The scriptures do not change the name: from Genesis, to Deuteronomy, to the prophets, to the New Testament, it is our people who are called the children and the sons of God.

The title “sons of God” runs through the whole book. After Deuteronomy called Israel “the children of the Lord your God,” did anything change in the prophets? No. Hosea 1:10: “Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered.”

“And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people.” That place is where our people are today: America and the diaspora, Jamaica, Haiti, Africa, Europe. Everywhere we were told we are not God’s people. “there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.”

God calls us the sons of the living God. That is who we are. So the sons of God of Genesis 6 are the same nation the prophet speaks of: the children of Israel, scattered and counted as nothing, yet still his sons. The world does not know us, but God does, and in the very place where we were called not his people, he will call us his sons again.

Genesis 6:4 says the children of the sons of God and the daughters of men “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and that “There were giants in the earth in those days.” Judith’s song names that kind of people: “For the mighty one did not fall by the young men, neither did the sons of the Titans smite him, nor high giants set upon him: but Judith the daughter of Merari weakened him with the beauty of her countenance.”

The sons of the Titans and the high giants are those giants, the men of renown of Genesis 6, the offspring of the sons of God.

That is where Esau gets his Titan movies, and his Greek mythology of Hercules and the half-gods. He always mixes some lies in with the truth. He tells those stories because he looks at us as gods: because of our DNA, our physical prowess, our melanin. We are the sons of God, demigods on the earth, and that is why when our people are put into sports or anything physical, we dominate. Everybody wants our rhythm, but nobody wants our blues.

So the Titans of the Greek stories are not fallen angels or gods of another people. They are a twisted memory of the mighty men born when the sons of God went in to the daughters of men.

“the sons of God saw the daughters of men” in Genesis 6 is about men, not spirits; God says “My spirit shall not always strive with man, for that he also is flesh.” Psalms 82:6 shows who these sons of God are and what God calls them: “I have said, Ye are gods; and all of you are children of the most High.”

We are gods, and we are children of the Most High. That is why the sons of God in Genesis 6 are called by that name: they carried that DNA, made in the image of God.

It is also why their sin was so serious. Back in Genesis 6:4, “There were giants in the earth in those days; and also after that, when the sons of God came in unto the daughters of men.” The sons of God, the children of the Most High, took wives of the other nations, which was forbidden. The children born to them “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown,” and “God saw that the wickedness of man was great in the earth, and that every imagination of the thoughts of his heart was only evil continually.” So the Most High brought destruction, and later we had to pay for what we did as the sons of God; he told Abraham his seed would be afflicted in a land not theirs for four hundred years.
blog/2026/2026-05-16-2026-05-16-the-bold:
Saul finally confessed in verse 24: “I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice.” If you are a leader and you are in fear of your people, or you don’t want them to be mad at you, what can those people do to you? Manipulate you. You are a pushover; they can sway you to the left and to the right. Who is supposed to move you? The Lord, not the people you are supposed to lead. You are not leading the people; you are being led by the people.

Then verse 28: “And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” Damn.

That is what the bashful spirit costs. Verse 23 already said it: “Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.” When you are in that spirit the Lord can’t use you; you are not a good leader. Leadership may see something in you and put you in a position, and then when we question you on certain things you make excuses, or you separate yourself into a bubble with the men under you. You are bashful, you are bringing up a bunch of bashful brothers under you, and you are keeping the brothers under you hostage.

The Lord had made Saul king “When thou wast little in thine own sight”, when he thought he was a nobody. And because he feared the people and would not obey, the kingdom was torn from him and given to his neighbour, David, who was better than he.

What is going on in 1 Samuel 15? The Lord commanded Saul to utterly destroy all the Amalekites and everything they have, every last one of them. The Lord told Saul, wipe these devils out. And he didn’t do it.

The commandment was total: “Now go and smite Amalek, and utterly destroy all that they have, and spare them not; but slay both man and woman, infant and suckling, ox and sheep, camel and ass.” All that they have. All means everything.

Now hold that against Saul’s answer in verse 20: “Yea, I have obeyed the voice of the Lord, and have gone the way which the Lord sent me, and have brought Agag the king of Amalek, and have utterly destroyed the Amalekites.” Wait a minute: the king is still alive. What do you mean you followed the commandment of the Lord? Saul is playing the defensive, justifying himself, making excuses.

Then verse 21: “But the people took of the spoil, sheep and oxen, the chief of the things which should have been utterly destroyed, to sacrifice unto the Lord thy God in Gilgal.” It wasn’t me, it was the people, it was their fault; I couldn’t do nothing about it. That is bashfulness: you don’t take accountability. The commandment said spare the sheep and oxen not, and Saul brought them back and blamed the people.

So Samuel answered, “to obey is better than sacrifice.” To do what you were told is better than coming back saying, my bad, I thought I understood what you wanted, I decided to do it this way. You fulfill the commandment you were given, and if there is a problem, you say something.

“For we walk by faith, not by sight.” Christians use that all the time and don’t know what it means. But in this aspect we can use it about fear.

We fear what we see. We don’t fear the Lord; we fear what we physically see. A brother at camp gets unruly with us, he’s got a gun or a knife or whatever, and we fear that. But we don’t fear breaking God’s commandments. That we don’t really fear.

That was Saul. When he “saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid.” He walked by sight. He feared the Philistines he could see and the people who were scattering from him, but he did not fear transgressing the commandment of the Lord, and it cost him the kingdom.

“For God hath not given us the spirit of fear.” The Bible says the Lord never gave us that spirit. So the fear Saul had when his heart greatly trembled goes back into a lack of faith.

“But of power, and of love, and of a sound mind.” We are supposed to have the spirit of power, love and a sound mind.

“Be not thou therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me his prisoner: but be thou partaker of the afflictions of the gospel according to the power of God.” We are not supposed to be ashamed of the testimony of Christ. The bashful brother is ashamed and afraid; the one who has God’s spirit partakes of the afflictions of the gospel by the power of God.

“And when Saul saw the host of the Philistines, he was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” He was scared. This is the king. If the king is scared, what is that going to do to the men under him? If the officer is fearful, what is that going to do to the soldiers under him? It is going to spread.

“As the judge of the people is himself, so are his officers”: so are they that are under him. “And what manner of man the ruler of the city is, such are all they that dwell therein.” Whatever man the ruler is, like King Saul, such are all that dwell under him.

Take an example. Some brothers have been here six months, a year maybe, not long, still in regular clothes. Some officers have been here eight, nine, ten years. Those young men in the regular shirts are going to follow the example of the officers in the purple shirts. So if you are bashful, afraid, timid and shy, what does that communicate to them spiritually? That they can be timid, shy, fearful and bashful too. You don’t have to say nothing; your spirit is telling them, it’s okay to be like this, the officer can be fearful and timid, so I’ll follow his example, now I know how to move around in here.

It shall not be so. It shall not be so in here.

“And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul.” This is the level we have to get to: where we are not afraid of those brothers and sisters, and the other nations, that can kill the body and have power over us in this society.

“But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” That is the Lord. We need to fear the Lord, the one who can kill body and soul in hell.

Saul feared the Philistines and feared the people, and not the Lord. So, back to 1 Samuel 28:6: “when Saul enquired of the Lord, the Lord answered him not, neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets.” The Lord was not dealing with Saul anymore. He went to the witch at Endor, the same kind he had put out of the land, and Samuel told him, “the Lord is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” Because he was bashful, self-willed, easily manipulated and made excuses, he lost the kingdom. Fear the Most High, not man.

Saul saw the host of the Philistines and “was afraid, and his heart greatly trembled.” What is fear? “For fear is nothing else but a betraying of the succours which reason offereth.”

A soldier broke it down: the succours go into comfort, and fear betrays that comfort. What reason offers is the lies you make up in your head. You trick yourself into being scared, because you make up things in your mind which ain’t really there.

And on top of that, fear is a lack of faith. Your faith is supposed to be in the Lord, but a lot of the time your faith is basically what you can see with your eyes. Saul looked at the host of the Philistines with his eyes and his heart trembled, instead of trusting the Lord who had made him king.

This is the commandment Saul turned around and broke: “There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch, Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits.” The Lord said none of these would be found among Israel.

Saul had just rid the land of all of them: the soothsayers, the witches, the familiar spirits and the wizards. That is what the woman at En-dor throws back at him: “thou knowest what Saul hath done, how he hath cut off those that have familiar spirits, and the wizards, out of the land: wherefore then layest thou a snare for my life, to cause me to die?” You trying to get me killed.

Now the Lord has stopped answering him, “neither by dreams, nor by Urim, nor by prophets”, and the same man who cut them off says, “Seek me a woman that hath a familiar spirit, that I may go to her, and enquire of her.” Find me a wizard so I can know what is going on. His mind is all over the place. He is double-minded, breaking the very commandment he had enforced, and he disguises himself and goes by night so no one will see it.

That is where bashfulness leads: self-willed, disobedient, deceitful, making excuses, easily manipulated. Samuel tells him the Lord “is departed from thee, and is become thine enemy.” The Lord rent the kingdom out of his hand and gave it to David, and Saul and his sons would be with Samuel the next day. “There is that destroyeth his own soul through bashfulness.” Saul never believed in himself, so he never believed God; he had Samuel's counsel the whole time and would not listen, and when that guidance was gone he ran to the very thing the law forbade.

This is where the breaking of “the pride of your power” leads. “And upon them that are left alive of you I will send a faintness into their hearts in the lands of their enemies”. Into their minds: mentally and spiritually, you are going to be broken down. Then “the sound of a shaken leaf shall chase them”: no courage. And “they shall flee, as fleeing from a sword; and they shall fall when none pursueth.”

“And they shall fall one upon another, as it were before a sword, when none pursueth: and ye shall have no power to stand before your enemies.” Think about that spiritually. Take 2026. When black people get mad at other black people, do we show each other mercy, or do we go full-fledged? We even came up with terms for it: turning up, going savage, crashing out. But do we have that same level of aggression toward white police, or the other nations, or the Chinese? Not at all. We will stand and be aggressive with each other all day long, cuss each other out, beat each other up, kill each other. But we will not stand before the other nations. And to be clear, we do not advocate violence on anybody. The point is that the spirit is not the same toward the nations as it is toward each other.

That faintness is on the face of the African brother who said the colonizers left too early, that we are not prepared to rule ourselves. Not only defeated but subdued: low self-esteem, lack of confidence, self-hate, no faith in his own people. It is seen in a whole country left to itself that looks to the white man, to foreign aid and loans, to save it: a mall built under Chinese direction with not a brick out of place, while what our people build for ourselves has uneven steps and lopsided houses. You can’t do nothing right for yourself. That is what comes of low self-esteem.

So this is the fruit of verse 17, “they that hate you shall reign over you; and ye shall flee when none pursueth you”, and of verse 19, the pride of our power broken. These are the minds the Lord is going to use our brothers to change.
