“Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer: and ye know that no murderer hath eternal life abiding in him.”

That is Simon. He hated Onias, his brother, and his faction committed murders. This is the domino effect: it starts off as coveting; Simon coveted power. From there it turned to anger, from there to slander, and from there to murder. It is never just one sin, and not only are you affected, the people you sinned against are affected too.

Holding on to anger is like drinking poison and expecting the other person to die. You are drinking poison waiting for somebody else to drop dead, and they are not dropping dead. The only one being affected is you. This goes for men and women.

Onias was the opposite. He went to the king “not to be an accuser of his countrymen, but seeking the good of all, both publick and private”. He did not even go there to accuse Simon. That is the difference between a brother and a betrayer.

“There be three things that mine heart feareth; and for the fourth I was sore afraid: the slander of a city, the gathering together of an unruly multitude, and a false accusation: all these are worse than death.”

Simon did all three. The slander of a city: God does not like that thing, and Simon slandered the city. The gathering together of an unruly multitude: Simon had all the Greeks gather together to try to get the money from Jerusalem. And a false accusation: he accused Onias of doing this to Heliodorus. God said all these are worse than death.

Then think about this: don’t tell me what they say about me, tell me why they feel so comfortable telling you. In every school there is that one brother or sister that all the murmurers draw to, and they tell them all the things they don’t like about people. Why do they draw to you? You obviously did not have our back, because they are slandering and they feel so comfortable saying evil to you.

A deacon once pointed out a sister in red shoes with high heels and called her a hoe because of the shoes. The Bishop called Deacon Asaf, Deacon Malachi and the others over and asked them if she was; they said no. And he blew that brother’s spot up in front of them. You cannot come to me with evil. We must train ourselves to hate evil.

“Use not to make any manner of lie: for the custom thereof is not good.”

Use not to make any manner of lie, not a big one and not a small one. The custom of it is not good: when lying becomes your custom, it becomes what you are.

This follows the false witness of Exodus 20:16 and the maul, sword and sharp arrow of Proverbs 25:18. Simon made a custom of lying: he betrayed the money, slandered Onias, and called a man zealous of the law a traitor. These are basic laws, and our people must keep them.

Simon “was he bold to call him a traitor, that had deserved well of the city, and tendered his own nation, and was so zealous of the laws.” He was so bold he called Onias the high priest a traitor, that type of a brother, a man zealous of the law.

The law is plain: “Thou shalt not bear false witness against thy neighbour.” Don’t bear false witness.

These are basic laws, but for some reason in the black community they are so difficult. Just so, so difficult. Simon broke this one outright when he falsely accused Onias before the Greeks, and everything that followed came out of that false witness.

“But when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. Simon hated Onias the third so much that he had one of his men kill one of Onias’s priests. That is why it is never just one thing; it is a domino effect of sins. James shows where it comes from.

“From whence come wars and fightings among you? come they not hence, even of your lusts that war in your members? Ye lust, and have not: ye kill, and desire to have, and cannot obtain”. Simon wanted the upper hand over Onias, and he could not get it. So what did he do?

“ye fight and war, yet ye have not, because ye ask not.” Because you are not praying to the Lord about it. “Ye ask, and receive not, because ye ask amiss, that ye may consume it upon your lusts.” When you pray and still do not receive, it is because you ask for the wrong reasons. You have a lustful purpose behind it, a purpose that is not for the benefit of the nation.

This is a self-examination class for all of us: these are the attributes of Simon.

“Take ye heed every one of his neighbour, and trust ye not in any brother: for every brother will utterly supplant, and every neighbour will walk with slanders.”

Every neighbour will walk with slanders. “And they will deceive every one his neighbour, and will not speak the truth: they have taught their tongue to speak lies, and weary themselves to commit iniquity.”

There are people who love the slander. They teach their tongue to speak lies, and they are very good at it; there are some very good liars out there. You ever see a woman caught in the midst of adultery? She starts crying: this is not what it looks like. And some men will dismiss what they saw with their own eyes. Some of you are such a simp.

Don’t bring anybody like that around. They cannot roll with us. Let them stay over there with those other camps. That is what Simon was: a brother that supplanted, walked with slanders, and would not speak the truth about Onias.

“And if a soul sin, and hear the voice of swearing, and is a witness, whether he hath seen or known of it; if he do not utter it, then he shall bear his iniquity.”

What does that mean? Whatever the judgment is on that man, you get the judgment. This is why in the hood, in the ghetto, people see murders all the time and say, I’m not saying nothing. Then weeks later, a month, a year, that same person ends up dead, and you say, what did she do, they never killed nobody. No: they were a witness, and they chose not to utter it.

Read on and the law also says “if a soul swear, pronouncing with his lips to do evil, or to do good, whatsoever it be that a man shall pronounce with an oath, and it be hid from him; when he knoweth of it, then he shall be guilty in one of these.” And when he is guilty, “he shall confess that he hath sinned in that thing”.

A story from camp: the brothers were planning who to take traveling, and one brother’s hair was unkempt. He was told to trim it, and he answered, well, I guess I’m not traveling then. A couple of men heard it. A young man from Detroit told what was said, and when the officer who heard it first was questioned the next week, he said, I heard it, I was going to tell you next week. Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me.

Be mindful of brothers. They may seem decent on the outside, but you have to be mindful of the things they say, or don’t say.

“Ye have heard that it was said by them of old time, Thou shalt not kill; and whosoever shall kill shall be in danger of the judgment: But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”.

It does not start with the murder. It starts with anger at your brother without a cause. “and whosoever shall say to his brother, Raca, shall be in danger of the council”. Raca means thou fool, vain fellow, and the council there is man’s council.

“but whosoever shall say, Thou fool, shall be in danger of hell fire.” Just continuing the sin, the name calling and all of that, puts you in danger of hell fire. That is when God has to step in.

These are the attributes of Simon, and the class is a self-examination for all of us. Simon’s anger toward Onias turned into slander and name calling, calling him a traitor, and it ended in murder.

“A man that beareth false witness against his neighbour is a maul, and a sword, and a sharp arrow.”

Why is he a maul, a sword and a sharp arrow? Because that man will get people hurt, and will get people killed. A false witness is a weapon.

That is what Simon’s false witness against Onias became. He called the high priest a traitor, and before long “by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. His lie was a sword in the hands of his faction, and it drew blood among his own people.

“This Simon now, of whom we spake afore, having been a betrayer of the money, and of his country, slandered Onias”. Simon of the tribe of Benjamin revealed the secret of the money to the Greeks and then slandered Onias the third, telling them Onias was the one who did that to Heliodorus. This Simon was no damn good.

Now look at the ones who stand next to that kind of man: “Whoso is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: he heareth cursing, and bewrayeth it not.”

The type of man who is a partner with it hates his own soul. He hears the cursing and does not tell it. He keeps it tucked in. That goes directly against the law in Leviticus 5, where the one who hears and does not utter it bears the iniquity.

So it is not only the Simon who is guilty. The one who stands by, hears the evil, and keeps quiet is partnered with him, and he is hating his own soul.

“Whoso privily slandereth his neighbour, him will I cut off: him that hath an high look and a proud heart will not I suffer.”

There is a lot of slander in the Israelite community; Deacon Asaf has been going over it in classes these last two weeks. There are camps that thrive off slander, hatred, name calling, ridicule and false accusations.

God already told you he is going to cut off people who do that. Cut off means he is going to kill them. So for you to join with these people, you are nothing but a fool.

And the high look and the proud heart come from the slander; that is what they do. They think God is with them, and the men and women around them, as stupid as they are, believe God is with them. God is not with them, not according to these scriptures.

Simon slandered Onias the third. So how serious is slander? “For I have heard the slander of many: fear was on every side: while they took counsel together against me, they devised to take away my life.”

Slander is not a light thing. It is the first step of a counsel against a man’s life. The ones who slander take counsel together, and what they devise is to take away his life.

That is exactly the road Simon walked. He slandered Onias to the Greeks, and it did not stop at words: “when their hatred went so far, that by one of Simon’s faction murders were committed”. The slander of many leads to the taking of life.

“And after him rose up Nathan to prophesy in the time of David.” So we know who we are talking about: this is David, in the days of Nathan the prophet, the prophet the Lord sent to him after Bathsheba. The next verse carries on: “As is the fat taken away from the peace offering, so was David chosen out of the children of Israel.”

That is the same David of 2 Samuel 11. He went out on the roof, “he saw a woman washing herself; and the woman was very beautiful to look upon.” Bad to the bone. He sent and inquired: I got power, let me send some people over there, let me make this official. One with a spiritual mind made it plain: this is the wife of Uriah the Hittite, this is somebody's wife, bro. “And David sent messengers, and took her” anyway. Wisdom and understanding were right there, and he pushed them aside.

“and she came in unto him, and he lay with her”. She wasn't right either. She didn't resist, she wasn't opposed; she thought she came up. “And the woman conceived, and sent and told David, and said, I am with child.”

You see how Satan can deceive you. Satan put that lust in him to where he just didn't care, and he went the extra mile: he put Uriah in the front of the battle, got him killed, and took the wife. What he saw, the desire, the action, the cover-up, and the consequences: his first child was gone. Yet Sirach remembers David as the one chosen out of the children of Israel, and that leads to what the Lord did with him.

“The Lord took away his sins, and exalted his horn for ever: he gave him a covenant of kings, and a throne of glory in Israel.” The Lord did forgive David. He loved David, and David messed up.

David saw Bathsheba from the roof, took another man's wife, put Uriah in battle to be killed, and lost the child. That is as bad as it gets. But David repented, and the Lord took away his sins, exalted his horn, and gave him a covenant of kings and a throne of glory in Israel.

And that's another thing. A lot of times we are going to fall and do things that are not comely according to the scriptures. That don't mean you bunker down, go into a fetal position and say woe is me. You get yourself together, you repent, and you move forward. You don't go back. What did Christ say? Go, and sin no more.

You got to pick up the pieces and keep moving. We are all going to make mistakes. It is how you handle the mistake: it happened, so what are you going to do now, moving forward?

The Lord set both harvests before Israel from the beginning: “I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live.”

What you put in, you are going to get; you are going to receive a reward. Life and blessing for the one who sows to the Spirit, death and cursing for the one who sows to his flesh. Heaven and earth are called as witnesses, so no one can say he was not told. God is not mocked.

And the choice reaches past you: choose life “that both thou and thy seed may live.” What a man sows, his children reap with him.

“he that soweth to the Spirit shall of the Spirit reap life everlasting.” When you sow yourself into the scriptures, the Lord is going to give you blessings: he will show you favor, have mercy on you, and give you abundance. That is Joshua 1:8: “This book of the law shall not depart out of thy mouth; but thou shalt meditate therein day and night.”

We should meditate on the scriptures day and night, “that thou mayest observe to do according to all that is written therein: for then thou shalt make thy way prosperous, and then thou shalt have good success.” Meditating and doing is the sowing.

When we do that, the Lord makes our way prosperous. He gives us the abundance we desire, spiritually, emotionally, all the increases we desire, when we put our mind on the Lord. That is reaping of the Spirit.

“And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve.” You cannot serve two masters. You can't serve the flesh and serve God at the same time. You have to choose; ain't no in between.

That is why he said he would rather you be cold or hot. If you are lukewarm, battling that middle ground and playing games, he will spew you out of his mouth. Sowing to the flesh and sowing to the Spirit cannot be done at once.

“whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” Choose the Lord, sow to the Spirit, and of the Spirit reap life everlasting.

“whatsoever a man soweth, that shall he also reap.” What you put in, you are going to reap. When you put in the sin, the consequences are going to happen, period. Paul says it plainly: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

Sin is death. That is the corruption reaped by the one who sows to his flesh: sow that sin to your flesh and you will be judged by it. And the gift of God, eternal life through Christ, is the “life everlasting” reaped by the one who sows to the Spirit.

What you put in, you are going to receive as a reward. Wages for sin, a gift for the one who sows to the Spirit. God is not mocked.

1 Samuel 10:6 says you “shalt be turned into another man.” 2 Esdras 14:34 tells you what your part is in that turning.

“Therefore if so be that ye will subdue your own understanding, and reform your hearts, ye shall be kept alive and after death ye shall obtain mercy.”

Subdue your own understanding and reform your heart. We have to be transformed in the renewing of our minds. Transformed.

That is what the brother with the addiction runs from. He comes to the table having drunk a whole fifth in one night and says he is not an alcoholic. Even the white man knows the first step of recovery is to admit it: you have to realize you need help, that you are sick. Has he watched the classes on alcohol the Bishops and Deacons go over all the time? No. Why not? Because he is running away from his issues, and you cannot run away from that thing. You have to subdue your own understanding, reform your heart, and let the word turn you into another man, and then you shall be kept alive and after death obtain mercy.

A lot of us are not finding comfort in the scriptures because we lack faith. You don’t believe the Bible can transform you. You don’t believe it can turn you into another man, that you could become a whole different person. But 1 Samuel 10:6 says it: “And the Spirit of the Lord will come upon thee, and thou shalt prophesy with them, and shalt be turned into another man.”

John 3:3 says the same thing to Nicodemus: “Verily, verily, I say unto thee, Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

Being turned into another man is being born again. The brother who drank a whole fifth in one night, the one who says, I can’t put it down, it’s a part of me, is not stuck being that man. Except he be born again, turned into another man, he cannot see the kingdom. The bottle is the battle, and the Bible is how you are turned into another man and win it.
blog/2026/2026-06-20-2026-06-20-the-madm:
“Hath Israel no sons? hath he no heir? why then doth their king inherit Gad, and his people dwell in his cities?” Historically, when Gad was moved out of the land, Ammon moved their rusty butts into our land and dwelt in our cities. Amos tells what Ammon did to get there: “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border.”

When they caught our people, they ripped up the women with child. They hung them upside down, just like the white man did to us, cut their stomachs so the baby fell out, and crushed the babies. That is what the Bible says they did, and why: they wanted to enlarge their border and take over our lands. They slaughtered Gad. God says, I'm not forgiving you for that; I'm not letting you slide.

“But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind.” Rabbah is the city of Jeremiah 49:2, where the Lord will cause “an alarm of war” to be heard. A day of battle is coming, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: that's the Lord.

“And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the Lord.” Put the leader of North Korea, Kim Jong-un, on the screen. Whether it is that particular man or not, whoever is the leader in the land of Ammon at that time is going to be a prisoner of war. That is what the prophecy says, so look for it.

“And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.”

“then shall Israel be heir unto them that were his heirs, saith the Lord.” What does that mean? Romans 8 jumps right to it: “And if children, then heirs; heirs of God, and joint-heirs with Christ; if so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together.”

The condition is that we suffer with him, that we may also be glorified together. The suffering comes first, the inheritance after, just as Gad lost his cities and the Lord promises to give them back.

“Search the scriptures.” Our job is to search the scriptures. The nations don't; they leave their scripture searching to Matthew through Revelation with their misunderstanding from Christianity. “The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

Searching the scriptures is not only for ourselves. What the Lord reveals by it belongs to us and to our children, so that we and they may do all the words of this law.

“It is the glory of God to conceal a thing: but the honour of kings is to search out a matter.” When God conceals something, it is in parable form, metaphors and allegories, and it is our job to figure out what the Lord means by A, B and C.

Read Jeremiah 48, “against Moab”, or Jeremiah 49, “Concerning the Ammonites”, and unless you search the scriptures and pray to the Lord, you'll say, I don't know who Moab is, I don't know who the Ammonites are, I don't know who Gad is, I'm confused, so I'll stick to Matthew through Revelation. That's what the churches do. Christians don't know and Muslims don't know, confused and discombobulated, unable to identify these nations today.

The honour of kings is to search it out: to find who Moab, Ammon, Gad and Asia are today. The matter is concealed, but it is there for those who search.

What happens when sin reigns in your body and has dominion over you? “And the guide of them who keep my commandments and precepts, saith the Lord God: let not your sins weigh you down, and let not your iniquities lift up themselves.” He is the guide of those who keep his commandments and precepts.

“let not your sins weigh you down”: sometimes you fall in the midst of sin, and Satan gets in your ear and whispers, you're no good, you need to leave this truth, the Lord can't use a person like you. Well, he used Samson. He used David. He used a lot of our forefathers that fell to sin. “and let not your iniquities lift up themselves”: don't let them rise back up in your body again.

“Woe be unto them that are bound with their sins, and covered with their iniquities like as a field is covered over with bushes, and the path thereof covered with thorns, that no man may travel through!” You may say, I'm not bound with my sin. Bound in your sins is sin reigning in your body and having dominion over you. Just like no man can travel through that path, we can't reach you with the scriptures any more. Your heart is hardened, your sin has dominated your life, and you're not you anymore. The scriptures have no effect on you.

“It is left undressed, and is cast into the fire to be consumed therewith.” Death and destruction: that is the final outcome, brothers. Stop watching the porn. “And such were some of you: but ye are washed”: that is the way out, not staying bound.

“Know ye not that the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom of God?” To know who the unrighteous are, you have to know what righteousness is, and the law defines it: “And it shall be our righteousness, if we observe to do all these commandments before the Lord our God, as he hath commanded us.”

That is what righteousness is: observing to do all the commandments before the Lord, as he commanded. So the unrighteous who will not inherit the kingdom are those who will not do the commandments.

That is the problem with Christianity. It is not that the Lord's arm is too short or his ear too heavy; it is that your sins have separated between you and your God. They are not trying to transform their lives to that of the nation of Israel according to the holy scriptures. And that is why Paul lists fornicators, idolaters, adulterers and the rest: every one of them breaks the commandments that are our righteousness.

“Be not deceived: neither fornicators”, “nor adulterers”. Fornication covers the whole list of sexual sins in Leviticus 18. And for the porno brothers, Christ said: “But I say unto you, That whosoever looketh on a woman to lust after her hath committed adultery with her already in his heart.”

So porn falls into that category. It is adultery in the heart, and adulterers shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

Who still struggles with porn? Not who is always watching; who still struggles with it? Nine hands went up in the room. The fight is real, and it has to be named for what it is before it can be fought.

The Christian says, oh no, that's not the righteousness; go to Romans 10:4: “For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one that believeth.” See, we ain't got to keep no laws, so that cancels out Deuteronomy 6:25. No, numbskull. We don't run from scriptures; we explain and edify on the scriptures.

Christ is the end of the law of animal sacrifice for righteousness. Christ took the place of the animal sacrifice. And where they think they have you, “to every one that believeth”, read verse one for the context: “Brethren, my heart's desire and prayer to God for Israel is, that they might be saved.”

The whole subject is Israel being saved. Israel had “a zeal of God, but not according to knowledge”, “going about to establish their own righteousness”. Christ is our righteousness in the law because he suffered and took the place of the law of sacrifice. That does not do away with the commandments of Deuteronomy 6:25; it is why the unrighteous, who will not keep them, still shall not inherit the kingdom of God.

“Let not sin therefore reign in your mortal body, that ye should obey it in the lusts thereof.” The word reign means to rule: don't let sin rule your mortal body. Every brother says, I got the porn under control, I am in control. There's no such thing as control of sin. Once you start obeying that lust, it has you in control; you don't have it in control.

“Neither yield ye your members as instruments of unrighteousness unto sin: but yield yourselves unto God, as those that are alive from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness unto God.” Men and women are alive from the dead. We have to submit ourselves to Christ; he is our commander, our leader, and what he says we must do.

“For sin shall not have dominion over you”: Paul is reiterating. Dominion goes back to reign in verse 12. “for ye are not under the law”, the law of sacrifice, “but under grace”, the grace of Christ. “What then? shall we sin, because we are not under the law, but under grace?” Should we keep watching porn because we're not under the law of sacrifice? “God forbid.”

One brother said, I got it under control. In a store, thinking about porn, he was on his phone looking at it, forgot where he was, took his pecker out and started looking at all the ladies. Does that sound like he had it under control? He got arrested; he's in jail. Another decided to look at porn while he drove home, and bam, he crashed. It has you in check. You need a checklist in your mind so you can say, I'm messed up, I need help, because I could die or I could be in jail. That is sin reigning, and the unrighteous shall not inherit the kingdom.

Men, we want dominion. We want rulership; we want to subdue the nations. God said, “Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion,” and he told them, “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it.” Being made after his image, we were supposed to subdue the earth and bring everything under foot.

When you read “after our likeness,” understand it is more than what you look like. At that time everybody was of color, yet God gave a specific people rulership. David shows what the likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is not just appearance; it is being righteous. Christ is black, God is black, and we are made after his image, but the image alone does not bring the dominion. In being righteous we will subdue and have dominion over things.

So the government must be in place, and in that we must be keeping the commandments. It is the only way we are going to get it. That government cannot happen unless we are righteous.

“My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge: because thou hast rejected knowledge, I will also reject thee, that thou shalt be no priest to me”. What does that part mean, that thou shalt be no priest to me?

There was a promise made to us and our ancestors: “And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Israel.” A kingdom of priests. That is what Israel was called to be.

Go back to Hosea and it tells you why we lost it: “seeing thou hast forgotten the law of thy God”. That is the knowledge. Usually we jump over to Malachi 2:7, but the verse tells you right there: the knowledge is the law of God, his laws, his commandments, his statutes. Because we forgot it, he rejected us from that priesthood.

That is why we are destroyed as a race, as a people, mentally and spiritually. The twelve tribes of Israel are a destroyed race. This is why other races come into our communities and run the hospitals, the stores, the clinics. The black man and the brown man do have the ability, and many of us have the knowledge to do it, but they do not want us to have the capabilities.

“For your hands are defiled with blood, and your fingers with iniquity.” Our hands in the black and brown community are defiled with blood. In Joliet a young man, twenty-three years old, shot to death his own mother, his aunt, his uncle, his bedridden brother and his three sisters, killed another man and shot one more, and then shot himself. That's trauma right there, and the law explains it: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart.”

The Lord shall smite thee with madness: meaning our people are insane. No rhyme, no reason to what they do or why they do it. That's being smitten with madness. We have generational curses. Three teens on a thirty-hour spree of armed robberies and the murder of a churchgoing man; a woman charged with stabbing and killing a three-year-old boy, appearing in court laughing and smiling: that is stricken with madness.

The Bible says, thou shalt not kill, and we are not taught that in church, so some of us grow up with a hateful and murderous spirit on us. No matter how bad, insulting or degrading these videos are, they are filtered through the Bible, showing the stage and state of where we are today, and it is still proof that we are the children of Israel under the curses. The Bible ain't the white man's book. The Bible is our book.

That is why the Lord's hand is not shortened and his ear is not heavy, and still he does not save: “your iniquities have separated between you and your God.”

“Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne: mercy and truth shall go before thy face.” God's throne is all about justice and judgment. That's exactly what the world doesn't want.

“nor any pleadeth for truth”: they are not pleading for God's truth. The families of our brothers and sisters put to death unjustly, Sandra Bland and the rest, want the truth regarding their case, but they don't want God's truth as a whole. We may march with them and support them, but there is no internal change: they are mad at the white man and still celebrating Christmas and the white man's holidays. “be not conformed to this world: but be ye transformed by the renewing of your mind.” If I used to celebrate Easter, now I celebrate Passover. They are making a conscious effort not to change.

The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, the habitation of his throne. That is why the world, which cries for justice, will be angry when it comes.

Everybody says, I can't wait until Jesus comes back. Let's see what the Bible says: “And the nations were angry, and thy wrath is come.” All these nations, countries and religious organizations say they want the Messiah to return, and the Bible prophesies they will be angry.

Why are they angry? Because “Justice and judgment are the habitation of thy throne.” The Lord is coming with justice and judgment, and the nations don't want that. Many of those nations are living on stolen land, like America. This is stolen land. They are lying when they say they can't wait. Christ's wrath is coming; he's not coming to hand out lollipops and hugs and kisses.

“and the time of the dead, that they should be judged, and that thou shouldest give reward unto thy servants the prophets, and to the saints, and them that fear thy name, small and great.” You know what that reward is? Power. He's going to give his servants power.

“and shouldest destroy them which destroy the earth.” That's them. They say the aerosols in the black and brown community are destroying the ozone layer, not their rockets and missiles. All that climate change global BS: they are the ones destroying the earth, digging up and sucking out the oil that is meant to lubricate the tectonic plates, and then they wonder why the earthquakes are happening. They know it, and that's why they will be angry at his return. None calleth for the justice of God.

“None calleth for justice, nor any pleadeth for truth.” You might say, that's not right; our people are in the street all the time crying, no justice, no peace. But the justice our people want is called money. They don't want the justice of the Bible. Here is God's justice: “If any man have an ear, let him hear. He that leadeth into captivity shall go into captivity: he that killeth with the sword must be killed with the sword. Here is the patience and the faith of the saints.”

Now that's justice. And you know what our people say? No, you hate the white man. They know what the scripture means: the one who led into slavery going into slavery, the one who killed with the sword being put to death by the sword. And they say, no, we don't want that kind of justice. We want money, money, money.

That is Isaiah 59:4: none calling for God's justice. They cry for justice in the streets, but when the justice of God is read to them, they call it hateful.

“But in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and of silver, but also of wood and of earth; and some to honour, and some to dishonour.” The great house is the nation of Israel; think of it as whatever IUIC school you come from. Every camp leader, the head of the sanctuary, must be able to identify the gold brothers and the silver brothers, the gold sisters and silver sisters, and also look through the school and say, this brother and this sister is earth, this one is wood.

If you can't discern that, you'll have problems in the school, putting people in positions that don't fit them. Marcus Garvey had his ships and put his best friends over them, and they didn't know how to run a ship: one crashed, one went to his girlfriend's house, and he lost it all because of friendship. Shake the friendship appointments. Who is best qualified? Who knows what they're doing? A dummy who doesn't study set up as a school leader, and all hell breaks loose. If sanctuary leaders have no discernment, they are spiritually blind and destined for ruin.

Some brothers and sisters are just slow and need more time to grow. Fine; don't put them in that position yet if others are better qualified. “If a man therefore purge himself from these, he shall be a vessel unto honour, sanctified, and meet for the master's use, and prepared unto every good work.” Purge yourself from the wood and earth spirits. They see this truth not as a government, not as the mustard seed of a government, but as a social club, dancing every new moon and confused when it comes to God's work. That is how a people groping like the blind becomes vessels unto honour.

“Yea, truth faileth; and he that departeth from evil maketh himself a prey.” If you depart from evil by repenting, you make yourself a prey to everybody around you; everybody around you hates your guts now. Amos says the same thing: “They hate him that rebuketh in the gate, and they abhor him that speaketh uprightly.”

That includes some of your own mothers and fathers, sisters and brothers. They hate the one who rebukes and abhor the one who speaks uprightly, because “truth is fallen in the street, and equity cannot enter.”

“and the Lord saw it, and it displeased him that there was no judgment.” There was no true judgment in the earth. The one who departs from evil is hated for it, and the Lord sees it.

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes: we stumble at noonday as in the night; we are in desolate places as dead men.” We got eyes, but we act like we ain't got none. We act like what we just saw didn't happen. The curse said it would be so: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.”

We are like blind people, but we have eyes. We see we're not prospering as a people. We see we're under constant oppression as a people. But we act like we don't see it, because oppression has become so normal to us; it's our everyday life.

It's high noon, but in our minds we are so spiritually blind it is like night for us. “we are in desolate places as dead men”: that's the black and brown community, desolate places, our people like the walking dead. Isaiah 59 is Deuteronomy 28:29 in real time.

That is why verse 9 says, “Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us.” We want to live filthy lives, evil lives, violent lives, and then expect justice from God. It don't work like that. Oppressed and spoiled evermore, and no man shall save thee.

There is a difference between being spiritually slow and being spiritually dead. “we are in desolate places as dead men,” but Sirach shows what the nation needs: “Again, there is another that is slow, and hath need of help, wanting ability, and full of poverty.” We usually read it as an individual, but think about it on a bigger scale. You might say this is Joe or Bob. No, this is us.

Slow, needing help, lacking ability, full of poverty: that is our people. “yet the eye of the Lord looked upon him for good, and set him up from his low estate,” and lifted up his head from misery, so that many that saw it marvelled at him.

The nations are going to marvel when God raises us up. It will be such a shock that this low, degenerate race of people is now going to rule the earth. We lack the ability now; it is the Lord's eye that sets us up from our low estate.

The voices of our people conceive and utter from the heart words of falsehood, lies on top of lies. Christ answers: “He that believeth on him is not condemned: but he that believeth not is condemned already, because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten Son of God.” If you believe on the black Messiah, you are not condemned; if you believe not, you're not even keeping commandment one.

“And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness rather than light, because their deeds were evil.” Christ is that light that came into the world, and men love darkness, sin, rather than light, Christ and keeping the commandments. It didn't change from Isaiah to John; it's the same thing: “we wait for light, but behold obscurity.”

“For every one that doeth evil hateth the light, neither cometh to the light, lest his deeds should be reproved.” They hate Christ, they hate keeping the laws, they hate the commandments, because if you come to Christ your deeds will be reproved: have no other gods before me, bow down to no graven image, remember the Sabbath, honour your father and your mama, thou shalt not kill. They don't want to hear that.

“But he that doeth truth cometh to the light, that his deeds may be made manifest, that they are wrought in God.” We want Christ, the word of God, to make our deeds manifest. What am I? Lord, show me.

Leviticus 26 says that even “when they be in the land of their enemies”, like today here in America, “I will not cast them away, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly”. Then: “But I will for their sakes remember the covenant of their ancestors”. Who said bloodline ain’t important? The Bible says he will remember the covenant of your ancestors. Luke 1 is saying the same thing in the New Testament.

“Blessed be the Lord God of Israel; for he hath visited and redeemed his people, And hath raised up an horn of salvation for us in the house of his servant David”. The horn of salvation is Christ. He is the king, out of the house of David. “As he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets, which have been since the world began: That we should be saved from our enemies, and from the hand of all that hate us”. That is what Leviticus 26 is saying: in the land of their enemies he will not cast them away.

“To perform the mercy promised to our fathers”, our ancestors, “and to remember his holy covenant; The oath which he sware to our father Abraham”. That is the covenant of the ancestors in Leviticus 26:45, remembered for their sakes and brought to pass through Christ.

And what is it for? “that we being delivered out of the hand of our enemies might serve him without fear”. The God who brought our fathers out of Egypt in the sight of the heathen has not broken his covenant with us. He will deliver us out of the hand of our enemies so that we serve him without fear.

Moses said “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee”. When we got emancipated we thought we were free. Juneteenth. Then the white man took the sheet out of the closet, cut two holes in it, put on the white robe, and it was time for the KKK, patterned after the capirotes of Spain from the Inquisition. Spain was in this country, and what they had over there they brought here. As soon as we thought we were free, they gave us hell.

The Most High speaks to that in Zechariah: “And I am very sore displeased with the heathen that are at ease: for I was but a little displeased, and they helped forward the affliction.” God was a little displeased with us, because we broke his laws and his commandments. But the heathen afflicted us more and more and more. That is what God is saying right there.

Then back to Moses: “thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Imagine building your own town because white folks don't want you drinking their water or going to their school: your own cab company, your own hospital, your own bank. Then you hear a noise, and they are dropping dynamite on the city from planes and murdering a lot of us. That is the heathen helping forward the affliction, far beyond the little displeasure God had with us.

So the curses of Deuteronomy 28 came on us for our sins, but the nations went further than God sent them, and he is very sore displeased with them for it. The heathen that are at ease today are the ones who will answer for what they added to our affliction.

Cain said, “Behold, thou hast driven me out this day from the face of the earth; and from thy face shall I be hid”: God was not dealing with him anymore. “and I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond in the earth.” A fugitive is somebody always on the run, someone who never pays for his crimes. A vagabond is in everybody's land and everybody's home.

But Cain did not escape forever. Wisdom shows he was put to death: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” Cain murdered Abel, and Cain was killed the same way. The judgment caught up with him.

So what did it mean, I shall be a fugitive and a vagabond? It speaks of his descendants. Has America paid for its crimes? Have the whites in South Africa paid? In Australia? None of them has paid for their crimes yet. They have been on the run from justice, living in everybody's land.

That goes with Job 20, read in the same class: “His bones are full of the sin of his youth.” The fugitive has never paid, but as Cain perished in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother, judgment will come on his children. As Job said, “he shall vomit them up again”: everything taken will be restored.

Isaiah says “Thy sons have fainted, they lie at the head of all the streets, as a wild bull in a net”. That is why our young men hang on the corners: uncontrollable, like wild bulls in a net. It's a trap; this system is a trap. “they are full of the fury of the Lord”. What is the fury of the Lord? Deuteronomy 28:15-68, the curses God put upon us, and they are on our young men.

Even this one: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Some of our young men are mentally deranged. The ones doing that new type of singing, drill: they are murderers, they are killers, and they don't care.

It is seen in the neighborhood. A house in Queens, a playground across the street with about twenty adorable little kids running around. Time went by, those little kids grew up, and they were having shootouts, bullets flying through the house, the kids and the wife thrown on the floor. That is what they turned into.

So the sons fainted at the head of all the streets are the sons of Israel under the curse of madness. They are full of the fury of the Lord, the rebuke of thy God, and that is why they cannot be controlled.

“Therefore hear now this, thou afflicted, and drunken, but not with wine”. We are an afflicted people: look at the news, and we are afflicted from sun up to sun down, over and over. You can turn a blind eye to it, but it's there. And we are a drunk people. What does it mean we're drunk? We're drunk with lies, drunk with religions, drunk with falsehood.

Micah shows that wine represents falsehood: “If a man walking in the spirit and falsehood do lie, saying, I will prophesy unto thee of wine and of strong drink; he shall even be the prophet of this people.” Wine and strong drink symbolize lies. The man walking in falsehood prophesies lies, and he becomes the prophet of this people.

So what are we drunk with? Lies. Some of us believe in these false Christian religions, Islam, politics; we're drunk in some philosophy out here. But the Lord “pleadeth the cause of his people”, and he says “I have taken out of thine hand the cup of trembling”. That is why we are waking up now. “even the dregs of the cup of my fury”: the dregs is the bottom, the last few drops left in the cup. “thou shalt no more drink it again” after this captivity is over. He will put it into the hand of them that afflict us, Esau and the nations.

“These were more noble than those in Thessalonica, in that they received the word with all readiness of mind, and searched the scriptures daily, whether those things were so.”

That was the attribute Job had: “the cause which I knew not I searched out.” The Bereans received the word with all readiness of mind, and they searched the scriptures daily to see whether the things they were taught were so. That made them more noble.

We have to be the same way. Search things out daily. Do not just hear it and move on, and do not come asking without having looked first. A father to the poor, a judge in the gate, and a man who searched out what he did not know: that is the kind of man Job was, and the kind we have to become.

“Because I delivered the poor that cried, and the fatherless, and him that had none to help him.” Job is telling you what he used to do. The fatherless are the orphans, and he delivered them and the ones who had no one to help.

That goes into God’s law: “He doth execute the judgment of the fatherless and widow, and loveth the stranger, in giving him food and raiment.”

Job judged the way God judges. And he did not stop there: “The blessing of him that was ready to perish came upon me: and I caused the widow’s heart to sing for joy.” When somebody is about to die and wants to speak to you, sometimes you are at a loss for words and do not know what to say to bring them comfort. Job knew exactly what to say. Then he comforted the widow, mourning and crying because her husband just died.

That is a hard thing. You have to pray to the Lord: give me the words. You have to let a dying believer know, it is going to be okay; even when you leave this world, you are going to be all right. When we die, that is not the end of it for us, and that is what comforts us.

“When I went out to the gate through the city, when I prepared my seat in the street!” What does that mean, he prepared his seat in the street?

“Judges and officers shalt thou make thee in all thy gates, which the Lord thy God giveth thee, throughout thy tribes: and they shall judge the people with just judgment.”

So Job was a judge. He sat in the gate and judged the people with just judgment. That is why “The young men saw me, and hid themselves: and the aged arose, and stood up. The princes refrained talking, and laid their hand on their mouth.” When Job rolled on the scene, everybody shut the hell up. Princes covered their mouths, young men moved the hell out of the way, and the old men stood up and saluted him. The nobles held their peace; they had nothing to say either. That is total respect and honor.

“As I was in the days of my youth, when the secret of God was upon my tabernacle”. What is the secret of God? This shows the relationship between Job and us.

“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

God reveals his secrets to the Israelites. The things revealed belong to us and to our children for ever, and they are revealed for a purpose: that we may do all the words of this law. The secret of God was upon Job’s tabernacle because he was of that people, and he kept that law.

“And they waited for me as for the rain; and they opened their mouth wide as for the latter rain.” They waited for his words with their mouths open. When he was teaching or giving counsel, he was dropping blessings on them, dropping understanding.

It says the same thing as the song of Moses: “My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall distil as the dew, as the small rain upon the tender herb, and as the showers upon the grass”.

So when Job spoke, it was like that: “my speech dropped upon them.” And that right there is prophetic. It is going to come again in the future, near to come.

“My glory was fresh in me, and my bow was renewed in my hand. Unto me men gave ear, and waited, and kept silence at my counsel.” Job was up there. He was no pushover, no punk.

This is what Jethro told Moses: “Hearken now unto my voice, I will give thee counsel, and God shall be with thee: Be thou for the people to God-ward, that thou mayest bring the causes unto God”.

That is what Job was doing. He was for the people to God-ward, bringing their causes to God, and men waited in silence for his counsel. “After my words they spake not again”: after Job spoke, you had nothing to say. “I chose out their way, and sat chief”: he counseled them and directed them, and dwelt as a king in the army.

“I was a father to the poor: and the cause which I knew not I searched out.” Whatever Job did not know, he searched out. Sometimes brothers try to fake stuff. Don’t fake it. Job said, if I did not know it, I searched it out.

Christ said it: “Search the scriptures; for in them ye think ye have eternal life: and they are they which testify of me.”

We have to get to that point. Search it out. Get the Who’s Who with the Apocrypha, get your Zondervan Bible dictionary, get the complete works of Josephus, get your concordance, and do your own work. Before you ask us a question, how about you search it out, and then ask your question after you have done research on it. That is what Job did with every cause he did not know.

Job looks back on his life: “Oh that I were as in months past, as in the days when God preserved me; When his candle shined upon my head, and when by his light I walked through darkness”. When his candle shined upon my head: the Holy Spirit was on me. But what does “by his light I walked through darkness” mean?

“For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life”. The commandment is the lamp, and the law is the light.

That is the light Job walked by. We can only walk through darkness the way Job did: with God’s commandments. Job kept the law, and that law was the light that carried him through a dark world.

“I put on righteousness, and it clothed me: my judgment was as a robe and a diadem.” That shows you how Job used to dress. The way he dressed, that is how his righteousness reflected.

“Let thy priests be clothed with righteousness; and let thy saints shout for joy.”

That is why it was written down beside Job 29:14. Sometimes you just scribble in your Bible, and when you look at it again you see why. God wants his priests clothed with righteousness, and Job put on righteousness and it clothed him. His outward robe and diadem matched the righteousness he walked in, and the saints shout for joy when the righteous are clothed that way.

Elihu tells Job: “By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.” This was Elihu speaking to Job prophetically about times to come. Are we not oppressed today? Yes.

Moses wrote the same thing in the curses: “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways: and thou shalt be only oppressed and spoiled evermore”. That is what Elihu was talking about. The oppressed crying out by reason of the arm of the mighty is Israel under the curses, oppressed and spoiled evermore.

Solomon said it too: “So I returned, and considered all the oppressions that are done under the sun: and behold the tears of such as were oppressed, and they had no comforter; and on the side of their oppressors there was power”. They have the guns, the nuclear weapons, the court system; they have it all, and we have nothing. That is the arm of the mighty.

But the Most High “looked down from the height of his sanctuary” to “hear the groaning of the prisoner; to loose those that are appointed to death”. We are the prisoner: sons of God in a weak body, ruled and dominated by a wicked race of people and subject to their laws. We groan waiting for “the redemption of our body”. We want our godhood back, rulership back, dominion back, to reign on this planet like we once did.

“And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah”. Judah is going to be the teachers. “and bring him unto his people”: Judah is the one the spirit comes on first, to go and gather the tribes. “let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.”

We just read that, and then we go back to Zechariah: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” The Zion there is Judah, and Moses' blessing lines up with it. Judah is called out first, brought unto his people, and God is his help from his enemies, the daughter of Babylon he is dwelling with.

That is why the next words of Zechariah are about those enemies: “he that toucheth you toucheth the apple of his eye.” He that touches Israel touches the apple of God's eye. The Lord promised to help Judah from his enemies, and in Zechariah he sends his hand against the nations which spoiled us.

Zion “dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Who is the daughter of Babylon? David answers: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem; who said, Rase it, rase it, even to the foundation thereof.” E D O M: that's the red people, the ones called so-called white folks. “Rase it” means destroy it, destroy it, even to the foundation.

Then watch what David calls Edom: “O daughter of Babylon, who art to be destroyed”. Edom is the daughter of Babylon, and Edom is destined to be destroyed. “happy shall he be, that rewardeth thee as thou hast served us.”

So Judah is dwelling with Edom, the daughter of Babylon, here in the land of the north. The same Edom is the one the vision of Obadiah is spoken “concerning”, and the class went on from here to show America in the Bible through Edom: the pride of their heart, exalting themselves as the eagle, setting their nest among the stars. The daughter of Babylon Zion is called to flee from is Edom in America, and her end is to be destroyed and rewarded as she served Israel.

Zechariah cries “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is sometimes spoken of as Jerusalem the city, and sometimes as the twelve tribes. But the Psalm shows which Zion this is: the Most High “chose the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved.” That is what it is talking about.

So the Zion that dwells with the daughter of Babylon is Judah. The call just before it, “Come out of her, my people”, shows that God's people are in Babylon, and Zechariah is more specific, tribe by tribe: “Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north”. The land of the north is North America. That's Babylon.

Judah is the one living here in the land of the north. Benjamin can go back to the Caribbean islands, Ephraim can go back to the Caribbean islands, Levi can go back to the Caribbean islands; it is Judah that is always here. So when the Lord says “Deliver thyself, O Zion”, he is calling the tribe of Judah, the mount Zion which he loved, out of America.

Zechariah 2:9 says “I will shake mine hand upon them, and they shall be a spoil to their servants”. Write this down: the servants there is us. Right now we are their servants. God will shake his hand upon the nations, and the nations shall be a spoil to their servants. The wording might be difficult for some of us, so here is a precept to explain it further.

“Therefore as I live, saith the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel, Surely Moab shall be as Sodom, and the children of Ammon as Gomorrah, even the breeding of nettles, and saltpits, and a perpetual desolation”. See that: “the residue of my people shall spoil them, and the remnant of my people shall possess them.” Possess them means own those nations.

So when we go back to Zechariah, “they shall be a spoil to their servants: and ye shall know that the Lord of hosts hath sent me.” The servants are Israel, the remnant of God's people. The nations that made us serve are going to be spoiled by us and possessed by us. America is described as Babylon, the land of the north, and the day is coming when the ones who served there will spoil it.

Deuteronomy 28 shows crystal clear who this demon is that's feeding us.

First, why: “Because thou servedst not the Lord thy God with joyfulness, and with gladness of heart, for the abundance of all things”. It lines up with Luke: these be the days of vengeance, because we broke the commandments of the Lord. We ain't happy to keep the Most High's high holy days. We show joyfulness and gladness of heart for the Fourth of July and these pagan, evil, wicked holidays; but when it comes to Passover, the Sabbath, the day of atonement, the feast of unleavened bread, the beautiful holy days the Lord gave you, you got your lips stuck out. You mad.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. God did that. That is how we're fed: for food, for water, for clothing, even the textiles they stole, for hospital care, for anything you need, you have to go to the same enemy. We don't own nothing. “and he shall put a yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” Who put the yoke of iron on our neck? The so-called white man, the serpent of Revelation. And the evil preachers who deceived us will pay too. Jeremiah 23: woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture. Taking his Bible and lying to God's people with it is a serious crime. So the woman nourished from the face of the serpent is Israel in this captivity, fed by the enemy the Lord sent against us for not serving him with gladness.

Ezra lays out everything Israel lost: “our sanctuary is laid waste, our altar broken down, our temple destroyed; Our psaltery is laid on the ground”. The psaltery is the music. “our song is put to silence, our rejoicing is at an end, the light of our candlestick is put out”, the menorah is put out. “the ark of our covenant is spoiled, our holy things are defiled, and the name that is called upon us is almost profaned”, the name Israel.

It goes on: “our children are put to shame, our priests are burnt, our Levites are gone into captivity, our virgins are defiled, and our wives ravished”, our wives were raped; “our righteous men carried away, our little ones destroyed, our young men are brought in bondage, and our strong men are become weak”.

Then: “And, which is the greatest of all, the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour; for she is delivered into the hands of them that hate us.” What is the seal of Zion? Is that talking about the six-point hexagram, the star of Remphan, the star of Moloch? No. Isaiah shows what the seal of Zion is: the law.

So the seal Solomon asked to be set upon the heart and the arm is the same seal of Zion Ezra mourned: the law of God. The greatest of all Israel's losses was not a symbol but the honour of the law, delivered into the hands of them that hate us.

The Song of Solomon is a metaphor: the whole book represents the Lord's relationship with his chosen people, Israel. So what did Solomon mean, in his righteousness, when he said “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”? The heart is the mind. What is set as a seal upon our mind and upon our arm? Is it the six-point hexagram? Heck no. Here is what he was referring to.

“Therefore shall ye lay up these my words in your heart and in your soul”. These my words are the laws of God, laid up in your heart, meaning your mind. “and bind them for a sign upon your hand, that they may be as frontlets between your eyes.” In ancient times Israel would write the laws on leather and wrap them around their arms. Those were the frontlets, and the frontlets between your eyes are on your forehead.

So go back to the Song: “Set me as a seal upon thine heart”, that's the mind; “as a seal upon thine arm”. The seal is the law, the laws of God, the words of God, bound on the arm and laid up in the mind. People who will not be proven wrong search for scriptures that use the word shield or seal and try to make them say it is the Star of David, forcing a square peg into a circle. That is a complete lie; the seal is the law.

Ezra said “the seal of Sion hath now lost her honour”. Here is what the seal of Zion is: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” Seal the law among my disciples. The law is the seal. The law is the seal.

That is what Solomon meant by “Set me as a seal upon thine heart, as a seal upon thine arm”: the law of God set on the mind and bound on the arm, as Deuteronomy said to bind the words for a sign upon the hand. It is not the six-pointed star.

And it is the same seal the servants of God are sealed with in Revelation. So what is the seal we have to be sealed with? The law. The law. The law. There is nothing else to be said about it; if you keep pushing that star, that is your own vain opinion. Brothers and sisters, come on one accord and stop following the so-called white man and his lies.

“And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.” Then jump up to verse 3: “Hurt not the earth, neither the sea, nor the trees, till we have sealed the servants of our God in their foreheads.”

What is the seal talking about? Go right back to Isaiah 8:16: “Bind up the testimony, seal the law among my disciples.” The servants of God are sealed in their foreheads with the law, the same place Deuteronomy said the words of God would be “as frontlets between your eyes”, in the mind. Some are still saying the star of Moloch, the star of David; that is simple.

So the seal of Song of Solomon 8:6, set upon the heart and upon the arm, is the seal of the servants of God in Revelation: the law, laid up in the mind of the tribes of the children of Israel.

Ezra says that after Adam transgressed, death came “in him and in his generations, of whom came nations, tribes, people, and kindreds, out of number.” Genesis 4 shows one of those lines: Cain's. And in Cain's line, “Jubal: he was the father of all such as handle the harp and organ.”

Cain's line handled the music. They were behind all the music back then, and music is very influential, very powerful when it is in the wrong hands. Is it in the wrong hands today? Yes, it is.

Then Tubal-cain was “an instructer of every artificer in brass and iron”, and brass and iron mean weapons. So Cain had power over entertainment and power over weaponry and warfare. Remember Esau was a man of war; that was Esau's blessing, and it was Cain's blessing too. There is nothing new under the sun.

This is how “every people walked after their own will, and did wonderful things before thee, and despised thy commandments.” Wonderful there means evil; they started to mess around with the daughters of men. And they despised the commandments, which shows the commandments were around back then; that is how Noah knew clean from unclean. The wicked had the music and the weapons then, the same as they do now, and it ended in the flood that destroyed them.

After Cain slew Abel, “Adam knew his wife again; and she bare a son, and called his name Seth: For God, said she, hath appointed me another seed instead of Abel.” Seth was Abel's replacement, the replacement of righteousness in the earth.

“And to Seth, to him also there was born a son; and he called his name Enos: then began men to call upon the name of the Lord.” Ezra says the nations that came out of Adam “despised thy commandments.” When the sons of God despised God's commandments, God stopped dealing with us. But once Seth had Enos, that line began to call upon the name of the Lord, and God started dealing with us again.

Those tribes back then were called the sons of God. Tribes, sons of God: that sounds like the Israelites. Nothing new under the sun. The tribes of the sons of God were around back then and they are around now; wicked, evil leaders were around back then, and the righteous are around now. The wickedness is always around, and the righteous are always born within the evil.

That line carries straight to the flood. Ezra says God brought the flood on those that dwelt in the world, “Nevertheless one of them thou leftest, namely, Noah with his household, of whom came all righteous men.” That goes back to Shem's line: not Ham's line, not Japheth's line, but Shem's, the line that came down from Seth.

Isaac told Esau, “And by thy sword shalt thou live, and shalt serve thy brother.” That goes right back to Cain being a fugitive and a vagabond: wandering all around, in lands that don't belong to him, acquiring them by the sword, killing and massacring and holding himself unaccountable. Some say they did not steal the Native Americans' land, they conquered it. What is the difference? After you conquered it, did you give it back? You kept it and gave it to your children, and then gave land to the Irish and British who came afterward and conquered nothing. That is stealing.

“and it shall come to pass when thou shalt have the dominion, that thou shalt break his yoke from off thy neck”: once David's lineage went off, Esau broke free of our rule and began to conquer. “And Esau hated Jacob because of the blessing,” and said in his heart, “The days of mourning for my father are at hand; then will I slay my brother Jacob.” What did Cain do to Abel? He slew him. Nothing new under the sun: the same people doing the same exact thing. Rebekah told Jacob, “thy brother Esau, as touching thee, doth comfort himself, purposing to kill thee”: how evil, to find comfort in killing your own brother.

Wisdom tells what became of Cain: “But when the unrighteous went away from her in his anger, he perished also in the fury wherewith he murdered his brother.” The unrighteous is Cain. When he killed Abel it was not a tap on the back of the head; he brutally killed him in his fury. And Cain was killed too, the same violent way he killed Abel.

That is why Rebekah said, “why should I be deprived also of you both in one day?” She knew: if Esau killed Jacob, God would kill Esau. You kill your brother, and you are going to die too.

Rebekah told Jacob to flee to her brother Laban's house because Esau wanted him dead, so he ran to Laban, and “Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.” He took rods of green poplar, hazel and chesnut, “pilled white strakes in them,” and set them before the flocks at the watering troughs. The stronger cattle conceived among the rods, “so the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.” “And the man increased exceedingly.”

So Jacob was Laban's shepherd; he took care of the sheep and the cattle. He was a shepherd just as Abel was a shepherd, and Esau was the man of the field just as Cain was a man of the field. The same two lines keep repeating.

And Jacob tells what that shepherding cost him: “This twenty years have I been with thee;” “That which was torn of beasts I brought not unto thee; I bare the loss of it.” “Thus I was; in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep departed from mine eyes.” “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle: and thou hast changed my wages ten times.”

Laban was a grimy man. He did Jacob dirty: Jacob took care of his cattle day and night, bore the losses himself, and Laban kept lowering his pay. Yet God increased Jacob exceedingly in spite of it.

“Good is set against evil, and life against death: so is the godly against the sinner, and the sinner against the godly.” “So look upon all the works of the most High; and there are two and two, one against another.” There is always a good side and a bad side.

Genesis 5 shows it. “Jared lived an hundred sixty and two years, and he begat Enoch.” Wait a minute: didn't Cain have a son named Enoch too? He did. Seth's Enoch “walked with God: and he was not; for God took him,” taken up the way Elijah was, walking with God just as Noah walked with God. You had a righteous Enoch and a wicked Enoch.

It goes on down the line. Seth's line had Methuselah, who lived “nine hundred sixty and nine years,” the longest of any man, and Lamech, who named his son Noah, “saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which the Lord hath cursed,” the ground cursed when Adam sinned. Cain's line had its own Lamech. Two and two, one against another.

Genesis 5 keeps saying each father “begat sons and daughters,” yet it names specific sons, because those particular children were significant: they birthed prophets. Among the other sons and daughters there was wickedness. That is why Noah is named and found perfect: he had siblings, but he was the righteous one out of all the sons of God of his time dealing with the daughters of men.

Sirach names the righteous line: “Sem and Seth were in great honour among men, and so was Adam above every living thing in creation.” Adam had his righteous child, Seth, born “in his own likeness, after his image,” and Noah had his righteous child, Shem: “Noah begat Shem, Ham, and Japheth.”

And out of Shem's line came us. The line God honoured runs from Adam through Seth to Noah and on through Shem to Israel.

These are Cain's children: “And unto Enoch was born Irad: and Irad begat Mehujael: and Mehujael begat Methusael: and Methusael begat Lamech.” So Cain had a son named Enoch, a descendant named Methusael, and one named Lamech.

Now set that beside Genesis 5, Seth's line: Jared begat Enoch, Enoch begat Methuselah, Methuselah begat Lamech, and Lamech begat Noah. The same names on both sides. It is always two: the left hand side of wickedness and the righteous side. Cain had his Lamech and his Enoch; Seth's line had its Lamech and its Enoch. Righteous Enoch, evil Enoch.

That is Ecclesiasticus 33 lived out in the generations before the flood: “there are two and two, one against another.” And the righteous line, the one named in Genesis 5, is the line of prophets that led to Noah, “a just man and perfect in his generations.”

“But Noah found grace in the eyes of the Lord.” “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God.” Noah was also a son of God, and out of all the sons of God in that time who were doing wickedness with Cain's daughters, Noah did not. There is always that light shining in the darkness all throughout time.

What does perfect mean, and what does it mean to walk with God? God told Abram, “I am the Almighty God; walk before me, and be thou perfect.” Meaning what? Keep his commandments. When it says Noah walked with God, it does not mean he went on long walks and talks on the beach with God. It means he walked in his ways.

Righteous, perfect and just all mean keeping God's commandments. The commandments that Seth kept, Noah was keeping also, while all flesh around him corrupted its way upon the earth.

God said of Abraham, “Because that Abraham obeyed my voice, and kept my charge, my commandments, my statutes, and my laws.” That is what it means to walk before God and be perfect.

Abraham kept the laws, statutes and commandments just as Noah did. “Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with God”: he kept the commandments that Seth kept, and that is why he found grace in the eyes of the Lord when the rest of the earth was corrupt and filled with violence.

So the law was not new at Sinai. Noah kept it, Abraham kept it, and those who keep it are the ones God preserves when “The end of all flesh is come before me.”

“the sons of God saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.” Who are the men here? Eve said of Cain that she had gotten a man from the Lord, so the daughters of men are Cain's children. The sons of God came out of Adam's line through Seth. And the sons of God started messing around with Cain's daughters.

Genesis 5 shows why Seth's line is called the sons of God: “In the day that God created man, in the likeness of God made he him.” God made Adam in his likeness, so Adam was the son of God. “And Adam lived an hundred and thirty years, and begat a son in his own likeness, after his image; and called his name Seth.”

Was Cain made in Adam's image? No. Everyone is not made in God's image. Seth was, and Abel was, but Cain was not. Cain was a man of the Lord, a regular man; God made him, but he was not God's son. He was somebody else's son: of that wicked one.

So when the sons of God, made in God's likeness through Seth, took the daughters of Cain, the line that was in God's image mixed with the line that was not. The children “became mighty men which were of old, men of renown”: powerful, famous, fierce fighters, but wicked as hell, because they intermingled with Cain. Cain had built a city, and the sons of God began dwelling in it and following his ways, just as the sons of God today dwell in Esau's city and learn his ways.

Luke traces Christ's line all the way back: “Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.” There it is written plainly. Adam was the son of God, and that line, Seth's line, were the sons of God of Genesis 6.

Abel was one of them, but Cain killed him. Then Adam and Eve had Seth, who replaced Abel, and the line of the sons of God continued through him.

So “the sons of God saw the daughters of men” is Seth's line looking upon Cain's daughters. What followed is why “it repented the Lord that he had made man on the earth.” The sons of God started to behave like Cain and his daughters, and God said, “I will destroy man whom I have created from the face of the earth”: destroy everything and start over. “The earth also was corrupt before God,” because the sons of God mingled with Cain's children; Cain gained dominion, “and the earth was filled with violence,” just as Cain was violent.

Genesis 7 ends with four words: “and the Lord shut him in.” Noah did not close that door; God did. Revelation 3:7 shows who holds that power: “he that openeth, and no man shutteth; and shutteth, and no man openeth.” That is Christ, the one “that hath the key of David.”

Why did God close the door himself? Because of what Noah would hear outside. Noah was a man, and a man has a soft spot. There were babies out there, people begging for their babies, screaming and crying. Noah's own kin were out there too, his siblings and relatives, crying out, why are you doing this? If the door were left to Noah, he might have opened it. So God said, get back, I'll close the door. Noah had to sit inside and hear the screaming, the crying and the begging until there was nothing to hear anymore. That is a terrible thing to live through.

The door was shut only after a long season of mercy. Noah was a hundred years building that boat, and the people were warned the whole time: repent, stop following Cain, keep these laws. They said, we good. God was longsuffering with them. Noah was found righteous “in this generation” because he kept the commandments; that is how he knew the clean beasts from the unclean and how he walked with God. When the fountains of the great deep broke up and the windows of heaven opened, only the eight souls on that boat lived.

It is the same today. Right now the door of repentance is open, and Christ is longsuffering with our people. This is the time to get it right. Once that door is closed, that is it; no one can open it, the way the great gulf is fixed. As it was in the days of Noah, so it is now.
