Holy, and beloved. Baruch shows who the beloved is: “He hath found out all the way of knowledge, and hath given it unto Jacob his servant, and to Israel his beloved.” Israel is his beloved, and it is to Israel he gave all the way of knowledge.

So the “holy and beloved” of Colossians 3:12 are the children of Israel: holy because he severed them from other people, beloved because he calls Israel his beloved.

That is why the Lord, through the apostle Paul, instructs the Colossians on how to deal with one another: “bowels of mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness, longsuffering; Forbearing one another, and forgiving one another”. Why? Because we are the same people. We are the sons and daughters of the living God, and there is a way we have to govern ourselves and treat each other.

In verse 11 Paul references us as the Greeks, the Barbarians and the Scythians. Then in verse 12 he says it one more time, plainly: “Put on therefore, as the elect of God”. He is speaking in a language we can understand, not for the heathens to understand. Isaiah tells us who the elect of God is: “For Jacob my servant’s sake, and Israel mine elect”.

Israel is his elect. So the elect of God that Paul is instructing in Colossians 3:12 are Israelites.

They know good and well this Bible don’t belong to them. But in slavery they played on our ignorance. We couldn’t read or write; they taught it to us by oral tradition, wouldn’t let us read the Bible, and gave us the slave Bible where the majority of the Bible wasn’t even there. They wanted to keep us docile, ignorant and misinformed. But there is a God, the God of Israel, who has poured his spirit upon his people in these last days, and now we know what the Bible is talking about: Israel mine elect.

Colossians 3:12 calls the elect of God “holy and beloved”. Leviticus tells us how to be holy, and who it is for: “And ye shall be holy unto me: for I the Lord am holy, and have severed you from other people, that ye should be mine.”

Holy means severed, separated from all other nations on the face of the earth. He has severed us from other people, “that ye should be mine”: that ye, you Israelites, should be his people.

So right there in Colossians 3:12 the Lord is saying it ain’t all nations. Just in case anyone was confused by what Paul was saying in verse 11, he clears it up in verse 12. The ones told to put on mercies, kindness, humbleness of mind, meekness and longsuffering are the holy people, the ones severed from the other nations to be his.

Servants ruling over us happened with Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America present day. The Lord explains it to Ezra: “And he said unto me, I will liken my judgment unto a ring”.

A ring is a circular motion. You see this curse? It comes right back around, empire after empire, and it keeps happening because we are the people of God. But this is the last time. All praise to the Most High.

So the slavery in America where Colossians 3:22 was used against us is one more turn of that ring of judgment on Israel. It was not the Lord making the white man our rightful master; it was his judgment coming back around on his own people, and it ends with this last time.

In 1673 Mr. Baxter published his Christian Directory with directions to masters in foreign plantations who have negroes and other slaves, a rubric to follow. In their evil minds they really believed they were masters. Did the Lord allow this to happen? Absolutely. But that is not what Colossians 3:22 is talking about. The first direction: remember that they have immortal souls and are equally capable of salvation with yourselves. That is where the false sense of equality comes from. It comes from slavery; it comes from Christianity.

Who is salvation for? “Him hath God exalted with his right hand to be a Prince and a Saviour, for to give repentance to Israel, and forgiveness of sins.” A savior brings salvation, and that salvation is only for the children of Israel.

They believed they could be saved and then us; they are the people, and we come after. That is not how it goes. The same directions said that they and you are equally under the government and laws of God, and that is incorrect: we are not equal with these people. Christ was exalted to give repentance to Israel, so the servants of Colossians and the salvation preached to them belong to Israel.

The slave masters' directions said that God is their reconciled tender father. God is our reconciled father, but that reconciliation is not for everybody. What does re mean? To do again: repeat, redo. Reconcile means to do it again. So if they wrote that reconciliation was for the slaves, that means they knew who we are.

Reconciliation cannot apply to the other nations, because they were never a people close or near to God. The Israelites are the only ones that have been close or near to God. Daniel shows it: “Seventy weeks are determined upon thy people and upon thy holy city, to finish the transgression, and to make an end of sins, and to make reconciliation for iniquity, and to bring in everlasting righteousness, and to seal up the vision and prophecy, and to anoint the most Holy.”

That is determined upon Daniel's people and holy city, and the most Holy anointed is Christ. Through Christ we get our reconciliation. So the very masters who twisted Colossians 3:22 wrote down, in their own directions, that their slaves were the people God reconciles: Israel.

The third direction to the masters: serve your necessities by your slaves so as to prefer God's interest and their spiritual and everlasting happiness; teach them the way to heaven. So in want of all things we wanted food, clothing, housing, shelter, and we also got that old time religion from them too.

“Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. In want of all things: even our religion had to come from the enemy we were serving.

The next page shows what that religion was for. They wrote that we were redeemed with them by Christ from the slavery of Satan and may live with them in the liberty of the saints in glory. They want us to go to heaven with them and live with them. That's called hell. That mind was beaten into us: a brother on the street asked if the Edomite could be saved, and said if he goes to hell, so will I, because he doesn't want to go anywhere without his master. That is the want of all things the curse brought, and why the master's reading of Colossians 3:22 still holds our people.

“Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh”. Going precept upon precept and in context, these servants would have to be Israelites, and these masters would have to be Israelites. It is a scripture they cherry-picked to fit their evil narrative. In The Religious Instruction of the Negroes in the United States they wrote of us, the 697,697 slaves of the 1790 census, as the original stock, in a state of absolute heathenism. They inserted themselves as the people and made us the heathens.

But the Lord did say this would happen: “Thus saith the Lord God; Because that Moab and Seir do say, Behold, the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen”. Moab and Seir look at the house of Judah and call us heathen.

How did we become like the heathen? By following after the heathen: celebrating their pagan rituals, Christmas, Thanksgiving; eating crab, shrimp, pork, lobster; praying to a white man. That is what makes us heathenistic. So the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israel, and the enemy calling Judah heathen is only what the Lord already said Moab and Seir would say.

Our enemies would like to think God cast us away because we became like the heathen, and that he isn't going to redeem us. Even with us becoming heathens, this is what the Lord says: “Know ye therefore that they which are of faith, the same are the children of Abraham. And the scripture, foreseeing that God would justify the heathen through faith, preached before the gospel unto Abraham, saying, In thee shall all nations be blessed.”

The scripture foreseeing: the Lord already knew we were going to become heathens. He saw that this would happen to us, and he would justify us through faith, through Christ. They may be mad all over again; it doesn't matter. We are still God's chosen people.

So the heathen Galatians speaks of justifying is Israel fallen into heathenism, the same servants Colossians 3:22 speaks to. That justification is only for one people, as Isaiah 45:25 shows.

The masters' book called us the most needy of any people in their country. It does say needy, and the Bible says it too: “The instruments also of the churl are evil: he deviseth wicked devices to destroy the poor with lying words, even when the needy speaketh right.”

The needy in that book is us. The churl devised wicked devices with lying words: cherry-picking “Servants, obey in all things your masters”, writing directions for masters to bring slaves to their religion, forbidding our meetings and our reading.

And even when we speak straight out of the Bible, going precept upon precept, they call it hate speech. That is the needy speaking right and the churl answering with lying words to destroy the poor. So when Colossians 3:22 is read in context, it speaks of Israelite servants and Israelite masters, and the lying words that turned it against us are the churl's devices.

Galatians says God would “justify the heathen through faith”. Who is that justification for? “In the Lord shall all the seed of Israel be justified, and shall glory.” Shall the seed of what be justified? Israel.

So it is what it is. Yes, we became heathen, following after the heathen in their holidays, their foods and their white image; but we are still going to be justified through Christ, and we shall glory. The justification is for one people, the seed of Israel.

That is why the servants of Colossians 3:22 are Israelites and not the slave master's property to be taught his religion. The masters' books called us heathens in need of their instruction, but the Lord had already written that all the seed of Israel, heathen as we became, would be justified in him.

The masters' own book says of us: they are in the eye of the law property. In the eyes of their laws, we were their property. The Lord told us why: “And it shall come to pass, when ye shall say, Wherefore doeth the Lord our God all these things unto us? then shalt thou answer them, Like as ye have forsaken me, and served strange gods in your land, so shall ye serve strangers in a land that is not yours.”

We are serving strangers in a land that is not ours, a land we are not familiar with. That is the servitude the Lord allowed because we forsook him.

So the slavery here was the curse on Israel for serving strange gods, not the obedience Colossians 3:22 teaches between Israelite servants and Israelite masters. They took the scripture and used it to hold us as property, but the Lord had already told us we would serve strangers.

Jeremiah said we would serve strangers in a land that is not ours. The Lamentations goes further: “Servants have ruled over us: there is none that doth deliver us out of their hand.” Servants have ruled over us. This is Bible prophecy.

It happened in the time of Assyria, Babylon, Persia, Greece, Rome, and America in the present day. It keeps happening over and over again. Why? Because we are the people of God. But this is the last time.

So the masters who took Colossians 3:22 and told us “Servants, obey in all things your masters” were themselves the servants ruling over Israel, just as the prophets lamented, with none to deliver us out of their hand.

We were their property, and they still view us as that. They may have said we were equal in salvation, but while we were here they treated us like beasts: chattel slavery, three-fifths of a man. They never looked at us as their equals.

Nehemiah prayed it: “And it yieldeth much increase unto the kings whom thou hast set over us because of our sins”. This is happening because we sinned against our God. “also they have dominion over our bodies, and over our cattle, at their pleasure, and we are in great distress.” Dominion over our bodies, to look at us as their property, at their pleasure.

Their own book says it plainly: they are in the eye of the law property over which there is an absolute control; and by law or custom we were excluded from education, and by consequence from the reading of the word of God. If we were equal, why were we excluded from education? Because they don't want us to know the truth of the Bible, that servants obey your masters isn't talking about them. They want to keep us docile and uneducated.

Their book says we may, according to the power lodged in our hands, forbid religious meetings, and no independent churches were allowed, so we depended on them alone. It went on during the Inquisition too, when they changed Christianity into the all-inclusive Catholic system and went around killing us, the real Jews, tearing up our safe houses and taking our book. The same thing is going to happen again, because now we know the truth. The only way the lie could hold strong was to destroy anybody who did not get down with it.

Revelation shows it: he “deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do in the sight of the beast; saying to them that dwell on the earth, that they should make an image to the beast”. “And he had power to give life unto the image of the beast”: that is the false image of Christ. “that the image of the beast should both speak, and cause that as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed.”

If we did not agree to it, we were killed. Over time our people knew it wasn't true, but they didn't want to be killed, so they went with the lie, generation after generation. But it's a new generation on the earth, and we aren't accepting the lies any more. We know we are the people, and we know what comes with the territory.

Paul elaborates on the masters: “Let as many servants as are under the yoke count their own masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God and his doctrine be not blasphemed.” The servants are under the yoke, the yoke of bondage. If you had a master who still believed in the law of sacrifice, but you believed on Christ, you still honoured him. He follows sacrifice, but you still treat him with respect.

“And they that have believing masters, let them not despise them, because they are brethren”. Now you have Israelite masters who believe on Christ. Don’t despise a master, your brother, that believes on Christ, because they are brethren.

Not one time has the Lord ever said we are brothers with the other nations. So that is showing you those masters are Israelites. When Colossians 4:1 tells masters to give their servants what is just and equal, it is speaking to Israelite masters over Israelite servants, their brethren.

Colossians 3:22, read in context, says “Servants, obey in all things your masters according to the flesh; not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but in singleness of heart, fearing God”. Why? Your master was taking care of your clothes, your raiment, your housing, your food. So why would you disrespect him? Number one, that is your brother. Number two, he is doing this for you: as you do your duties and work, he takes care of you.

Sirach says it: “If a servant say to his master, I will not do as it pleaseth thee; though afterward he do it, he angereth him that nourisheth him.” The master nourishes the servant, and a servant who refuses him angers the one that feeds him.

And you are not just angering the master. You are also angering the Lord that nourisheth us. That is the order Colossians 4:1 completes from the other side: the servant honours the master, and the master gives the servant “that which is just and equal; knowing that ye also have a Master in heaven.”

“Masters, give unto your servants that which is just and equal”. They said that they were the masters. Did they do that? No. They were living in the big house; we were living in the outhouse, and when we got emancipated, did they ever give us the forty acres and the mule? No. So they are showing that they are hypocrites. They are impostors. They’re the damn devil that the Bible speaks of.

Remember, Colossians, Ephesians and Philemon were all written generally at the same time, to the same region. Ephesians says the same thing Colossians does: “Servants, be obedient to them that are your masters according to the flesh, with fear and trembling, in singleness of your heart, as unto Christ; Not with eyeservice, as menpleasers; but as the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart”.

The servants are serving “as unto Christ”, as “the servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart.” This is instruction to one people serving under Christ, not a charter for the slave masters of America, and the verse ends by reminding the masters they “also have a Master in heaven.”

Now this makes more sense: “There is neither Jew nor Greek, there is neither bond nor free, there is neither male nor female: for ye are all one in Christ Jesus.”

Neither Jew nor Greek we already understand from Colossians 3:11: the Greek-speaking Jews and the Jews. Neither bond nor free: the Israelite servant and the Israelite master. Neither male nor female: the manservant and the maidservant, the Israelite man and the Israelite woman.

“for ye are all one”: we are all one nation, under Christ. That is all it is talking about. So the servants and masters of Colossians 4:1 are one people in Christ, and that is why the master must give the servant what is just and equal.

To go a little deeper into who these servants are, Jeremiah says: “That every man should let his manservant, and every man his maidservant, being an Hebrew or an Hebrewess, go free; that none should serve himself of them, to wit, of a Jew his brother.”

Being a what? An Hebrew, or an Hebrewess. So these servants are Israelites. And the one they served was “a Jew his brother.”

That is the servant and master of Colossians 3:22 and 4:1: Israelite servants and Israelite masters, brothers. Christianity took a scripture about brethren and cherry-picked it to fit its evil narrative over us.

More on these servants: “For unto me the children of Israel are servants; they are my servants whom I brought forth out of the land of Egypt: I am the Lord your God.”

The children of Israel are servants, and they are his servants, the ones he brought out of Egypt. That is who the servants of Colossians are, and why the masters must remember they “also have a Master in heaven”: the servants belong to the Lord.

They changed the narrative and flipped the script, inserting themselves into the scriptures where they are not. Where they are, Leviticus shows it right after: “Both thy bondmen, and thy bondmaids, which thou shalt have, shall be of the heathen that are round about you”, and “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. They were originally our possession, but we sinned against our God and became their possession. Don’t worry: it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

When we read precept upon precept, in the context of the scriptures, we see how we have been lied to as a people. Paul asks: “Who art thou that judgest another man’s servant? to his own master he standeth or falleth.”

Who are you to judge another man’s servant? To his own master he stands or falls. So our real master is Christ. That is the “Master in heaven” of Colossians 4:1, the one both servants and masters answer to.

And the servant is not left alone: “Yea, he shall be holden up: for God is able to make him stand.” There it is. For God is able to make him stand.

Tatum claimed he had not seen black Hebrew Israelites going out and saying anything in the community when a black man died. That is a lie; he has been found a liar. That is what we do literally every week. We teach in the hoods and the ghettos where our people are: O Block in Chicago, East St. Louis, Memphis, Miami, Compton, LA, Philly. We go toe to toe and face our people.

“And they taught in Judah, and had the book of the law of the Lord with them, and went about throughout all the cities of Judah, and taught the people.”

They taught in Judah: we go to our people just like the forefathers did. They had the book of the law of the Lord with them: we bring the Bible with us. They went throughout all the cities: we do not just go to one city or one state. Wherever our people are scattered, wherever our people are being afflicted, we are there, teaching the people.

Tatum said black people need to do better: y’all whole life is activism, y’all still complaining and protesting like y’all still slaves. Why were the brothers in Ocean Springs, Mississippi? Because one of our brothers, Nolan Wells, had a mysterious death with a bunch of white people around it, in a town known for lynching black people. Yes, we are activists. Yes, we stand up for righteousness and speak against the evils and atrocities that happen to our people. That puts fear in our oppressors, and he is doing their bidding: hey, you’ve been cooning great lately.

So what is better than standing up for God and standing up for his people? “And herein do I exercise myself, to have always a conscience void of offence toward God, and toward men.”

We always have to do what is right toward God and toward our people. Better looks like getting your household in order, not committing fornication and adultery, taking care of your family. What is better than that? That is what a conscience void of offence looks like, and he is not speaking from the point of a black man.

A 1966 CBS documentary, Black Power, White Backlash, went into Cicero, Illinois, where 15,000 black people worked in the factories every day but not a single black family lived, and every one of them had to leave when the sun went down. A resident said there are many good coloreds, but the ones that are going to march, I don’t like.

They do not like it when we march, because when we march we have our pride, our dignity, our respect and our confidence. They do not like when we stand up as the nation of Israel; it angers them and it makes them afraid. We have been marching; Marcus Garvey was marching back in the day.

“But Pharaoh shall not hearken unto you, that I may lay my hand upon Egypt, and bring forth mine armies, and my people the children of Israel, out of the land of Egypt by great judgments.” Mine armies. We have been marching since Egypt, and we marched around the walls of Jericho.

Israel came out of Egypt as the armies of the Lord, by great judgments on the ones who held them. That is why our marching troubles our oppressors.

Officer Tatum was asked if black men like him were better off during slavery, and he answered, 100 percent. He said that after slavery there was an explosion of success, black Wall Street, men married to the women they had children with, and now look at the inner cities. What he does not understand is that he thinks white people just switched and started loving us after they let us out of slavery.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages: they came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”. When Christ returns, these same people who had us in slavery, and have us in slavery, are going to try to fight against Christ.

“their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly.” These same slave owners rejoice to devour the poor, and they do it secretly. Even though slavery supposedly ended with the emancipation proclamation in 1863, then what? You had the school to prison pipeline. Redlining. Sundown towns. Sharecropping. It is still the same thing.

Look at us now, and why? Because he is setting up all these traps. That is why he is still oppressing us to this day, and that is the “yoke of iron upon thy neck, until he have destroyed thee.” But Tatum cannot see that.

Habakkuk said their rejoicing is “to devour the poor secretly.” Who are the poor? “What shall one then answer the messengers of the nation? That the Lord hath founded Zion, and the poor of his people shall trust in it.”

The poor of his people. We are the poor that they are devouring secretly. The poor are Israel, and it is Zion that the Lord founded for them to trust in.

Tatum blames the murders, the violent crime and the abortions in the inner cities on our people alone. But who legalized abortion? The white people. Who started Planned Parenthood with Margaret Sanger? He just skips past that; according to him they are not the cause. That is the secret devouring of the poor, and it is the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48 still on our neck.

A pastor named Pam declared that the gospel cannot be for one ethnicity only, that it cannot be just for black men or for white men, and that this is a heretical doctrine preached by false, cultic ministries. Either the cultic ministries are right or Jesus is right; somebody is wrong. It’s you, Pam.

“But he answered and said, I am not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel.”

It is only for one nation, twelve tribes. If you are not part of that, you are not getting in. Some of our people are bugged the hell out, and it is a direct correlation to slavery. A white pastor even said God blessed black Americans through white people and slavery, and Tatum agrees with that. But Christ was sent to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, the same people under the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“Therefore thou deliveredst them into the hand of their enemies, who vexed them”. That is what happened to us: we have been delivered into the hands of our enemies, the yoke of iron of Deuteronomy 28:48.

“and in the time of their trouble, when they cried unto thee, thou heardest them from heaven”. That is what is happening now. The Lord is starting to hear our cry. We are supposed to pray unto the Lord until he brings vengeance; that is what the Bible tells us to do.

“and according to thy manifold mercies thou gavest them saviours, who saved them out of the hand of their enemies.” How is that happening? By the purple and gold going to this city and that city, this country and that country, teaching the word of God. These are the saviours, and the saviours showed up in Ocean Springs, Mississippi.

So when we see these things happen to our people, yes, we are going to be there, and no, we are not going to stop. We don’t care if we have coons among our own people; we are going to rise up and save the day, because that is how God ordained it. Tatum is mad about it. Get mad. You hate your people and you hate your God.

They do not like when we stand up on our feet with confidence as the nation of Israel, not as blacks, but as the nation of Israel.

“And after three days and an half the Spirit of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet; and great fear fell upon them which saw them.”

Great fear falls on them when they see us rise up as the children of God, as the army of the living God. That is what the man in Cicero feared when he said he could not stand the ones who march, and it is what puts fear in our oppressors when the brothers show up in a town like Ocean Springs. The yoke of iron destroyed us, but the Spirit of life from God stands us back on our feet.

The holy city “had a wall great and high, and had twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names written thereon, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”.

Praises to the Most High for that. The kingdom is only for God’s people. The gates of the city carry the names of the twelve tribes, and no other nation’s name is written there.

That settles what Pam called heresy. Christ was not sent but unto the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and the city he brings has twelve gates for the twelve tribes. The same people the Lord sent into bondage with a yoke of iron upon their neck are the people whose names are on the gates.

Leviticus 25:46 says “they shall be your bondmen for ever”. For how long? Forever. Esau thinks he can change his judgment. No. No. You cannot change it. God said it, it is in writing, it is stamped. So that means you are going back into slavery.

“I know that, whatsoever God doeth, it shall be for ever: nothing can be put to it, nor any thing taken from it: and God doeth it, that men should fear before him.” Whatever God does is forever. Nothing can be put to it to change it, nor anything taken from it. There it is: that men should fear before him.

Isaiah shows it coming to pass: “the house of Israel shall possess them in the land of the Lord for servants and handmaids: and they shall take them captives, whose captives they were; and they shall rule over their oppressors.” For servants and handmaids, because that is the role the Lord gave them, and for how long? Forever. The judgment of Leviticus 25:44-46 cannot be undone.

Leviticus 25:46 says of the heathen bondmen, “ye shall take them as an inheritance for your children after you”. Hold that, and hear Psalm 2: “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.”

The Lord is saying, don’t worry, it is going back to that. He is going to give us the heathen for our inheritance. Meaning what? We are going to own them. That is what it is saying right there. We were their possession, but they were originally our possession; we sinned against our God and became theirs, and it is going to go back to the way it is supposed to be.

“Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” If they don’t want to get right, boom, upside the head. “Be wise now therefore, O ye kings: be instructed, ye judges of the earth.”

So the inheritance of Leviticus 25:46 and the inheritance of Psalm 2:8 are the same: the heathen given to Israel for an inheritance and a possession, ruled with a rod of iron.

Paul beseeches the brethren “by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That “him” is Christ, and Genesis 49:10 shows why: “unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” He is the only one who can gather all twelve tribes together. When people on earth say they are the ones Christ is using to gather the twelve tribes, don't listen to that.

Jacob's blessing lays it out. “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the sceptre is the kingship. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: between the feet means the loins, the seed. The lawgiver comes out of Judah's loins, which shows there is no immaculate conception. “until Shiloh come”: until Christ comes.

That is why Paul tells them “be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled.” In his time many were running around saying the resurrection had come and gone already. Paul reminds them not to let anyone deceive them; Christ had not returned, and the gathering belongs to him alone, when he comes.

Paul says “that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.” The falling away is not people leaving Christianity to join Islam, the way Christians read it. The falling away means the twelve tribes of Israel have to fall and go into captivity, and Luke 21:24 shows it.

“And they shall fall by the edge of the sword”: the Israelites. “and shall be led away captive into all nations”: slavery. “and Jerusalem shall be trodden down of the Gentiles”: Jerusalem taken over by other nations, in particular the Edomite nations, “until the times of the Gentiles be fulfilled”, until that time of rulership is over.

So two things have to happen before Christ returns: all twelve tribes must go into captivity, which is where we are now, and the man of sin must be revealed, the son of perdition. Perdition means eternal damnation, spiritual ruin and hell; it comes from the Latin perdere, to destroy or to lose. It is the fate of the wicked, the absolute loss of one's soul, the final loss of salvation and unending punishment.

The Lord shall consume that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth”, and 2 Esdras 13 shows the Son doing it: “this my Son shall rebuke the wicked inventions of those nations, which for their wicked life are fallen into the tempest.”

Those wicked inventions are the ICBM missiles and all that technology, their satellites spread across the globe. Christ will rebuke all of it and “shall lay before them their evil thoughts, and the torments wherewith they shall begin to be tormented, which are like unto a flame.”

Then: “he shall destroy them without labour by the law.” He will not need their weapons; the law does the destroying. God is saying his law is fire, the same fire that is in the mouth of those who teach it. That is the spirit of his mouth and “the brightness of his coming” that destroys the Wicked in 2 Thessalonians 2.

Paul says the Wicked's “coming is after the working of Satan.” Our comings are supposed to be after Christ the Lord, but the white man's comings and goings are after Satan, and that goes back to Genesis 4.

The Lord speaks to Cain: “If thou doest well, shalt thou not be accepted? and if thou doest not well, sin lieth at the door.” Then the speech switches. “And unto thee shall be his desire”: now he is talking to Satan. Cain's desire shall be unto Satan, “and thou shalt rule over him”: Satan shall rule over Cain.

So from the beginning Cain was put under Satan's rule, and his line has walked after Satan ever since. That is why the coming of the man of sin is “after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders”: he is following the one who was set to rule over his father.

“Is not my word like as a fire? saith the Lord; and like a hammer that breaketh the rock in pieces?” This is the same power Paul describes when the Lord consumes that Wicked “with the spirit of his mouth.” God's word is the fire and the hammer.

We have to believe that. Sometimes we only believe what we can see. The Lord said the angels are all around us; we just don't see them. In the same way, we don't see the word working in the spirit, but it is working. When it is spoken it breaks the rock in pieces, whether the hearer receives it or not.

That is why we must use God's word and not our own eloquence. Those who reject it are condemned by it, and when Christ comes, that same word destroys the Wicked by the brightness of his coming.

Paul says the Wicked shall be revealed, “whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth.” The spirit of God's mouth is the holy Bible, and Jeremiah 5:14 shows how it consumes: “behold, I will make my words in thy mouth fire, and this people wood, and it shall devour them.”

Some of us speak very well and have eloquent words, and that is fine, but we must use God's word; that is where the power is. We read the Bible but don't see the spiritual effect it has in this realm, because our eyes are closed. God is saying, my word is fire. Speak it whether they hear or forbear. Even those who reject it are at home tossing and tumbling in their beds, because the way it is broken down haunts them.

As we teach the word of God, we are judging, and many are being marked for death. Everyone who hears it and rejects it and refuses it: remember that Christ said it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah than for those who do not hear his messengers. The words are the fire, the people who reject them are the wood, and that is how the Lord consumes the wicked with the spirit of his mouth.

Christ said this to the Pharisees, who were so in love with Rome: “Ye are of your father the devil, and the lusts of your father ye will do.” The lusts are the desires; they will do whatever their father desires.

“He was a murderer from the beginning”: that is Cain, not the spiritual demon. Cain murdered Abel. “When he speaketh a lie, he speaketh of his own: for he is a liar, and the father of it.” Cain is a liar and the father of lies. Why? Because Satan is his father; Satan is his daddy.

This ties to Genesis 4:7, where Satan was set to rule over Cain, and to 2 Thessalonians 2:9, the Wicked “whose coming is after the working of Satan.” The line of Cain comes and goes after Satan, murdering and lying, just as their father did.

The Wicked comes “with all power and signs and lying wonders”, and Christ warned of the same: “there shall arise false Christs, and false prophets, and shall shew great signs and wonders; insomuch that, if it were possible, they shall deceive the very elect.”

The great signs and wonders go with their science and their technology. Something major is going to happen. No one knows when, but before this kingdom goes down there is going to be a worldwide event to deceive the world, and some of us, God forbid, will be deceived by it.

That is why we must hold to God's word. The lying wonders come after the working of Satan, and only the word, the fire in our mouths, will keep us from being taken in when they come.

“Set thou a wicked man over him: and let Satan stand at his right hand.” That is Genesis 4:7, where Satan was set to rule over Cain, and it is 2 Thessalonians 2, the Wicked “whose coming is after the working of Satan.”

The wicked man has Satan standing at his right hand, and he follows everything Satan says. That is why his coming is with “all power and signs and lying wonders”: it is Satan's working carried out through the man he rules.

So the scriptures line up from the beginning to the end: Cain under Satan's rule, the Pharisees doing the lusts of their father the devil, and the man of sin coming after the working of Satan, until the Lord consumes him with the spirit of his mouth.

Revelation 13 describes the same working Paul does: “he doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men.” That fire coming down from heaven is thermonuclear fire.

“And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles which he had power to do.” See what it calls them: miracles. Those are the signs and wonders. It says the same thing Matthew 24 says and 2 Thessalonians 2 says, “signs and lying wonders”, only with a different word.

So the Wicked's coming after the working of Satan shows up as their science and their weapons, fire from heaven that looks like miracles, used to deceive the world. The Lord will consume him with the spirit of his mouth and destroy him with the brightness of his coming.

“Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother”. Use this verse to your advantage; don't run from it. In Romans 9:13 Paul speaks on behalf of God, and that is what God says about Esau. But God's law to us is: thou shalt not abhor an Edomite, for he is thy brother, a wicked brother.

And look at our condition: “Therefore shalt thou serve thine enemies which the Lord shall send against thee, in hunger, and in thirst, and in nakedness, and in want of all things”. If you know you have to serve this man for food, water and clothing, you can't go around saying I hate your guts, I just want to harm you. You think you're going to have a job? You're going to lose everything.

There was a brother at camp on Eastern Parkway, on medication, who said he couldn't work because he gets violent: I hate white people; when I sit in the office or do construction, I look at them and I just want to harm them. And there was a martial artist, a black belt, who drew young Haitian brothers to him, skinny at first and diesel two or three months later, calling themselves the barbershop crew in Brooklyn. One night a brother called to be gotten out of jail: they were getting diesel and learning to fight to do home invasions and burglaries.

The bottom line is, professing yourself to be an Israelite is not on the premise of wanting to harm white people. A lot of Israelite camps teach that, and the leaders of those camps are bums: either they are bums or they live off the congregation, and they can talk that way without repercussions because they have no boss to answer to. We serve our enemies under the curse, so we keep the law: we do not abhor the Edomite.

In an interview with Soft White Underbelly came the question: when you're teaching this, doesn't it cause people to be angry? Yes, they get angry. The Bible says anger is okay: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath”.

The sin would be if you start murdering people; the sin would be if you start stealing. Remember the series American Gods: Anansi was on a slave ship and asked, are you angry? That's good; anger gets stuff done. Surely oppression makes a wise man mad. Not I'm going to go kill everybody, but let's organize, let's do better. And you know who got that actor fired? Black people, who said what he was saying would make white people mad. The whole show was cancelled, and all those black people lost their jobs.

So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” does not mean you can't be angry at what was done. Be angry and sin not: let the anger drive you to organize and build, not to harm, steal or kill.

“But I say unto you, That whosoever is angry with his brother without a cause shall be in danger of the judgment”. The key is without a cause. If I'm mad with you and I have no reason to be mad with you, I'm in danger of judgment.

But now somebody does something to your daughter, your wife, your loved one: do you have a reason? Yes. At one of the schools a sister's phone kept going ding, somebody sending her indecent pictures on Instagram. It went on for a while until the heads of the school had everybody bring their phones up and closed the doors. One brother said his phone was dead; they said don't worry, we got a charger. Sure enough, it was him. They told everybody to move back, and the husband said, move out my way. That is anger with a cause.

As the saying goes, in order to be a man of peace you must be capable of great violence; if you're not capable of violence, you're just harmless. So “Thou shalt not abhor an Edomite; for he is thy brother” forbids hatred without a cause, not the defense of your own.

“If it be possible, as much as lieth in you, live peaceably with all men.” That's if possible. As much as lies in you, you live peaceably, and that includes the Edomite the law says you shall not abhor, for he is thy brother.

But we've seen some instances on the news where it was impossible; you had to throw hands with some people, because some people are irate and some people are unreasonable. Paul did not say peace at any cost; he said as much as lieth in you.

So the law of Deuteronomy 23:7 is not a command to be harmless. It is a command not to carry hatred and seek harm. We live peaceably as far as it depends on us, and we are not the ones who start it.

In 2 Esdras 1:5 God commands the prophet: “Go thy way, and shew my people their sinful deeds”. Go and show the people. Ezekiel was given the same charge: “get thee to them of the captivity, unto the children of thy people, and speak unto them, and tell them, Thus saith the Lord God; whether they will hear, or whether they will forbear.” Whether they hear or forbear, our job is to go and tell them.

Then God tells him why: “Son of man, I have made thee a watchman unto the house of Israel: therefore hear the word at my mouth, and give them warning from me. When I say unto the wicked, Thou shalt surely die; and thou givest him not warning, nor speakest to warn the wicked from his wicked way, to save his life; the same wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood will I require at thine hand.”

So as a prophet and teacher, it is required that we tell you what you are doing wrong, because if we don’t, we are liable to have that blood on our hands. It is not that we even have a choice. You call yourself a prophet, a teacher: your job is to go correct the people and help the brother.

That is why showing the people their sinful deeds is not hatred. Sometimes you have to show someone their shame, and that is God loving them too, because he could leave them right there to die and find out after death. It is our job to warn our people, to hopefully bring them to repentance, and when they come, to help them reform their ways. But they have to be willing to listen, and they cannot want correction for others while refusing it for themselves.

If you see a brother that is in error and you don’t correct him, what does the scripture say you are? “Thou shalt not hate thy brother in thine heart: thou shalt in any wise rebuke thy neighbour, and not suffer sin upon him.”

If you see a brother in error and do not rebuke him, you hate your brother in your heart. Leaving sin upon him is not love; rebuking him in any wise is. So we have no choice but to tell our people what they are doing wrong, or we hate our brother in our heart.

That is the love behind 2 Esdras 1:5, “shew my people their sinful deeds, and their children their wickedness which they have done against me”. Showing the people their sins is how you keep from hating them. And it goes both ways: when a brother comes to you and says this is wrong, hear it and learn, because you do not want to be on the outside of what is about to happen.

After his image and after his likeness means his spirit, the commandments of God. A lot of the time people think the image and likeness only means looking like God. Ephesians 4:24 shows what his image is: “put on the new man, which after God is created in righteousness and true holiness.”

That is after the image of God: created in righteousness. The man God made in his image was made to be righteous and holy, not only to share his color.

So being after his image is more than the hue of your skin. Black and wicked is not the way to go; you are still the devil. We say the white man is a devil, but there are black devils too. Just because you are black does not make you special unless you are righteous. It is the laws of God that make us special.

“Let us make man in our image, after our likeness” is not talking about all people. The man is Adam, and verse 28 shows it: God blessed them and told them to “Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth, and subdue it: and have dominion.” That is Adam and the line coming from him, which would eventually be the twelve tribes of Israel.

Genesis 2:7 is read together with it: “the Lord God formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul.” Formed from the dust of the ground: we know God is black, Christ is black and the apostles were black. The real Jews are black, and the Caucasian race, Esau as the Bible calls them, is cursed.

Solomon says the same in Wisdom of Solomon 7, that he is “the offspring of him that was first made of the earth”, and that God gave him to know “the operation of the elements.” The elements in the soil are the elements in man: oxygen, iron, calcium, sodium, potassium, magnesium, in different percentages. When God made us from the dust, he took from those elements and worked them to form man, the way he formed land and sea. That is what we call the periodic table today, and it is what Esau tries to do with his so-called science: play Frankenstein and try to become God.

But the image goes deeper than the dust and the skin. The breath God breathed in is wisdom, “the breath of the power of God, and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty.” He gave it to us so that we would know better. Being made after his image and likeness is his spirit, the commandments of God.

Genesis says “after our likeness”, and Psalms 17:15 shows what that likeness is: “As for me, I will behold thy face in righteousness: I shall be satisfied, when I awake, with thy likeness.”

His likeness is righteousness. David beholds God's face in righteousness and is satisfied to wake in his likeness. So man made after God's image and likeness was meant to be righteous.

Read with Ephesians 4:24, the new man “created in righteousness and true holiness”, it is plain: black is black, but being made in his image means being black and righteous, because black and wicked ain't the way to go: you're still the devil. We say the white man's a devil, but there's black devils too. Just because you are black don't make you special unless you are righteous; it is the laws of God that make us special. The dust of the ground made the body; keeping the commandments is what makes us his likeness.

“Of his own will begat he us with the word of truth, that we should be a kind of firstfruits of his creatures.” We were formed in his image, in his likeness, to be righteous. The literal firstfruits given to God had to be perfect; an animal could not be spotted. And James says pure religion is “to keep himself unspotted from the world.” But we all fall short.

So who is James writing to? “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad”. Moses said it: “I said, I would scatter them into corners, I would make the remembrance of them to cease from among men”. The Most High scattered us and made our remembrance cease. That goes with Deuteronomy 28:64, where we are scattered and serve gods of wood and stone. When we were serving gods of wood and stone, we were spotted.

So James is writing to the twelve tribes scattered abroad, ones that were living as sinners. Count it joy when God starts showing you who you are. To live an unspotted life, we have to learn what we were doing wrong so we can fix it. So why are you mad? That is the whole purpose. God sends teachers to show us how to get right; we get cleansed because we are swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath.

And once we are unspotted, we go out and help others the same way: to visit “the fatherless and widows in their affliction”, the ones with no guide, no hedge, nobody to lead them, so they can become unspotted too. The scattered, forgotten tribes are the firstfruits God begat with the word of truth, and the good and perfect gift from above is the wisdom that makes us clean again.

“Then beware lest thou forget the Lord, which brought thee forth out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.”

That's why you do it: why you teach the laws diligently to the children, talk of them in the house and by the way, and sing the psalms and spiritual songs over and over. The repetition keeps the house from forgetting the Lord who brought us out of the house of bondage.

Now if you forget the Lord, guess what? You're going to be tempted. Forgetting the Lord leaves the armour off, and the wiles of the devil find a way in. Remembering him is how the family puts on the whole armour of God and stands.

“Ye shall not tempt the Lord your God, as ye tempted him in Massah. Ye shall diligently keep the commandments of the Lord your God, and his testimonies, and his statutes, which he hath commanded thee.”

Well, how don't you tempt him? Teach them diligently. Husband in order, wife in order, redeeming the time. Diligently keeping the commandments, testimonies and statutes: that's how you do it, by instructing them.

So all these scriptures go together. Do half of them and you have only pieces of the armour. Do them all, in the house, with the children, and the family has put on the whole armour of God, “that ye may be able to stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children”. Teach them what? The laws of God. “and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.”

It is a routine of the word. It's repetition: sitting in the house, walking by the way, lying down, rising up. Children are not mature enough to make that cognitive decision on their own; the parent has to put the law in them diligently, over and over.

That is how the children put on the whole armour of God. The husband in order, the wife in order, the time redeemed, and the laws taught diligently at every part of the day, so the house can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.”

This is another piece of the whole armour. If you are not redeeming the time because the days are evil, you are not going to teach your children to learn how to fear God. Walking circumspectly, not as fools but as wise, is how a parent sets the example the children follow.

The days are evil: the social media zaps our young out, and Esau sets it up so they can be taken for sweat equity. Redeeming the time means using it for the Lord and for teaching the house, so the family can put on the whole armour of God and “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“Speaking to yourselves in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord”.

Over and over you sing these songs, you read these words. It's repetition, the same routine of the word Moses commanded when he said to teach the laws diligently in the house, by the way, lying down and rising up. It is there to mold the children's minds concerning the laws of God.

The world molds them with its music and its social media; the psalms, hymns and spiritual songs mold them with the law. That repetition in the house is part of putting on the whole armour of God, so they can “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“Wives, submit yourselves unto your own husbands, as unto the Lord. For the husband is the head of the wife, even as Christ is the head of the church: and he is the saviour of the body.”

The whole armour of God is not put on in pieces. If we want to strengthen our families: one, the husband in order; the wife in order; and the children will learn how to obey the Lord by your behavior. The husband is the head as Christ is the head, and the wife submits as unto the Lord.

If the husband and wife are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order. So the order of the house, the husband as head and the wife submitting, is part of the armour that lets the family “stand against the wiles of the devil.”

“Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right. Honour thy father and mother; (which is the first commandment with promise;) That it may be well with thee, and thou mayest live long on the earth.” “And, ye fathers, provoke not your children to wrath: but bring them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord.”

These scriptures are put together with “Put on the whole armour of God” for a reason. If you do half of these things, you are not putting on the whole armour of God; you are putting on pieces. It begins at home. Husbands in order, wives in order; if they are not in order, you can't expect the children to be in order.

Children learn how to obey the Lord by the behavior of their parents, and in turn they are putting on the whole armour of God. The father brings them up in the nurture and admonition of the Lord, and that is how a family stands against the wiles of the devil.

Now there is context, and no one can say we are making it up. We don't need a cosigner; the Bible says what it says.

With that key, Ezekiel 35 opens up. “Because thou hast had a perpetual hatred”: a hatred that has gone on for centuries, from Esau their father to his children toward us. It is in their blood to hate us; their hatred is damn near biological, from the womb to the tomb. That is why they do such terrible things to us: eating us, hanging us, castrating us, raping us, mutilating us. A sister whose husband was murdered sought justice in court; they hung her from a tree, shot her full of holes, cut the unborn baby out of her, stepped on its head and set it on fire. Damn! That is a perfect hatred. There's no record of black folks ever doing that to white folks. What we did to the French in Haiti was retaliation, and they deserved it; she was innocent.

They took one as Romans and later as Israelis, and the other as Christians, as conquistadors. “I have heard all thy blasphemies”: this is a direct precept to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9, the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not, possessing the land and professing to be the people that belong there. They have said it to our faces: yes, you are the real Jews, but the land is ours now. They know; the world does not.

“When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate.” As long as that nation is on the earth, there can be no peace; when there is no more Edom, the earth rejoices. “thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it.” The judgment on Edom is complete, with no exceptions, and they shall know that he is the Lord.

“Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith the Lord.” Jeremiah 23 really talks about the essence of hirelings. How do they scatter the sheep? In Christianity they scatter them into the Baptist church, the Catholic church, the holiness church, whatever denomination. We are being divided rather than united as the twelve tribes of Israel. Even in the time of Christ there were the Sadducees, the Pharisees, the Stoics, the Epicureans and the Herodians; we were being scattered then, and it's happening today.

Moses said where it would lead: “And the Lord shall scatter thee among all people, from the one end of the earth even unto the other; and there thou shalt serve other gods, which neither thou nor thy fathers have known, even wood and stone.” Under these wood gods, like Christianity with the old wooden cross, and the many denominations under Islam, our people are scattered everywhere in those false religions, even in Judaism.

Remember, this is about Israelites; it is not so much talking about Esau. “Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away”: driven them away from the truth that they are the Israelites of the twelve tribes. But the Lord says “I will gather the remnant of my flock out of all countries whither I have driven them”.

Against the hirelings who scatter the flock, the Lord promises “I will set up shepherds over them which shall feed them: and they shall fear no more, nor be dismayed, neither shall they be lacking”. Jeremiah shows what they will feed us with: “And I will give you pastors according to mine heart, which shall feed you with knowledge and understanding.”

Knowledge and understanding of what? God's laws. It isn't talking about feeding them with jumping up and down, screaming and foaming at the mouth.

Right now we are lacking as a race, as a people. We are lacking knowledge, wisdom and understanding; and when you break it down, we are lacking rulership, dominion of the earth, our own country, a fortified family, a nation. We are lacking everything. Pastors after God's heart, feeding us the laws, are the shepherds who end that lack.

“For the entrances of the elder world were wide and sure, and brought immortal fruit.” The elder world was during the time of Adam. Ezra says “the righteous should inherit these things, but that the ungodly should perish. Nevertheless the righteous shall suffer strait things, and hope for wide”. Strait things is tribulation.

So all Israel is going to go through tribulation, the righteous and the unrighteous. “they that have done wickedly have suffered the strait things, and yet shall not see the wide.” The false prophets say “No evil shall come upon you”, but “a whirlwind of the Lord is gone forth in fury”, and it will not return until he has performed the thoughts of his heart.

What we see on the news, death after death, is just the beginning. A young black girl tied to a tree with a ratchet strap, the kind trucks use to hold down wood, and they call it suicide. Tonya Miller, 27, and Juliana Enza, 16, found hanging from trees, ruled suicides; look at all these names. They can insult our intelligence with this because we are not unified and not connected to the Lord; there is no consequence. They don't do it to the Chinese or Japanese. And it is not only the men: all you independent women, get ready. I don't see color; well, color sees you. It's going to escalate. They won't ask what God you serve: you're in the image of God, and they will come for all the melanated brothers and sisters. The righteous suffer the strait things and hope for the wide.

“They say still unto them that despise me, The Lord hath said, Ye shall have peace”. They are speaking to people who really hate God. At the sit down, the man with the hat kept saying that when tribulation comes, we're not going to be here; the church won't be here. Christians just lie and tell you there's going to be peace.

But Paul and Barnabas were “Confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith, and that we must through much tribulation enter into the kingdom of God.” The only way we're entering the kingdom of God is through much tribulation. So what Bible are these Christians reading?

That is why Jeremiah says “Hearken not unto the words of the prophets that prophesy unto you: they make you vain: they speak a vision of their own heart, and not out of the mouth of the Lord.” A vision of their own heart is their own mind, what they feel at that moment: I don't know who this is for, but God has a message for you. It is not coming from the Bible, and the Bible says tribulation.

“And the Lord shall scatter you among the nations, and ye shall be left few in number among the heathen, whither the Lord shall lead you. And there ye shall serve gods, the work of men’s hands, wood and stone, which neither see, nor hear, nor eat, nor smell.”

In all the lands we were scattered, “if from thence thou shalt seek the Lord thy God, thou shalt find him, if thou seek him with all thy heart and with all thy soul”, meaning do everything God says to do. “When thou art in tribulation, and all these things are come upon thee, even in the latter days, if thou turn to the Lord thy God, and shalt be obedient unto his voice; (For the Lord thy God is a merciful God;) he will not forsake thee”.

When thou art in tribulation, even in the latter days: so these Christians don't know what they are talking about when they say the church won't be here. Israel is in tribulation in the latter days, and Jeremiah said “in the latter days ye shall consider it perfectly.” Our people will not repent unless they get a foot up their behind; death makes people reconsider their ways. We say we are Christians, we serve the same God, and the white man doesn't give a damn about that. But the Lord is merciful: seek him with all the heart and he will not forsake us nor forget the covenant of our fathers.

“I have not sent these prophets, yet they ran: I have not spoken to them, yet they prophesied.” He did not send these pastors, these Christian reverends. Yet they ran: I am going to build a church here. I have not spoken to them: when they say God spoke to me, it is a lie. And “I have heard what the prophets said, that prophesy lies in my name, saying, I have dreamed, I have dreamed.”

How did the Lord speak to his prophets? “Hear now my words: If there be a prophet among you, I the Lord will make myself known unto him in a vision, and will speak unto him in a dream.” “My servant Moses is not so, who is faithful in all mine house.” “With him will I speak mouth to mouth, even apparently, and not in dark speeches; and the similitude of the Lord shall he behold”.

The only one the Lord spoke with mouth to mouth was Moses. So when you hear black women go, God told me: God told you nothing. Stop lying. The Lord spoke to me this morning, his voice was so clear: that is a lie. But people believe this crap.

Miriam said God spoke to her too, and she was a prophet, and the Lord answered, “wherefore then were ye not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?” If even a true prophet was rebuked for putting herself beside Moses, what about these pastors who say God spoke to them? They should have stood in his counsel and caused the people to hear his words; that is the only way to turn the people from their evil way, and you can only transform them with the Bible, the commandments of God.

“And ye my flock, the flock of my pasture, are men, and I am your God, saith the Lord God.” The Lord uses men to lead. It has always been that way and it is never going to change. You will not change the order of things just because you are weak, or scared of your wife.

Sisters, the beta men on social media are influencing you, making you think the man is supposed to worship the ground you walk on. That will not influence the men in purple and gold. We are not worried about being called names, narcissist or misogynist. The question is, do you want a man or do you want a boy?

When your husband gets around the brothers and comes home acting different, he is supposed to. He examines himself, sees he is lacking, and comes home on fire to fix his house, with a little more pep in his step and a little more to say. The same goes when he has been rebuked for adultery or for not dealing with his wife the right way: he is supposed to move different. It works in every area if he truly believes.

This is why there is an attack on the household. Satan and his people know that to destroy us they have to attack our foundation, and the foundation is the home. Paul warned that in the last days perilous times would come, with those “Having a form of godliness, but denying the power thereof”, and “of this sort are they which creep into houses, and lead captive silly women laden with sins, led away with divers lusts.” They get in through the phone and the conversations, whoever is influencing them. We are building a nation, and if we are not strong on the home front, we will not get off the ground.

“I will make him an help meet for him.” To help is to give assistance or support to someone, to provide something useful or necessary in achieving an end. Meet means suitable for him. So the help is the one who assists in making what the husband wants happen. Sometimes the help thinks she is supposed to lead, or thinks she is supposed to guide, but that is not what a help is.

Genesis 3:16 comes after the transgression: “thy desire shall be to thy husband, and he shall rule over thee.” Some have taken this to mean it was only at this point that the woman was supposed to listen to her husband. No. She was told she was the help back in Genesis 2; Genesis 3:16 confirms the rule after the fall.

So why do we feel today that being a help is a bad thing? Sisters, the help is the greatest thing you are ever going to be. The moment you decide being the help is not the greatest thing you can be, or think you are supposed to be something outside of the help, you are going to destroy your marriage.

It cuts both ways. Brothers, the moment you decide not to provide, not to leave the house and work, not to be the man God told you to be, watch what happens to your household: your marriage will crumble and your life will be in shambles. It is a domino effect. And headship is maintenance, a routine thing a husband has to keep doing. A wife will never say she is trying to overthrow you, but it is in her spirit, the same way a man wants to do things his own way when he gets orders from those ranked above him. So you will have to remind her: I am the head, you have to listen to me.

Write this down: women were never designed to lead men. God made the woman “an help meet” for the man, and when that order is turned around, Isaiah 3:12 calls it what it is: “As for my people, children are their oppressors, and women rule over them. O my people, they which lead thee cause thee to err, and destroy the way of thy paths.”

That is a curse. It is not a good thing; it shows things out of order, not how God set it up. A woman's body alone shows she was not made to lead men into danger: her cycle comes, she is pregnant for nine months, and she is supposed to lead you somewhere?

Women ruling over you is a curse, brothers. Some of you are scared to lead your house and have let her lead. If you are passive, scared, afraid of confrontation, she is going to walk all over you. It is not a secret; everyone sees it, and other men see it in your demeanor. You have to change the way you think. Stand up and take your place back.

The women were designed to be a help to their husbands. When they step outside of that, and when the brothers allow it, chaos follows. That is why there is dysfunction in our nation right now: because the men do not want to lead.

“How long wilt thou go about, O thou backsliding daughter? for the Lord hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man.” A new thing: women being over men was never heard of. It is not natural, and it is not the natural state of a man to be run by a woman. But you allow it.

God did not set it up that way. In Genesis 2 he made the woman a help meet for the man. When she compasses him instead, the order is upside down.

Cases come up where a brother does not know what is going on in his own house. His wife pays all the bills while he is on the couch playing video games, and he cannot understand why his home is in confusion. It is because his wife is running things. She has been the breadwinner from day one, so she looks at it as normal, and he is used to it. He did not want a wife; he wanted a mama.

Agag was not supposed to be kept alive in the first place. King Saul trusted the enemy; Samuel did not. “Then said Samuel, Bring ye hither to me Agag the king of the Amalekites. And Agag came unto him delicately.” He came crouching and speaking softly: “Surely the bitterness of death is past.” And Samuel still carried out the word of the Lord: “Samuel hewed Agag in pieces before the Lord in Gilgal.”

This is the wisdom Samuel applied, and the wisdom we have to learn to apply: “Never trust thine enemy: for like as iron rusteth, so is his wickedness.”

“Though he humble himself, and go crouching”: is that not exactly what Agag did, coming delicately? “Yet take good heed and beware of him, and thou shalt be unto him as if thou hadst wiped a lookingglass, and thou shalt know that his rust hath not been altogether wiped away.”

The things that were written aforetime were written for our learning. Esau does not forget, but we do, because we are not tapped into the scriptures. When we apply what the scriptures show us, we learn that our enemies have been the same from day one, and they are not going to change. That is the perpetual hatred we never learned.

Esther 2:5 gives Mordecai’s line: “a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai, the son of Jair, the son of Shimei, the son of Kish, a Benjamite.” Mordecai, and Esther with him, were of the tribe of Benjamin. Go back to 1 Samuel 9 and see who Kish is.

“Now there was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish, the son of Abiel, the son of Zeror, the son of Bechorath, the son of Aphiah, a Benjamite, a mighty man of power.” Kish was a mighty man of power.

“And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly: and there was not among the children of Israel a goodlier person than he: from his shoulders and upward he was higher than any of the people.”

So Saul and Mordecai come out of the same line, the line of Kish. This was not a regular line; this was a mighty Benjamite line. Keep that in mind for what follows, because the enemy Saul was sent against in his day, the Amalekites and their king Agag, shows up again in Mordecai’s day. The hatred is perpetual, and it runs down the same lines.
